President Donald Trump made myriad false and misleading claims during his address to the United Nations General Assembly on Tuesday, many of which he has repeated frequently throughout his second term in the White House.

They covered topics such as U.S. munitions supply, drug seizures, oil and the economy.

Here's a closer look at the facts.

___

CLAIM: “We have more munitions than we could ever possibly even think of using, and we’re building them at levels that we have never done before.”

THE FACTS: Published reports and experts contradict this claim. Weapons stockpiles are diminishing, according to officials from the U.S. military, NATO and the Middle East, and it will take years for U.S. military contractors to replenish Tomahawk cruise missiles as well as Patriot and THAAD missile interceptors, according to defense experts.

In August, officials told The Associated Press that the U.S. military is experiencing a “beyond critical” shortage of advanced missile interceptors in Europe largely driven by President Donald Trump’s war with Iran, raising concerns about vulnerabilities in NATO countries to a potential Russian attack.

One U.S. defense official said the most concerning shortfall involves Patriot missile interceptors, which can shoot down Russia’s high-speed ballistic missiles. A NATO official confirmed low inventories of Patriot missiles among American and NATO forces in Europe. Both spoke on condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive military matters.

“The United States has enough munitions for any plausible scenario in the Iran war, but the depleted inventories have created a window of vulnerability for a potential Western Pacific conflict,” the Center for Strategic and International Studies said in a May report. “The time needed to rebuild those inventories has thus become a major concern.”

___

CLAIM: “When you add the United States and Venezuela together, we have more than 60% of the oil in the world.”

THE FACTS: Trump’s numbers don’t add up. In a deal announced at the end of August, the U.S. entered into a joint venture that gives it 100-year rights to 17 oil fields in Venezuela with proven reserves of 65 billion barrels of oil. It is estimated the country has reserves totaling more than 303 billion barrels of crude oil.

The deal vastly expanded the U.S. proven oil reserves by 46 billion barrels. But because Venezuela’s energy infrastructure has been severely degraded, it will take years before new investments will lead to significantly higher oil production, experts say.

But even if that were not an issue and the largest numbers were used, the combined resources would only account for about 22% of the world’s nearly 1.6 trillion barrels of oil reserves.

In 2025, world oil production was just over 27 billion barrels of crude, according to OPEC's 2026 Statistical Bulletin. The U.S. produced nearly 5 billion barrels of crude oil in 2025 and Venezuela produced 394 million barrels. The two countries combined produced nearly 19.6% of the world's crude.

___

CLAIM: “The United States has carried out dozens of strikes on cartel drug boats, destroying 97% of the drugs coming into the ocean and sea.”

THE FACTS: Trump has made similar claims in recent months, with varying percentages. But experts say the real number can’t be known because it is impossible to determine how many drugs are not intercepted.

Asked in April for the source of Trump’s statistics after he said in a Truth Social post that 98.2% of drugs smuggled in via such routes had been stopped, the White House directed The Associated Press to Customs and Border Protection data on drug seizures.

The data showed that drug seizures made in the coastal/interior region, which includes open and coastal waters, were 98.2% lower in November 2025 than they were in July 2025. But this is not a measure of all trafficked drugs and it is only a snapshot of two specific months, not an overall trend.

“Drug seizure data measure interdiction activity, not actual trafficking volume,” Dessa Bergen-Cico, a professor of public health at Syracuse University who studies drug trafficking, told the AP at the time. “As drug policy researchers have noted, no one knows how much goes uncaught, and changes in seizure data are insufficient to make definitive claims about policy outcomes.”

Interdiction activity refers to the prevention of illicit drugs from reaching their destination.

Claims the AP has previously fact-checked

CLAIM: “More Americans are working today by far than ever before.”

THE FACTS: It’s true that “more Americans are working today by far than ever before," but the statement needs context. The economy adds jobs most months, so U.S. payrolls are constantly hitting new highs. Jobs have increased in the U.S. in 65 of the last 80 years.

___

CLAIM: “Since I took office, we have created more than 1 million new private sector jobs."

THE FACTS: The U.S. has added 807,000 jobs since Trump’s second administration began, close to his claim of 1 million. But by historical standards, it’s not a particularly large increase.

___

CLAIM: “Since I took office, it has been my great honor to settle eight wars.”

THE FACTS: Although Trump has helped mediate relations among many nations, his impact isn't as clear-cut as he makes it seem. In at least two instances of peace he claims credit for achieving, there were no wars to end. He also began the ongoing war between the U.S. and Iran.

___

CLAIM: “We've secured commitments for $21 trillion in new investments from all over the planet.”

THE FACTS: This $21 trillion figure appears to be exaggerated, highly speculative, and far higher than the actual sum of domestic and foreign investments in the U.S. The White House website offers a far lower number, $11.2 trillion, and that figure appears to include some investment commitments made during the Biden administration.

___

Associated Press writer Ben Finley and fact-check news editor Barbara Whitaker contributed to this report.

___

Find AP Fact Checks here: https://apnews.com/APFactCheck.

A reptile believed to be struggling in sand at a Southern California beach was simply making history: a sea turtle laying eggs on the U.S. West Coast.

And three days later, there were more. An olive ridley turtle — maybe the same one — laid eggs on Sept. 19, a few miles away near the Huntington Beach Pier in Orange County, authorities said.

“This is the first-ever recorded natural nesting for any sea turtle species” on the West Coast, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s West Coast Fisheries division said on Facebook.

Olive ridley turtles are the smallest of sea turtles, with adults weighing up to 100 pounds (45.3 kilograms). NOAA said they're found worldwide but primarily in the tropical waters of the Pacific, Indian and Atlantic oceans.

The first nesting spot was near Seal Beach on Sept. 16, followed by the discovery at Huntington Beach. Both sites were subsequently fenced off. Incubation typically lasts 45 to 60 days, NOAA said.

“We’re excited about it,” said Trevor McDonald, marine safety chief at the Huntington Beach Fire Department.

Lifeguards patrolling at night saw a turtle digging in the sand and thought “maybe this turtle is sick. We just don't see this very often,” McDonald said. “Then they observed the turtle starting to lay eggs.”

Heidi Stephen said her 9-year-old son, Jude, begged her to take him to Huntington Beach to see the nest Tuesday.

“It's so magical,” Stephen said.

George Zamora said he hopes the eggs can survive any impact from tides, storms and popular beach events.

“Let them do their thing,” Zamora said. “Let them be born.”

___

White reported from Detroit.

Nigella Lawson said she was "full of cake, hope and expectation" as she made her judging debut on The Great British Bake Off.

The 66-year-old TV cook joined fellow judge Paul Hollywood for the new Channel 4 series, which returned on Tuesday evening.

Presenters Alison Hammond and Noel Fielding introduced Lawson to the Bake Off tent, where contestants greeted her with a round of applause.

During the first episode, Lawson said she "loved" being in the tent.

She said: "I’m full of cake and hope and expectation.

"The standard is incredibly high."

Discussing the bakers she added: "It’s also important for them to learn. None of us are finished articles."

The new series kicked off with a chocolate stout cake task before the bakers were set a coffee and walnut cake for their technical challenge.

open image in gallery The series kicked off with a chocolate stout cake before the new bakers were tasked with making a coffee and walnut cake for their technical challenge ( Channel 4/Love Productions/Patch Dolan )

While tasting Tom’s tipsy cherry chocolate stout cake, Lawson said: “The flavours are giving me a lot of pleasure but I think you have gone a little heavy handed on the bicarb (bicarbonate soda).”

She praised Mo’s peanut and caramel chocolate stout cake as “sensational” and said it looked “irresistible”.

“When you have a bit of salt in something you are just singing a song,” she said.

“That looks rather spectacular. I’m in heaven.”

Hollywood said he loved the cake and added that the flavours were “absolutely spot on”.

“Looking forward to seeing what you are going to do next,” he said.

The bakers’ creativity was pushed to the limit again as they made a self-portrait showstopper.

open image in gallery Mo was named star baker this week ( Channel 4/Love Productions/Patch Dolan )

Lawson said she was excited about the first showstopper of the series to see the bakers show off their “artistic skill”.

She appeared moved during Gabe’s showstopper, Blu Romantic portrait cake, which involved cracking a “mirror” to reveal the true identity.

Lawson added: “If you are not the Picasso of patisserie what I want is a bit of personality, some wit.”

Asked about the apparently missing portrait, Gabe, who is a drag artist and performs under the name Blu Romantic, said: “There is a mirror on the front of the cake. Usually my drag persona isn’t around, so you have to get into that mirror so that you can see it.”

Hollywood cracked the mirror to reveal a picture of Gabe’s drag king persona, and Lawson said: “Oh, that is clever.

“That is rather profound actually. A lot of us feel we have a person beyond the surface.”

During the showstopper another contestant, Shannon, became unwell and was unable to finish her bake.

Fielding later announced that Mo had been named Star Baker while Hammond revealed nobody would be going home in the first week.

Lawson replaced Dame Prue Leith, who announced in January that she was stepping down after nine seasons on the show.

Bake Off will return next Tuesday at 8pm on Channel 4.

The former CEO of a defense contractor told the FBI that he attempted to bribe Maine Sen. Susan Collins using shell companies and straw donors to hide nearly $200,000 in gifts, an article from ProPublica revealed on Tuesday.

Martin Kao told the agency that the donation was part of a nearly $1m effort to influence lawmakers of both parties in states around the country, which ProPublica first reported was backed up with receipts of his donations in FEC filings. The money to Collins’s campaign, Kao claimed to investigators, came directly in response to a request from Collins super PAC director Scott Reed, and resulted in Kao telling his company’s associates in emails that the senator had committed to steering $32m worth of government contracts their way.

The former Navatek CEO pleaded guilty to campaign finance violations in 2022 and was sentenced to 87 months in prison in early 2025, just one month after Donald Trump returned to office and began a purge of the FBI officials and agents who took part in the investigations into his attempts to overturn the election and January 6.

Several figures involved with obtaining Kao’s testimony were let go, according to ProPublica, and the agency’s public corruption unit was effectively frozen. The illegal campaign donations to Collins were originally reported in 2021, and at the time both the Collins re-election campaign (which received the money in the 2020 cycle) and the Collins PAC returned the money.

But Collins’s Senate team, locked in one of the most important Senate races of the 2026 cycle, is furiously denying the report and Kao’s newly reported allegations of a pay-to-play scheme. The senator’s D.C. office did not immediately return a request for clarification from The Independent regarding when they were notified the case had been dropped. In total, Kao donated to nearly two dozen politicians in the House and Senate, Republicans and Democrats, including Collins before his guilty plea in 2022.

open image in gallery Susan Collins is fighting in one of the most important Senate races this cycle ( Getty )

“The seven-year-old allegations made against Senator Collins and her staff in this piece are categorically false. There have never been any allegations of wrongdoing by the Collins for Senator campaign, and the campaign was never the target of the FBI investigation,” wrote Collins’ deputy chief of staff, Annie Clark.

“It is important to note that during the Biden Administration the FBI and the Department of Justice thoroughly investigated the Navatek matter. The Collins campaign cooperated fully with the FBI throughout the investigation, producing all of the documents it requested and serving as fact witnesses in official settings. In response to the allegations in the ProPublica piece, the FBI clearly stated that a suggestion of wrongdoing by Senator Collins or her staff is ‘totally false.’ These issues were resolved in 2021, and the FBI has not contacted us about Martin Kao since then,” Collins’ deputy chief of staff wrote.

open image in gallery Collins sits on the powerful Appropriations committee, which can steer money to specific military research proposals ( Getty )

open image in gallery Collins' opponent, Troy Jackson, called Kao's claims evidence of 'corruption of the highest order.' ( Getty )

The senator’s office did not address why, as ProPublica’s report revealed, her office steered millions of dollars’ worth of government contracts to Navatek, or why a deputy to Reed at his super PAC emailed Kao and sought his phone number, so that Collins could call him and thank him for his support. Reed, in a statement to ProPublica, denied ever discussing Kao’s donation with Collins or her staff. He did not explain why he responded that it was “very smart” for him to make a donation to the PAC through a shell company. As a recipient of federal government contracts, any political donation from Navatek — either through a shell company or direct — is illegal.

According to Kao’s testimony, the company pitched individual lawmakers in private sessions on military research projects, often allegedly prompting Appropriations staffers to put language into bills making Navatek the logical (or only) choice for hyper-specific projects worth millions of dollars. At those meetings, Kao and former Navatek staffers all testified that lawmakers in the House and Senate would directly solicit donations that were understood to be bribes by all parties involved. No lawmakers were mentioned by name, specifically.

Then, completing the chain, Kao told investigators that committee staff and aides to lawmakers would lean on defense officials to see the contracts awarded to Navatek directly.

The FBI did not end up helping Kao secure any time off for his cooperation, and the former CEO was imprisoned last year. His company now operates as “PacMar Technologies”, under its previous ownership. An FBI spokesperson denied that the investigation ever turned up evidence implicating Collins’ staff (or staffers to any other lawmakers) or her allied PAC director, Scott Reed, in illegal activity. No one besides Kao and his associates at Navatek was ever charged.

Kao also told the FBI that while his company was taking more than $40 million a year in government contracts, the research it conducted did not result in any products the government eventually purchased.

Collins is dueling Troy Jackson in one of the most crucial seats for Democrats to pick up this cycle on their quest to obtain a majority in the Senate. Jackson, who replaced Graham Platner in August, called the detailed arrangement “corruption of the highest order” in a statement posted to X on Tuesday.

“Susan Collins delivered millions in taxpayer dollars for a corrupt donor bankrolling her campaign, and then Donald Trump helped her cover it up,” wrote Jackson.

Collins’s campaign did not immediately return a request for comment.

News.title: England learn more in scrappy Sri Lanka win than in summer of white-ball walkovers
News.content:
You do not expect spinners to dominate at Chester-le-Street, but this hot summer has produced strange events, none more so than Jacks recording the second-best figures by an England spinner in one-day international cricket having previously only taken three wickets in 16 games at home.

Sachindu Colombage, Sri Lanka’s debutant leggie who was playing club cricket in East Anglia a year ago, laid down a marker as he impressed with three for 44 starting with the wicket of Joe Root, his first dismissal in one-day international cricket since February.

England’s 89-run win was completed by Jacks taking three for none in four balls as Sri Lanka were bowled out for 176, their run chase a timid effort when they had a sniff of victory after restricting England to 265 and preventing them from hitting a six for the first time in an innings since 2019.

Vice-captain Jacks has evolved under Brooks’s leadership from an opening batsman to middle-order finisher who can chip in with the ball. “He is just a good leader with bat ball and in the field. He is buying into everything we want to do,” Brook said. “We are always talking about adapting to conditions and he has done it really well since coming back in. He could have moaned and ground about batting in the middle order and playing as an all-rounder but has accepted that will be his palace for a long time.”

Brook thought England made “just about par” on a very dry pitch and was reluctant to shower too much praise on batting consultant Kevin Pietersen, whose spin class the day before concentrated on making runs on a slow surface. “It will take time, more than one day. He’s not a miracle worker but it helps the more opportunity we get,” Brook said.

England were stretched and Pietersen will be happy. He told them to think about their approach, that in this type of game “rotation of strike is incredibly important”. He was right, they ran well, apart from Rehan Ahmed, and did not hit a six in an innings for the first time in seven years.

When England batsmen tried to force the pace they perished. Ben Duckett, Root and Brook all had opportunities to build an innings without seeing it through and it required Jacks to tip the total to more than 250. He batted within himself at first, but hit four fours in a row in the 47th over in a late burst that took England to a winning score.

News.title: Africa faces new threat as chronic disease rate leaps
News.content:
Chronic ailments like heart disease, cancers and diabetes now account for almost half of deaths in Africa and will soon overtake the continent’s infectious disease toll, new research has found.

Between 1990 and 2023 the proportion of deaths caused by non-communicable diseases (NCDs) almost doubled, from 25 per cent to 45 per cent, with heart disease and strokes now the leading killers.

The shift is not unexpected: public health experts have long warned that although African countries are making huge strides cutting infectious disease deaths through vaccinations, better sanitation and improved healthcare, lifestyle changes pose a new threat.

But the continent is not necessarily ready to tackle this “epidemiological transition”, researchers warned, in a study published in the Lancet Global Health journal on Tuesday.

“Although the epidemiological transition is well recognised, the speed and scale of NCD growth in Africa is particularly concerning,” they wrote.

“Health systems face increasing demands for chronic disease management, yet low-resource settings remain poorly equipped, underfunded, and unable to provide adequate preventive or treatment services.”

News.title: Zika mosquitoes still breeding in London
News.content:
Dr Medlock said there is still “no conclusive” evidence about how the insects arrived, but it’s possible that someone brought them back from holiday in their luggage, or that mosquito eggs were hidden on a tropical plant.

The mosquitoes are very temperature sensitive – they typically survive and multiply between 25C and 30C – and the UK has historically been too cold. But the species are gradually making their way north through Europe, after successive summers of record heat.

As temperatures drop in the coming weeks, the UKHSA hopes London’s invasive mosquitoes will die off naturally – though an unprecedented El Niño has made the predicament more challenging.

“This is a tropical mosquito, so the model has convinced me this won’t survive the winter,” Dr Medlock said. “Although we’ve got El Niño, [so] it’s very mild – it’s certainly warm enough still in East London [for the insects to survive].”

Diseases such as dengue and Zika virus do not typically circulate in Britain, but an infected traveller returning from a country where the diseases are present could carry the virus back with them.

If an invasive mosquito then bit an infected person, it could potentially catch and spread on the disease to others.

Several countries in Europe, including France, Italy and Spain, have started to see local transmission of mosquito-borne viruses, including dengue fever and West Nile virus, in recent years as the climate becomes more suitable for mosquitoes to survive and multiply.

Just last week, a third person died in Frankfurt, Germany, from malaria despite having no travel history, after mosquitoes infected with the disease were imported into the country on an aeroplane and subsequently infected eight people over the summer.

“We [already] see imported cases of malaria, dengue and chikungunya each year, with significant associated mortality and morbidity,” Dr Phillip Veal, a consultant in public health at the UKHSA, said.

“But if we [in Britain] follow the pattern of Europe, and all models suggest we will, Aedes albopictus and other Aedes species may become established. We’ve got a window of opportunity to do something, to prepare, to be ready, to fulfil our mission of protecting the public,” Dr Veal said.

Protect yourself and your family by learning more about Global Health Security

News.title: Tax rises ‘virtually inevitable’ after £8bn borrowing blow
News.content:
Tax rises are “virtually inevitable” after official figures showed the Treasury has borrowed £8bn more than expected so far this year.

Economists said the Chancellor faced an “uncomfortable” Budget after the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said spending outstripped tax receipts by £18.3bn in August, £3.5bn more than expected.

It means John Healey, the Chancellor, has borrowed £77.3bn so far this financial year, which is £8.1bn more than forecast.

Reacting to the figures, Emma Reynolds, the Chief Secretary to the Treasury, warned of “tough decisions” in Mr Healey’s Budget.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “The jump in borrowing in August compared to last year sets the stage for what is likely to be a much trickier Budget than Andy Burnham or Healey anticipated when they came to power.

“Another round of tax rises in October now looks inevitable.”

Philip Shaw, an economist at Investec, added: “We suspect that some tax increases are virtually inevitable.”

Ruth Gregory, deputy chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said the Chancellor would need to raise up to £14bn to restore the £24bn of fiscal headroom left by his predecessor Rachel Reeves to balance the books.

The Government’s debt interest bill soared to £8.8bn last month, according to the ONS, the biggest August figure since records began in 1997.

So far this year, the Treasury has spent £50bn on debt interest – £2bn more than forecast in March.

Nick Ridpath, an economist at the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said: “Debt interest spending is a worryingly large share of overall government spending.

“Both higher borrowing costs and higher inflation make life harder for a Chancellor who is looking to bring down borrowing and to spend more on government priorities.”

Higher prices caused by the Iran war mean the Chancellor must pay more interest on the country’s huge stock of inflation-linked debt.

Inflation is also pushing up the welfare bill. The Government spent almost £30bn in August on benefits, 7pc more than a year ago.

Despite this, the Treasury continued to see substantial tax receipts. Income tax, capital gains, and National Insurance receipts stood at £231bn in the financial year to August.

That is £16.6bn higher than the same period a year ago.

Inheritance tax receipts also grew. They have risen to £3.8bn so far this financial year, a £100m increase compared with a year ago.

Ms Reynolds, the Treasury minister, said: “At a time when debt interest costs billions of pounds that could otherwise be spent on improving lives, we must always know where the money is coming from to pay for public services.

“That is why we are committed to meeting our fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty.”

The figures also showed total debt rose to £2.985tn in August, taking the level just shy of £3tn.

Andrew Griffith, the shadow chancellor, said: “Labour has lost control of the public finances.

“It takes a rare fiscal incontinence to have both the highest tax take in history and see borrowing still shoot up.”

News.title: France releases infertile Asian tiger mosquitoes to fight dengue threat
News.content:
French cities are fighting the growing threat of diseases like dengue, chikungunya and Zika in mainland Europe by releasing millions of sterile male Asian tiger mosquitoes.

Terratis, a new company in the southern city of Montpellier, is breeding infertile males on an industrial scale as a long-term solution to the rapid spread of the disease-carrying insects.

The sterile males are bred at a factory in the southern city of Montpellier and then released in urban hot zones where the mosquitoes are most prevalent. After they have mated, females reproduce only empty eggs for the remainder of their lives.

“By using this technique, the mosquitoes will have no descendants and then, in theory, we can reduce the population with each generation,” said Clelia Oliva, the founder of Terratis.

“We are confident of being able to achieve a reduction of between 70 and 90 per cent in the towns in which we are releasing the sterile mosquitoes.”

The company, which started only two years ago, has experienced a dramatic surge in demand in the last few years as France tries to deal with the invasive species.

News.title: ‘42 surgeries in 48 hours’: Doctors face extreme pressure in South Sudan
News.content:
Dr Mathiang Agany had no idea what was coming.

On a humid morning in April, scores of patients were rushed into his basic hospital in rural South Sudan after a shoot out between rival gangs. As the most senior doctor, Dr Agany, a maternal health specialist, had to perform 42 surgeries in just 48 hours.

Working alongside a second surgeon, a nurse and an anaesthetist, Dr Agany, 44, carefully extracted bullets from the vital organs of nine patients.

In 22 cases, he glued together fractured bones; and in four others he clamped damaged tissues shut and repaired torn organs.

Over the same 48 hour period, he also delivered seven babies through emergency c-sections.

“You are tired... but you can relax later,” he told The Telegraph over a video call.

“My job [was] to keep people alive”.

Separate to the ruinous four-year civil war in neighbouring Sudan, the violence plaguing South Sudan is inter-communal, a self-perpetuating cycle of cattle raiding, territorial disputes and revenge attacks carried out by armed youth militias from pastoral communities known as Titweng (“cattle guard”).

Young children were among the victims, including a four-year-old boy, whose leg was fractured by a gunshot, and a nine-month-old baby girl whose chest was grazed by the same bullet that killed her father.

News.title: Afghan medical students face expulsion from Pakistan
News.content:
An educational lifeline for young Afghan women banned by the Taliban from training as doctors in their homeland is in jeopardy after Pakistan’s medical authorities tried to have them expelled.

Several hundred Afghan female students studying across the border in Pakistan have been threatened with removal, amid rising tensions and tit-for-tat exchanges between the neighbours.

The Pakistan Medical and Dental Council (PMDC) which regulates medical education earlier this month ordered medical and dental colleges with Afghan students to kick them out.

Within days, major institutions including King Edward Medical University (KEMU), Shaikh Khalifa Bin Zayed Al Nahyan Medical and Dental College, and the Services Institute of Medical Sciences, had ordered Afghan students to leave.

The nationwide order was estimated to have affected around 1,000 Afghan students, with 35 per cent of those thought to be female students.

Provincial high courts have now temporarily halted the expulsion pending further hearings, but Afghan students told The Telegraph they were terrified their careers would be ended.

“The government’s decision aimed to send us to the Stone Age because the Taliban in Afghanistan have banned female education,” said Sabiha Daftani, one of the 22 Afghan students given orders on September 7 by KEMU in Lahore on to leave within 24 hours.

“The fear is constant and haunting us,” she said.

MARCO SILVA has hinted that he could leave Benfica… just three months after taking the job.

The Portuguese boss, 49, left Fulham over the summer after five years in charge at Craven Cottage.



Silva went on to replace Real Madrid-bound Jose Mourinho at Benfica, but isn’t wholly enjoying the experience so far.

Last weekend’s 3-1 defeat at Porto left the Lisbon side already trailing their opponents by five points at the top of the table.



Benfica’s task had been made infinitely more difficult when former Tottenham and Barcelona centre-back Clement Lenglet was sent off after just 35 minutes.

Lenglet’s red card was for the lightest of slaps to the back of Andre Silva‘s head, the striker then theatrically going down and rolling around.

Speaking after his side’s 3-1 defeat, the Benfica boss suggested that officials in Portugal can be “influenced” by pre-match comments.

Per Portuguese outlet Record, Silva said: “I won’t comment on the sending off.

Villas-Boas called some of the decisions against his own team “difficult to understand” – but labelled Lenglet’s red card as “great refereeing”.

MANCHESTER United have taken another giant leap forward in their quest for a new £2billion stadium.

The Red Devils set out to replace the 75,000-seater Old Trafford with a colossal 100,000-seater stadium in early 2024.



Since then, the Premier League club have been met with a series of hurdles that they are slowly overcoming – with many in doubt that they will actually happen.

The latest green light in a barrage of red tape comes with the council’s public consultation process as United look to appease the wider community before they apply for planning permission.



Since July, Trafford Town Hall, Media City, Gorse Hill Studios and Metro Sports Club have all held sessions for the local residents to comment on the mega plans.

And many more have had their say online.

United – who currently sit 12th in the Prem – had club representatives in each of the meetings.

But the engagement process throughout the entire process is said to have been headed in the right direction.

The responses gathered from the sessions and online will now be used to formulate and alter their masterplan.

The £2bn project is set to create a whopping 48,000 jobs and 15,000 new homes.

And it will boost the UK economy by £7.3bn every year.

United will now go to fans who will get their say on the ground’s design.

At the council launch in July, Collette Roche – the CEO of new stadium development for United – explained that the controverisal tent design unveiled last year is not “set in stone”.

When they first released images and graphics of the flashy design, eager fans rushed to troll the plans.



Some fans compared it to a “circus”, while others likened it to budget holiday park Butlin’s Minehead, where Man Utd super fan Luke Littler won the UK Open darts.

In late August, United chief executive Omar Berrada said: “Over the summer we shared the proposed new location of the stadium.

“We will be working closely with our fans over the coming months to keep you involved in that process.”

The stadium is set to lie about 350 metres north-west of the existing Old Trafford stadium – with the land already secured.

XABI ALONSO’S first five Premier League games have been thrilling, ridiculous and worrying in equal measure.

The 12 goals Alonso’s side have conceded across their opening five games match the club record for the most shipped across that many games in the Premier League.

LEE CARSLEY wants to work with Max Dowman before the Three Lions come calling for the 16-year-old sensation.

Arsenal wonderkid Dowman is set to play with the Under-19s on Friday, but has been on England boss Thomas Tuchel‘s radar since before the World Cup.



Tuchel is considering asking Dowman to walk a few pitches over for his first taste of senior training with Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham at St George’s Park this week.

Under-21s boss Carsley could lose some of his youth stars to Tuchel’s group after Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Tino Livarmento pulled out of the four Nations League matches, starting with the opener at home to Spain on Saturday.



Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up by Tuchel as a result of all the dropouts

The major reshuffle could see Dowman bumped up to the U21s squad for their final Euro qualifiers against Kazakhstan, Slovakia and the Republic of Ireland.

But Carsley, targeting a Euros three-peat next summer, warned against rushing the Arsenal teen into the senior squad before he is ready.

Carsley said: “It’s important players develop at their own pace. Max is an outstanding talent, the timing and the balance of when he comes to the Under-21s is inevitable.

“He’s going to the U21s because of his talent, but we have to make sure we do that at the right time. We have to be patient and make sure that ultimately we want them to play for the senior team for a prolonged period.

“So we have to make sure that we get the time right with that. We had a similar issue a few years ago with Ethan Nwaneri.

“He was early and he made his debut and he’s done really well and there’s that tendency to push him on quickly.”

Nwaneri’s club career has stalled slightly, following his eye-catching start with Arsenal. He’s currently on loan at Borussia Dortmund, but it’s easy to forget he is still only 19.

Nwaneri won the Under-21 Euros last year, trained with the seniors in Florida before the World Cup and is an important part of Carsley’s current group.



Dowman has until March 30 to break Theo Walcott’s 20-year record as England’s youngest-ever player at 17 years and 75 days old in 2006.

The Gunners star doesn’t turn 17 until December 30 — meaning he could have two chances to make history before the end of the season, with the November and March international windows potential opportunities.

Carsley added: “Thomas and I speak regularly about squad selection and obviously Max is always in the conversation because of his talent.

“It’s not one size fits all. Some players are just ready for it, physically, mentally, ready to compete and they’re at the stage where they’re just above that age group, and we have to make sure that we get the time we want with that.”

Dowman is already a Premier League winner after making six appearances for Mikel Arteta’s champions in his debut season, breaking Nwaneri’s record for the league’s youngest-ever goalscorer against Everton in March.



Carsley name-dropped former team-mate Wayne Rooney, a once-in-a-lifetime talent who jumped age groups to make his senior debut at 17 years and 111 days, as an exception to the rule.

He said: “I always think back to Everton with Wayne when he was coming through. He was just ready, but he was at the right club at the right time.

“There’s a lot that went in the right direction for Wayne to be in that position. But we have to make sure that players will get minutes in their age groups.”



Dowman is expected to follow a similar path to Bellingham, who played a handful of games for the Under-21s in 2020 before earning a call-up to Gareth Southgate’s Euro 2020 squad in 2021.

Carsley revealed he feels a responsibility to help England find a successor to Kane at No. 9.

The former England interim boss called up 21-year-old Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear, who has scored six goals in eight Championship games since his £20m summer move from Tottenham.

Midfielder Miley (4 pts) played as an emergency right-back and made four tackles.

Willock (12 pts) earned three bonus points via two successful dribbles, three fouls won and a pass completion rate of 92%.

Newcastle have conceded the most shots (98) in the Premier League this season.



Belloumi (9 pts) was once again the Tigers’ standout player with five shots, six tackles and an assist.

Tzolakis (5 pts) saved Wissa’s (0 pts) penalty but was shown a yellow card for delaying tactics — he also got a bonus point for three keeper sweeps and two succesful claims.

Nottingham Forest 0 – 1 Coventry

Goals: Dasilva

Dasilva Assists: Rushworth

Possession: Forest 62% – 38% Coventry

Forest 62% – 38% Coventry Shots: Forest 24 – 10 Coventry

Forest 24 – 10 Coventry xG: Forest 1.2 – 0.7 Coventry

Despite a disappointing result for the hosts, popular midfielder Gibbs-White (6 pts) came away with a respectable haul courtesy of three bonus points.

He also created six chances for his team-mates.



Williams (4 pts) had three shots, created four chances, and missed out on three bonus points by one PPM having delivered four accurate crosses.

Forest need to improve their finishing as they rank third for total shots in the league but 18th for shots on target.

Rushworth (12 pts) is the first goalkeeper to provide an assist this season — he was also the best-performing player in his position in Gameweek 5.

Pinnock (8 pts) made five blocks to help the Sky Blues to their first clean sheet since promotion.

Thomas-Asante (7 pts) earned three bonus points via four interceptions, four fouls won and two successful dribbles.



The 27-year-old is categorised as a midfielder but played as a striker in the absence of the suspended Awoniyi.

Bournemouth 0 – 1 Liverpool

Goals: Isak

Isak Assists: Wirtz

Possession: Bournemouth 46% – 54% Liverpool

Bournemouth 46% – 54% Liverpool Shots: Bournemouth 9 – 12 Liverpool

Bournemouth 9 – 12 Liverpool xG: Bournemouth 0.8 – 1.6 Liverpool

£2.9m defender Hill (7 pts) made four tackles and earned three bonus points via four blocks.

Christie (2 pts) was responsible for over half the Cherries’ xG (0.5) via four shots but squandered his opportunities and failed to test Alisson (9 pts).

Scott (3 pts) won five free-kicks and ranks first among midfielders for bonus points and PPM.



Bournemouth are one of just three Prem teams yet to win a league game this season and find themselves 17th in the table but their performances have been better than their results suggest.

If all games had finished at half time, Marco Rose’s men would be top of the table.

20.4%-owned Isak (8 pts) ranks joint-fourth among strikers having scored his fourth goal of the campaign.

Liverpool’s goalkeeper fell one PPM short of three bonus points.

Jacquet (8 pts) is settling in nicely at Liverpool and has six more points than Van Dijk (7 pts) overall — the Frenchman is £1m cheaper than his senior partner too.



Leeds 0 – 0 Crystal Palace

Possession: Leeds 51% – 49% Palace

Leeds 51% – 49% Palace Shots: Leeds 13 – 12 Palace

Leeds 13 – 12 Palace xG: Leeds 1.4 – 0.7 Palace

Justin (12 pts) was the only player from either side to earn three bonus points — the adaptable defender also created a big chance and made three tackles.

Trafford (9 pts) made five saves and ranks joint-second among goalkeepers overall having amassed 39 points — nobody has made more saves at this stage.

Okafor (4 pts) completed six dribbles to take his tally for the season to 16, the highest among all forwards.

The Whites boast the best defensive record in the top flight having conceded three goals across their first five league games.



Bogle (6 pts), Justin and Muharemovic (7 pts) are all among the top eight Dream Team defenders at present — the latter had four shots against the Eagles.

Mitchell (9 pts) made five tackles while Pino (3 pts) was the only Palace player to earn a bonus point.

Manchester City 5 – 3 Sunderland

Semenyo’s (21 pts) big haul represents 47.7% of his season’s total of 44 points.



Gvardiol (5 pts) provided his third assist of the season from left back.

78.8%-owned Haaland (9 pts) took his time but eventually scored his seventh goal of the season and sits atop the rankings on 68 points.

Hat-trick hero Brobbey (25 pts) edged out Semenyo to be Gameweek 5’s top performer having mustered just 10 points from the first four Gameweeks.

The Black Cats’ No9 registered an individual xG of 2.8 from five shots.

Mukiele (4 pts) created a big chance, made four tackles and earned three bonus points but incurred minus four points for five goals conceded.

Iwobi (6 pts) created five chances (two big chances).

Midfielder Charles (6 pts) continues to rack up PPM easily with another 10 in this game, half of them coming from blocks.



After Cunha’s (11 pts) late equaliser, the Cottagers are now 19th in the table with just two points to show for their efforts.

The Red Devils rank first in the league for shots but have converted just eight of their 113 efforts into goals.

Rashford (4 pts), Mbeumo (7 pts) and Martinez (2 pts) had six, five and four shots respectively but met an in-form Leno (4 pts), who made five good saves.

Our next DEEP DIVE we’ll recap Gameweek 6’s Premier League action in mid-October.

Sports.title: What Mikel Arteta’s rivals think about Arsenal boss as new contract 'agreed'
Sports.content:
What Mikel Arteta’s rivals think about Arsenal boss as new contract 'agreed'

Mikel Arteta is close to signing a new contract at Arsenal with the Gunners having rewarded the Spaniard for his work at the Emirates Stadium following his appointment in 2019

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal with Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has agreed a new deal with Arsenal in a move that will be welcomed by the Gunners - but not their rivals. The Spanish coach was appointed in 2019 as a replacement for Unai Emery and has done some brilliant work with the north London side.

‌



He has completely reversed the club’s fortunes over recent years to take them from mid-table to the Premier League title. Arteta has also restored Arsenal at the top of the European game, having led them to the Champions League final last term.

‌



With Arteta now set to remain with the club for the foreseeable future, his rivals will now have to continue mulling over their attempts to get the better of him.

‌



But what have they already said? Mirror Football takes a trawl through some past interviews and press conferences to find out exactly what they think of the Arsenal boss.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Xabi Alonso

Let’s start with someone who knows Arteta very well: Xabi Alonso. The two Spaniards are childhood friends and have embarked on very similar careers, with glittering playing stints in the Premier League, while they have now turned to management.

They have already locked horns this season, with the Gunners running out 2-1 winners in the Premier League earlier this month.

Speaking ahead of that game, Alonso praised his friend for his work at the Emirates and vowed that they would never think differently of each other despite now being direct rivals.

‌



He said: “No, it [their relationship] won't change. Our friendship and mutual respect won't change because of competition, because the system he's built at Arsenal is truly remarkable, and it's a long-term process.”

Andoni Iraola

Alonso is not the only close friend that Arteta has in the Premier League. Current Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola also grew up alongside the pair in the Basque region of Spain.

And he has already played quite a crucial role in his career so far, with his former side Bournemouth having held Manchester City last season to hand the Gunners the title.

‌



Iraola claimed that it was just the reward that both Arteta and Arsenal deserved after a number of near misses.

Speaking at the time, he said: “Happy for him because I think he has done an incredible job there. For a lot of seasons very consistent. Sometimes he has been so close, the reward has probably come in the right moment."

View 4 Images Arteta and Alonso are childhood friends (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Michael Carrick

Another top-flight manager who is well-acquainted with Arteta is Manchester United boss Michael Carrick. The pair faced off on a number of occasions during their playing careers and have already sparred on the touchline.

They at first clashed back in the 2021/22 season, with Carrick overseeing an interim role at United. He was successful on that occasion with a 3-2 win and repeated that result last term.

Regardless, Carrick remains a big fan of Arteta and the work he has done in north London. He said: ''I think he's done a very good job at Arsenal and you can see they're going in a certain direction and been pretty strong with that.

‌



''He was a terrific player, very technical, and that’s the way his teams plays and obviously the way he has coached them in that style shows what type of player he was.''

View 4 Images Carrick is a big fan of Arteta's work at Arsenal (Image: Getty Images)

Unai Emery

Arteta’s longevity at the Emirates Stadium is a huge departure from his predecessor Unai Emery. The Spaniard was afforded just 18 months in north London after replacing Arsene Wenger.

‌



And that decision looks to have been for the betterment of both Arsenal and Emery - the pair having thrived apart.

The now Aston Villa coach has praised his compatriot for steering the ship back on course. He said: “The work Arteta is doing there now is brilliant and he’s doing more or less everything I was thinking needed to be done there.”

There was a brief flashpoint between the two when Emery chose not to shake Arteta’s hand after a game but that does not appear to have caused a lasting issue since then.

‌



View 4 Images Arteta and Maresca have already clashed this season (Image: Getty Images)

Enzo Maresca

One of Arteta’s main rivals this season looks to be Enzo Maresca. The Italian has replaced both his and Arteta’s former tutor Pep Guardiola at the Etihad and will be expected to put together a title charge throughout the season.

Speaking about the pair’s learnings under Guardiola, Maresca said: “Probably we [himself and Arteta] both have to be thankful because we worked besides and next to the one that I consider the best manager in the world. Probably we both have been quite lucky to work with Pep."

‌



Roberto De Zerbi

While Maresca will be one of those plotting Arteta’s downfall, the same could certainly be said of Roberto De Zerbi. The Italian is now in charge of Arsenal’s North London rivals Tottenham.

And while some fans might be wanting some hostility between the two, De Zerbi made his admiration of Arteta clear during his spell with former club Brighton.

He said: “Arteta is a great manager. He is very young and his style is clear. I enjoy watching Arsenal games… I try to learn something when I watch them. He was lucky to work with Pep Guardiola and now I think Arteta is one of the best coaches in the world.”

Sports.title: Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close
Sports.content:
Liverpool close in on Richard Hughes successor with FSG sporting director decision close

Liverpool's majority owners, Fenway Sports Group (FSG), have been pondering who to replace Richard Hughes with following his departure as sporting director earlier this month

View 2 Images Julian Ward is expected to become Liverpool's new sporting director (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Fenway Sports Group have reportedly decided to make an internal appointment to replace Richard Hughes as Liverpool's sporting director.

‌



Hughes left his role earlier this month following a turbulent summer, choosing to join Saudi Arabian side Al-Hilal. The former Bournemouth chief spent two years in the hot seat at Anfield, overseeing the big-money transfers of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Bradley Barcola.

‌



His departure followed that of Michael Edwards, who stepped down as the chief executive officer of football of FSG in July. A busy summer also saw a consortium, which includes Amazon founder Jeff Bezos, take over a third of the club.

‌



FSG have scoured the market for Hughes' replacement before deciding to keep things in-house by choosing Julian Ward. The Athletic reports that Ward will switch from FSG technical director to Liverpool's sporting director, with a process overseen by FSG president Mike Gordon now nearing its conclusion.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Ward has been at the club since 2012 and has held a variety of roles at Liverpool and owners FSG. He was European scouting manager for Spain and Portugal, then loan pathways manager and then assistant sporting director.

Ward was promoted to become sporting director following the departure of Edwards in the summer of 2022, but stepped down at the end of the 2022/23 season, shocking Liverpool in the process. He returned to the fold by following Edwards to FSG in 2024, where he has been tasked with overseeing player development pathways and the academy, and is now returning to Anfield as sporting director.

During his short-lived previous spell as sporting director, Ward oversaw the signings of Luis Diaz, Darwin Nunez and Cody Gakpo, among other players. He was also behind the arrival of Alexis Mac Allister in the summer of 2023, having stayed longer than his exit date to seal the deal for the Brighton midfielder.

‌



View 2 Images Julian Ward (second left), with Michael Edwards (centre) and Richard Hughes (second right) (Image: Nikki Dyer - LFC/Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

It means that David Woodfine will remain as Liverpool's assistant sporting director, working underneath Ward, while Pedro Marques - who was another candidate for the role and a close colleague of Ward - will stay as FSG's director of football development.

FSG did speak to external candidates, including Brentford technical director Lee Dykes, before deciding to elevate Ward back into the hot seat. He will therefore take charge of player recruitment at Liverpool following a difficult summer.

Article continues below

Hughes' spell in charge was bookended by the £123million signing of Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while Victor Munoz, Jeremy Jacquet and Ronald Araujo all also arrived this summer. But the slow-burn nature of the summer transfer window raised plenty of eyebrows and caused some friction, with Mark Burchill and Craig McKee also leaving the club to follow Hughes to Saudi Arabia.

Andoni Iraola, who arrived following an impressive spell at Bournemouth to replace Arne Slot, was exasperated by the club's transfer business, which saw a net spend of £172m accumulated.

Sports.title: Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham reignites World Cup feud - 'You don't talk without Messi'
Sports.content:
Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham reignites World Cup feud - 'You don't talk without Messi'

Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero came to blows during Sunday's Madrid derby, having also clashed during the World Cup semi-final between England and Argentina

View 2 Images Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero locked horns at the weekend

Jude Bellingham and Cristian Romero clashed during the Madrid derby at the weekend as the opposing players reignited their World Cup feud.

‌



Atletico Madrid got the better of Jose Mourinho and Real Madrid in an ill-tempered affair, which saw Bellingham and the former Tottenham defender clash and the match end 2-1.

‌



The duo were seen exchanging words through the match at the Metropolitano, with their World Cup semi-final clash clearly still fresh in the memory. England took the lead that night before the South Americans rallied late on, scoring their winner in stoppage time.

‌



According to Movistar’s El Día Después, Bellingham poked fun at Romero, claiming he was less vocal when he didn't have Lionel Messi in his team.

He allegedly said: "When you’re with [Lionel] Messi, you talk a lot. But here, nothing." Bellingham also called the Argentine a "coward."

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Romero responded by calling Bellingham a "cry baby" and mocked the Englishman for cutting an emotional figure as he said: "you cried over there [at the World Cup]".

Earlier in the game, Bellingham was on the receiving end of a nasty challenge from Romero, which saw the former Spurs star shown a yellow card despite a VAR review. Real also felt Kang-in Lee should've been shown a red card for his ankle-high challenge on Federico Valverde. They later had Dean Huijsen sent off, which only added to their frustration.

‌



Bellingham was furious at full-time, leading the protests against referee Miguel Angel Ortiz Arias by repeatedly shouting ‘"two red cards, two!" at the official.

View 2 Images The Englishman and the Argentina star were quick to recall their World Cup encounter

Mourinho was critical of the officials after the contest, with defeat leaving Los Blancos in fourth and six points off the pace set by Barcelona. He arrived his post-match news conference carrying an A4 sheet of printed paper with screenshots displaying two incidents he believed should have resulted in Atletico dismissals.

Article continues below

"We can skip the press conference because the story of the match is right here," the Special One said as he showed media the printed images. "Those were two clear red cards. Given the difficulties we faced afterwards playing 11 against 10, we can only imagine what 50 minutes of 11 against nine would have been like."

Sports.title: Cole Palmer accused of FAKING injury and pulling out of England camp with 'the hump'
Sports.content:
Cole Palmer accused of FAKING injury and pulling out of England camp with 'the hump'

After Cole Palmer pulled out of the England squad for the upcoming international break, a huge accusation has been levelled at the Chelsea star

View 3 Images Cole Palmer is suffering from a "small muscular injury" (Image: 2026 Gaspafotos/MB Media)

Ex-West Ham United defender James Collins has accused Chelsea midfielder Cole Palmer of fabricating an injury to pull out of the England squad. Three Lions boss Thomas Tuchel called him up for England's Nations League clashes against Spain, Czechia and Croatia.

‌



Palmer, 24, was snubbed by Tuchel for the Three Lions' World Cup squad, which proved to be one on the German's most controversial selection decisions. Under Xabi Alonso, Palmer started impressively by contributing four goals and two assists in seven appearances for the west Londoners.

‌



It was claimed Palmer had a "small muscular injury" which was picked up after he was named in Tuchel's squad. However, Collins, based solely of his own experience in the game (which was not with Palmer), has suggested the injury may not be genuine.

‌



Speaking on Boyle Sports and Footy Accumulators’ podcast, 'No Tippy Tappy Football', Collins said: "I would say that Cole Palmer had got the hump. He’s got the hump that he didn’t go to the World Cup, and he’s pulled out of the England squad.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



"That’s my opinion. I don’t know the lad, but from an ex-player point of view, I think he’s got the hump. It sounds to me as an ex-player that he’s gone to the fitness coach at Chelsea and said, 'Really, I don’t fancy it, just say something’. It might not be that, but I’ve played the game, and that’s what it looks like to me.”

Chelsea have been approached for a comment. But according to football.london, the Blues want to carefully manage his muscle injury, particularly after his campaign last season was disrupted with injuries.

View 3 Images Collins made the comment on a recent podcast (Image: 2023 Jacques Feeney/Offside)

‌



It will nonetheless be frustrating for Tuchel, who praised the ex-Manchester City ace for his return to form this season. When asked why he chose to recall Palmer and Real Madrid ace Trent Alexander-Arnold, the ex-Chelsea boss said: "They had a good start to the season. They never did something wrong. We just chose different players.

"So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad."

View 3 Images Tuchel was keen to see Palmer play after not selecting him for the World Cup (Image: AFP or licensors)

Article continues below

Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Declan Rice have also pulled out of the squad. Tuchel has since responded by bringing in Morgan Gibbs-White of Nottingham Forest and Everton ace James Garner.

There has, however, not been a recall for Phil Foden, which may surprise many given the Manchester City ace could deputise for Palmer, Rashford and Mainoo. Tuchel has also chosen not to call-up Crystal Palace midfielder Adam Wharton, despite losing many midfielders to injury.

Sports.title: Barcelona confirm Nou Camp exit decision after stadium awarded Champions League final
Sports.content:
Barcelona confirm Nou Camp exit decision after stadium awarded Champions League final

Barcelona will leave the Nou Camp for a second time in a matter of years to allow redevelopment work ahead of the stadium hosting the Champions League final in three years time

View 2 Images Barcelona will leave the Nou Camp as more renovation work is sanctioned (Image: The incident occurred while work was carried out at the Spotify Camp Nou (file))

Barcelona will again leave the Nou Camp as they prepare for more renovation work on the stadium, which has just been awarded the Champions League final.

‌



The iconic stadium has been experiencing a major facelift in recent years and the club have approved another £437million worth of building work, which will see the Spanish champions moving back to the Olympic Stadium, which they have called home in recent years.

‌



Barcelona plan to return to the Nou Camp in January 2028, for the second half of the 2027-28 season, but will again spend months at the stadium which held the Games back in 1992 and has served as a temporary home.

‌



Speaking at the club's AGM, treasurer Ferran Olive confirmed the plan is for the Catalans to finish the current campaign at their traditional home before beginning next season at the Olympic Stadium.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Currently Barcelona are playing at the Nou Camp with a reduced capacity of 62,000. That is owing to the third tier being closed, but once it opens the capacity will increase to 75,000. Once the project is totally finalised the stadium will boast a roof and hold 105,000 fans.

The club know they have little to no margin for error when it comes to setbacks. The European Cup showpiece will return to Barcelona for the first time in 30 years in 2029, with its last final playing host to the historic Manchester United comeback against Bayern Munich.

The stadium renovation work began in 2023 but has been hit with severe delays. The date for the work to be completely finished has been continually pushed back, which has hit the club financially.

‌



View 2 Images The club will return to the Olympic Stadium once again (Image: Joma Garcia/Action Plus/REX/Shutterstock)

Problems with money have been well documented, with previous new signings sweating on whether they will be allowed to be registered as Barcelona battle to balance the books.

The Catalans are reliant on finishing the project to help drive the club's revenue in the coming years, but are confident it will have an instant impact. They predict income will notable rise thanks to "additional stadium-related revenue, including ticketing, VIP hospitality, the museum and other associated activities with the team's return to Camp Nou."

Sports.title: Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest
Sports.content:
Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest

Lewis Hall has chosen to extend his contract with Newcastle despite being heavily linked with Manchester United in the summer, explaining the reasons for his decision

View 2 Images Lewis Hall has chosen to extend his Newcastle contract (Image: Serena Taylor, Newcastle United via Getty Images)

Lewis Hall admits it was a "no-brainer" to sign an extension with Newcastle despite Manchester United's interest as he talked up the impact of Matthias Jaissle.

‌



The new boss, who replaced Eddie Howe in the summer, has made an immediate impression and impressed with a Magpies side that endured a poor campaign last time out and looked to have lost a bit of direction under the previous regime.

‌



Hall had to watch leading lights like Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon leave St James' Park in the summer, which led to speculation he would follow. United were particularly keen and need a left-back at Old Trafford, but Newcastle dug their heels in and maintained he wouldn't be sold.

‌



Hall has got his head down under Jaissle, still only 38, and quickly decided that the former Red Bull Salzburg manager can lead Newcastle to great heights, committing to the club for the next five years.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Quizzed on whether the transfer talk impacted on him he said: “No, honestly, it didn’t [affect me]. I guess whenever you’re linked to another team, you know that you’re doing something right. I guess it’s just a credit to your own performances and how you are as a player, how you are as a person.

“I took that as a positive, but at the same time, I knew how much I love playing here and I knew that since the manager came in, I knew the ambitions and what we wanted to achieve.

“After not many conversations, not many training sessions, I knew that the manager was going to be really good for this club and I knew that as a team, bringing in new players and improving the squad was really important and as soon as we did that, it was a no-brainer really to sign.”

‌



View 2 Images Matthias Jaissle has made an immediate impression in Newcastle

Newcastle have won two of their five games, losing just the once, with Jaissle impressing as he transitions in a host of new summer signings, many of whom were largely unknown quantities.

Hall, whilst enduring difficult moments, which included giving away a stoppage time penalty against Liverpool, has been a strong performer and that has seen him recalled to the England squad.

Article continues below

He missed out on the World Cup in the summer, which owed to his performance levels dipping in the final weeks of the season. Hall was left frustrated that Howe played him on the right, not his natural position, which he reportedly attributed to his form dropping off.

Sports.title: JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference
Sports.content:
JJ Gabriel 'reaches first major agreement' as Man Utd star tells four clubs his preference

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel expressed a desire to leave Old Trafford last week and has since been linked with some of the biggest clubs in the world

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel of Manchester United (Image: Manchester United/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United teenager JJ Gabriel reportedly wants to move to Spain if he is granted an exit from the Red Devils. It emerged earlier this month that Gabriel had expressed a desire to leave United, and there are already reports of where the playmaker could end up joining.

‌



Reports last week claimed that Gabriel had refused to take part in training for United ahead of their Carabao Cup third-round tie against Brighton. The 15-year-old was expected to be involved in the matchday squad for Michael Carrick’s side before expressing a desire to leave United.

‌



Gabriel has been tipped to have a bright future in the game, and would have been United’s youngest-ever player had he made his debut against the Seagulls at Old Trafford last week. Yet Gabriel's determination to leave United has sparked intense speculation surrounding the youngster's next move.

‌



A new update has surfaced from Spain suggesting that Gabriel could be heading across Europe should he leave United. Spanish publication Sport have reported that Gabriel's shortlist of potential destinations now features four clubs, two of which are based in Spain. Real Madrid and Barcelona are among those reportedly keen on securing Gabriel's signature, alongside Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain.

The report further claims that Gabriel and his camp have already visited Spain, touring both Madrid and Barcelona. The United starlet has reportedly reached a 'first major agreement' to join one of those clubs instead of any other team. Reports suggest Gabriel is now keen on a move to Spain, giving Barcelona and Real Madrid the upper hand in the race to sign the coveted United youngster.

Gabriel has enjoyed an impressive opening few weeks of the season, most recently scoring a hat-trick against Sabah in the UEFA Youth League earlier this month. The playmaker has also contributed two goals and two assists across just two appearances for United's Under-21s in Premier League 2.

The teenager is just a couple of weeks away from being eligible to sign a scholarship with United when he turns 16 on October 6, and will need to wait until his 17th birthday before putting pen to paper on a professional contract.

Speaking on Friday, Carrick was keen to shift the focus away from speculation surrounding the teenager and towards his wellbeing. He said: "I’ll just repeat what I said [earlier this week]: he’s a young boy, it’s important we don’t put anything out here, the exposure and scrutiny we have to be careful.

"We have to be sensible and think about him. The situation will work itself out."

Sports.title: Leigh and Wigan conduct to be investigated by RFL
Sports.content:
Leigh Leopards and Wigan Warriors will be subject to an independent investigation into their conduct and actions over the past 12 months, the Rugby Football League (RFL) has said.

The Leopards and the Warriors have had an ongoing dispute for almost 12 months, dating back to the high-profile ticketing saga that led to Leigh's owner Derek Beaumont saying his club would not participate in the fixture over a disagreement about their ticket allocation of 4,800.

They ultimately did play the game and were eliminated from the play-offs with Wigan winning 18-6.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the Super League semi-final match between Wakefield Trinity and Leigh Leopards

With the Warriors set to host Wakefield in the play-off semi-final on Saturday, matters reignited again over the weekend after an original post from Wigan detailed ticketing arrangements for whichever side visited the Brick this weekend in the play-offs would receive an allocation of 5,000 tickets for safety reasons.

Leigh were beaten by Wakefield Trinity in their eliminator match, where a win for the Leopards would have seen them progress to face Wigan instead.

Beaumont put himself in the spotlight again with a tirade on social media site X following Wigan's statement and his activity could also breach the RFL's own social media code of conduct.

The RFL said in a statement: "The independent Rugby Football League and RL Commercial Boards have issued a letter to both Leigh Leopards RLFC and Wigan Warriors RLFC advising them there will be an independent investigation into the conduct and actions of both clubs and the governing body in relation to matters extending over the last 12 months.

"The RFL and RL Commercial will not make any further comment until the investigation is complete."

Wigan finished top of the Super League regular season table, while Leigh finished fifth.

Sports.title: Menzies reveals heart attack scare before Matchplay incident
Sports.content:
Players Championship 29 winner Cameron Menzies has revealed he feared he was suffering a heart attack on a flight to Switzerland, prompting him to take a serious look at his lifestyle.

Menzies saw off Gian van Veen 8-4 in the final to claim his second ProTour title of 2026 on Tuesday.

Menzies continued his sparkling Players Championship form to claim a fourth PDC ranking title at Maassport Den Bosch, after an impressive string of seven straight wins.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Cameron Menzies withdrew from the World Matchplay of Darts after becoming unwell during his second-round match against Ross Smith

After capturing his second title of the year, the Scot, reflected on his medical episode in Blackpool when he was forced to withdraw from the tournament after being taken ill during his second-round match against Ross Smith.

"Even before [the incident] happened, as you can see I've lost a bit of weight. Last year I was heading to Switzerland and I genuinely thought I was having a heart attack on the plane," explained Menzies. "I went for scans because heart problems is something that runs in my family.

"They told me I needed to lose weight, but the thing with the Ross Smith match is that I went for tests after and they believe it was dehydration but it caused my blood pressure to go high because I was panicking. I've never had that before."

Menzies: We're not all athletes here!

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the first-round clash between Luke Humphries and Menzies at the World Matchplay

The 37-year-old World Cup semi-finalist continued: "I went for blood tests to check for more serious issues, including my heart. I went to Glasgow Jubilee Hospital and spent 10 hours there, but everything came back fine apart from my blood pressure being a little high. I explained what happened in Blackpool and they believe it was dehydration. I hope it was, because it means I just need to look after myself a bit more.

"I'll go and have some water and electrolytes after this, but we're not all athletes here, I get that! It's long days. I've been here since 9.30 this morning. These are long days, so you have to look after yourself. I'm getting older now, so I need to look after myself.

"My breakfast today was porridge, so I've not eaten all day. I would usually go and get a pizza, but I need to try to be better.

"A lot of players go jogging or walking now. Darts is probably better than it's ever been because all these young kids are coming through and they're all fit athletes. It's not like when we grew up playing in clubs and pubs. These guys are in youth systems. They're catching up."

Menzies averaged more than 101 in his opening victory over Nick Kenny before surviving an impressive comeback from Canada's Jim Long in a last-leg decider.

After seeing off Slovenia's Benjamin Pratnemer 6-4, he then defeated top seed Wessel Nijman by the same scoreline.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of Scotland's 8-5 win over Republic of Ireland in the quarter-finals from the World Cup of Darts in Frankfurt

Menzies saw off Jeffrey de Graaf 6-3 with another stellar average to reach the semi-finals, where he overcame another Dutchman, Kevin Doets, to book his place in a third Players Championship final in his last five events.

He stormed into a 5-0 lead, denying Van Veen a dart at double during a brilliant opening burst, before the Dutchman responded with three consecutive legs.

The Scot held his nerve, however, winning three of the next four legs to seal victory and claim the £15,000 top prize in the Netherlands.

"I'm grateful to be in this position and it's not like I take it for granted or anything, but I would like to finish the year on a high. I'm in the Worlds and maybe the Grand Slam, so I'm in a very fortunate position," said Menzies.
