“The season has started well individually and as a team. England’s got unbelievable talent and players all over the pitch. I believe I am good enough to be in the England squad so hopefully I can show that.”

Sports.title: Mexican soccer banned promotion and relegation. Senators may bring it back
Sports.content:
The debate over the absence of promotion and relegation in Mexican soccer has reached the floor of the country’s Senate, where officials announced that a legislative reform to restore the system will be proposed on Tuesday.

Senator Clemente Castañeda of the Movimiento Ciudadano party put forward the proposal, backed by representatives from other party leaderships, including Ignacio Mier of the ruling Morena party.

Castañeda stated that the initiative is critical for “expressly incorporating sporting merit among the obligations that national sports associations must observe” and ensuring promotion and relegation are enshrined in Mexican law.

“When they closed off the possibility of promotion, they didn’t just change a sporting rule; they also restricted a path for players, staff, and sports projects to grow in a country that needs to open up opportunities,” Castañeda said.

The senator said that she invited the president of the Liga MX, Francisco Iturbide, and the commissioner of the Mexican football, Mikel Arriola, and they declined.

The Associated Press contacted the Mexican Federation for comment but did not receive a response.

Broken promises

Owners of Mexican top-flight teams eliminated promotion and relegation in April 2020, citing financial difficulties among second-division clubs that were exacerbated by the Covid-19 pandemic.

Under the original plan, the suspension was set for five years, with the system scheduled for reinstatement last year so that a team could earn promotion and another face relegation at the end of the most recent season in May of this year.

However, reinstatement never materialized. Starting last year, several second-division clubs began protesting to demand that authorities honor the agreement. At the time, the Mexican Football Federation stated that returning to the system was impossible because the necessary economic conditions did not yet exist.

“The whole pandemic thing was a sham; they always knew they were going to permanently shut down promotion and relegation,” said Alberto Castellanos, president of U de G Leones Negros, one of the protesting teams.

View image in fullscreen Senator Clemente Castañeda has led the introduction of legislation to reinstate promotion and relegation. Photograph: Luis Barron/Eyepix Group/LightRocket/Getty Images

High barriers and disillusioned investors

Liga MX imposed stringent requirements on second-division teams, mandating a certification process before they could aspire to play in the top tier. These rules included a venue capacity requirement of 30,000 seats – a standard not even met by all active first-division clubs.

The elimination of promotion directly affected new investors in Mexican soccer. Cancún FC was acquired in 2022 by an investment group led by figures like former Houston Astros general manager Jeff Luhnow on the premise that promotion would return.

“When we bought the team, we saw great potential – potential that often even Mexicans don’t see – but the current system fosters mediocrity; it’s very sad,” said Giovani Solazzi, the team’s president.

Facing pushback from some second-division owners, Mexican soccer authorities completely removed the promotion and relegation system from the regulations this year. Neither the Federation nor Liga MX provided an explanation for the decision.

Public outcry

The owner of Club América – one of Mexico’s most powerful clubs and arguably its most influential decision-maker – stated last month that he supports reinstating the system, provided the right conditions are met.

“I am in favor of promotion and relegation. Everyone makes comparisons, pointing out that it exists in Spain, England, or Portugal; however, those countries have very solid second divisions, whereas here, we haven’t managed to build that kind of solid second-division league,” he said.

Once promotion was officially scrapped, widespread protests broke out during second-division matches. Players responded on the pitch by standing motionless after the opening whistle or passing the ball passively without attacking.

“I arrived in Mexico on 8 June under the premise that there would be promotion – joining Morelia, a team contending for promotion – but then we were notified that it wasn’t happening,” said Spanish goalkeeper Roberto Galán. “That’s why we protested and the clubs were sanctioned, but the protests will continue because we have the right to make our voices heard.”

Fan groups have also shown up at stadiums wearing protest shirts to voice their discontent.

And last week, Mexico’s National Antitrust Commission (CNA) launched an investigation into potential monopolistic practices in the Mexican league centering on the absence of a promotion and relegation system.

Sports.title: Real Madrid call for La Liga president’s removal over his response to derby complaints
Sports.content:
Real Madrid want a new La Liga president in light of what they called “intolerable” comments from the incumbent, Javier Tebas, ⁠who said on Tuesday that claims of officiating bias against the club belonged to “another galaxy”.

After losing 2-1 to Atlético Madrid on ⁠Sunday, Real headlined the ⁠match report ​on their website, “Terrible refereeing decides the derby.”

Real were furious that Atlético’s defender Cristian Romero was not sent off for a stamp on ⁠Jude Bellingham and also complained about a challenge by Lee Kang-in on Federico Valverde.

Real’s manager, José Mourinho, aimed sharp criticism at the referee, Miguel Ángel Ortiz ⁠Arias, and those who appointed him. Mourinho said his side could win the title “if they ​let us compete on a level playing ‌field”.

He brought two printed screenshots of what he thought were red-card tackles committed by players to his post-match press conference.

Tebas responded to a pro-Real article on social media with a lengthy riposte to allegations of a “conspiracy” against the 15-time European champions.

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” said Tebas, who has often been at odds with Real Madrid and the club’s outspoken president, Florentino Pérez.

“This article goes further – it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

“Real Madrid are crucial to La Liga. But claiming that ‘La Liga is worth nothing’ without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one.”

Real responded with a statement on their website, saying: “Our club considers it intolerable that the president of La Liga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking ​Real Madrid.

“Given this inappropriate and persistent behaviour, we believe that the professional football competition in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and realising its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.“

Real sit six points behind the reigning champions and early leaders, Barcelona.

Sports.title: ‘Have some humanity’: Diogo Jota chants at Rúben Neves a wake-up call for Saudi Arabia
Sports.content:
The good thing about Cristiano Ronaldo playing in your league is that he is one of the most famous footballers ever and when he scores a great goal or reaches 1,000 (just 21 to go), many people watch. The bad thing about Cristiano Ronaldo playing in your league is that when something negative happens and he is involved, just as many people will watch and listen. Global attention is something that the big European leagues have had for years but it is something the Saudi Pro League, which has spent billions in search of achieving a similar stature, needs to get used to.

On Sunday 13 September, Ronaldo wrote to his 680 million Instagram followers to discuss the events of the night before when Al-Taawoun supporters were coming to terms with a 6-0 home thrashing by Al-Hilal, whose £150m-plus forward line, Ollie Watkins and Gabriel Martinelli, got five between them. Fair to say that some handled it better than others as what followed was in the worst possible taste.

At the end, what seemed to be a small number of fans saw Al-Hilal’s Rúben Neves in the centre circle and started chanting the name of his former Portugal and Wolves teammate Diogo Jota, who died in a car accident in July 2025who tragically died. Neves, who has a tattoo of the Liverpool star, was visibly upset and made a gesture which clearly said to those supporters that “God is watching you”. He also said to Saudi reporters after the game: “I hope they don’t go to pray afterwards.”

Ronaldo then weighed in. “The league must take action and punish this kind of fan behaviour,” he wrote. “This is no longer football, and there have to be limits. People who behave ‌like this should never be allowed to enter a stadium again.” Al-Hilal made an official complaint. This was a big story.

Ayman al-Hotami, one of Al-Hilal’s best-known fans, says: “I found the chants hard to believe but those responsible were few in number and very young. Al-Hilal’s fanbase completely condemn the chants and demanded an apology regarding the actions of individuals in their stands. We appreciate the club’s response in condemning this isolated incident, which represents neither the club nor our society.”

Away from home in small stadiums with low attendances, often the case when the big teams play outside Jeddah and Riyadh, the chants of a few can carry far. More than once, Ronaldo has heard the name of a certain Argentinian star coming his way and reacted badly. This, though, was on a completely different level.

View image in fullscreen Rúben Neves (centre) and Diogo Jota (left) played together at club and international level. Photograph: Scott Heppell/Reuters

The well-known Saudi broadcaster Waleed al-Farraj says: “To shout ‘Messi’ at Ronaldo is acceptable within the context of the rivalry between them, but to chant the name of his deceased teammate Jota at Neves is an inappropriate act. How can you play on people’s grief like this? You should have some humanity.”

The Saudi legend Sami al-Jaber, who played at four World Cups and had a short spell in England with Wolves, sent a message to Neves: “Rúben, your presence in Saudi football means a great deal to us. As Saudis, we take pride in our values of respect and hospitality … they transcend any sporting rivalry. This behaviour does not reflect those values. I hope you know how warmly you are regarded here, and how much you belong.”

Ronaldo’s call for action was met four days later. “The Saudi Arabian Football Federation (Saff) and the Saudi Pro League (SPL) condemn the unacceptable conduct by some supporters in attendance,” a statement said, adding that the chants were inconsistent with the values of Saudi football and sportsmanship in general. Al-Taawoun have been handed a ban of around £20,000 and ordered to play two matches behind closed doors. An earlier statement said that “exploiting personal tragedies for the purpose of abuse or provocation is unacceptable behaviour that has no place in Saudi football”.

View image in fullscreen Cristiano Ronaldo spoke out after fans of Al-Taawoun chanted the name of Diogo Jota to taunt Rúben Neves. Photograph: Reuters

Some felt that more could have been made of an opportunity to send a message to the rest of the league, one of zero tolerance and harsh punishments for those individuals responsible. Nobody would have complained – Al-Taawoun had condemned what happened and said it was “not representative of their supporters”. Here was a clearcut case of fans behaving badly as you are going to get.

European football has worked hard to try and stamp out offensive chants. “Stadiums in places such as Portugal and England are nowadays heavily controlled spaces,” says Simon Chadwick, professor of Afro-Eurasian Sport at Emlyon Business School in Paris. “Hence, when someone like Ronaldo encounters [verbal abuse] he will inevitably respond, thereby attracting attention from the media and others. Saudi Arabian fans need to get used to such a reaction fast.”



It is not just the international media that get involved. “Organisations such as the AFC and Fifa may even implement codes of conduct and penalties for situations like the Jota episode,” Chadwick says. “In other words, if Saudi fans and/or the Pro League can’t regulate or control the situation, then someone else will.”

With the Asian Cup coming to the country in January for the first time – and preparation for the 2034 World Cup on the way – Saudi Arabia will be hoping that such action will not be necessary.

Sports.title: Liam Rosenior told he lacks class and called ‘crazy’ by former player in astonishing tirade
Sports.content:
Liam Rosenior told he lacks class and called ‘crazy’ by former player in astonishing tirade

Liam Rosenior has been slammed by Strasbourg's former captain following his wild post-match celebrations last weekend.

Paris FC manager Rosenior celebrated in front of his old side's fans after his current team's 2-1 win in Ligue 1 on Saturday.



2 Rosenior sparked a brawl after holding nothing back when celebrating in front of his former club's fans Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

A brawl broke out as Strasbourg's players rushed over to confront the Englishman as he aggressively waved his arms and shouted.

But he refused to apologise for his actions, citing insulting chants about his family from some of the supporters as the reason he goaded them.

However, ex-captain Dimitri Lienard has now launched a tirade on the club's old manager following the incident.



'Have a little more class'

Speaking on the Club Racing show on YouTube, Lienard, who played over 300 games for Strasbourg, said: "Of course I don't condone insults that target family, it's happened to me too.

"But well, if coaches start doing that too, acting like show-offs or going to the stands..."



He added: "He forgot that in his last five matches, and I'm not talking about the European Cup matches... he had three defeats and two draws with Strasbourg before he left. His last victory dates back to November 9, 2025 against Lille."

Lienard then continued his rant against Rosenior, criticising him for leaving Strasbourg for Chelsea in the middle of the season.



The 42-year-old left the French outfit to replace Enzo Maresca as Blues boss in January, also recalling loanee Mamadou Sarr from his old side to join his squad in the Premier League.

"He talks to us about the Champions League. 'If I win it', 'Be happy if I win the Champions League', 'Be proud for me'," Lienard recalled. "But are you kidding me?!

"You go to Chelsea in the middle of the season, you take a defender who's the rock for us [Mamadou Sarr] to play him for one match, 90 minutes. You're joking, right?!

2 Rosenior's Paris FC are third in Ligue 1, two points off leaders Monaco Credit: AFP



"And then you come and give us a moral lecture? It's ludicrous, it's ludicrous. Frankly, I was seriously disappointed because I wasn't expecting that.

"I don't condone him being insulted either, but be a little more humble, have a little more class."

What else did Lienard say on Rosenior?

Rosenior explained that despite his decision to hit back at the Strasbourg fans he will always respect the 'wonderful' club.

But Lienard wasn't having any of that, slamming him once again for leaving the club mid-season and causing chaos on his return to face them with Paris FC last Saturday.



He said: "It wasn't 'thank you, you're welcome', it was 'goodbye'. Not a thank you to the people of Strasbourg.

"What did he think? That we were going to erect a statue in his honour? That we were going to roll out the red carpet for this gentleman? What did he think? That we were going to open a bottle of champagne for him?

"But you are crazy my friend! You are crazy my friend!

"I think he had forgotten the club's values ​​too: humility, respect, hard work."

Sports.title: Real Madrid go to war with LaLiga as they make damning ‘dishonest’ claim
Sports.content:
Real Madrid go to war with LaLiga as they make damning ‘dishonest’ claim

Real Madrid have published an explosive statement aimed at LaLiga president Javier Tebas following comments on social media.

Tebas was critical of the 36-time LaLiga champions following Sunday’s 2-1 defeat at city rivals Atletico.

4 Jude Bellingham was the recipient of a heavy challenge form Cristian Romero that angered boss Jose Mourinho Credit: Getty

4 There were other incidents that left Real Madrid incensed too Credit: Getty

Real Madrid released a statement after the match titled ‘A dreadful refereeing performance decides the derby’, criticising the referee Miguel Angel Ortiz’s decision not to send off both Kang-in Lee and Cristian Romero for robust challenges on Federico Valverde and Jude Bellingham respectively.

Boss Jose Mourinho later produced a picture of Lee's challenge on Valverde while slamming the decision not to dismiss the South Korean.

But Tebas further angered Real Madrid on Tuesday when he responded to an article on social media claiming there was a 'conspiracy' against the club.

What did Tebas say about Real Madrid?

“Here they go again, the mouthpieces and the regime’s television, building the same old narrative – the permanent conspiracy,” Tebas said.

“This article goes further – it claims that referees harm ‘the business that feeds them’. What exactly is it asking for? Refereeing based on revenue, viewership, or the badge? What a way to understand equality in the competition.

“Real Madrid are crucial to LaLiga. But claiming that ‘LaLiga is worth nothing’ without them reveals the disdain for the other clubs, their fans, and their history. The competition belongs to no one.”

The 15-time European champions responded to the statement on their website on Tuesday evening describing Tebas’ comments as ‘intolerable’.

The statement read: “In response to the statements made by the president of LaLiga, Javier Tebas Medrano, Real Madrid C. F. wishes to state the following.

“Our club considers it intolerable that the president of LaLiga uses his institutional position to continue discrediting and attacking Real Madrid in the manner he does in each of his public interventions.

“It is also very concerning that someone who is responsible for representing and protecting the interests of all LaLiga clubs is repeatedly obsessed with targeting Real Madrid, turning our club into a constant subject of his public attacks.

4 Mourinho came well equipped to his post-match press conference Credit: Getty

“His latest remarks are particularly serious and incomprehensible, unbecoming of a responsible manager, as they are made in response to an article by an independent journalist in a digital media outlet.

“However, he reacts against our club and goes as far as to comment on our sporting strategy, which is entirely inappropriate and irresponsible.

“It is utterly surprising that the president of LaLiga dedicates his time and personal platforms to constantly trying to publicly discredit Real Madrid, instead of contributing, from the responsibility of his position, to fostering trust in the institutions that must ensure the impartiality of the competition.

“By doing so, he continues to damage the image of our competition and Spanish football worldwide.”

Real Madrid call for new leadership

Los Blancos then called upon senior figures to consider replacing Tebas, claiming the league needs a leader who shows impartiality across the league’s 20 teams.

“Given this inappropriate behavior, which has persisted over time, we believe that professional football in Spain urgently needs a leader capable of managing it and developing its full potential with the fundamental duty of neutrality.

4 Tebas has been LaLiga president since 2013

“It needs someone who understands the nature of their role, as the president of LaLiga is not the owner of the competition but a manager serving the clubs that comprise it and entrust him with its direction. The clubs need someone who serves this mission with honesty.”

Real Madrid have made a mixed start to the LaLiga season having picked up 15 points from their opening seven matches.

Mourinho’s side sit in fourth place, six points adrift of pace setters Barcelona and are also behind Atletico and Real Betis.

Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne reveals the one thing that ‘drives him nuts’ about England players
Sports.content:
Paul Gascoigne reveals the one thing that ‘drives him nuts’ about England players

Paul Gascoigne has expressed his deep frustration at the lack of emotion shown by modern England players.

Gascoigne, who played 57 times for the Three Lions revealed the pride he felt every time he wore the national shirt.

3 Will Thomas Tuchel include showing more emotion in his pep talk during the international break? Credit: Getty

The debate about players' commitment to England has been brought to widespread attention after a number of players withdrew from the squad.

Five high-profile players pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia, and Croatia.

Cole Palmer is one of several players who have left the squad, with Declan Rice, Tino Livramento, Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford all returning to the parent sides 'due to respective injury issues'.

However, four of those players had started for their clubs in the Premier League over the weekend and did not appear to leave the pitch injured.

Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have since been drafted into the England squad for the upcoming Nations League clashes.

Speaking on talkSPORT Breakfast, Gazza highlighted his dismay at what he perceives as a lack of patriotism and pride among the current generation.

He said: "I mean, I loved playing for my country. You know, putting on that white shirt, I just thought of my family, made them proud, you know.

"It's quite emotional now talking about it. Playing for your country means so much.

"I see some of the players when they score and they don't really celebrate. And that drives me nuts. You know, I remember when I made my debut for the Under-21s and it was a tournament tour...

"I scored and there was no one in the crowd. So I jumped over the fence and celebrated on the motorway. Yeah, I was on the motorway again.

3 Gascoigne is regarded as one of English football's best ever talents Credit: GETTY

"You see some of them and they pull out the squad. It's not very good.

"But the thing is with Bobby Robson, it didn’t matter how bad you played for your club, if you played well for England, he would pick you again. So you knew that, but when you keep chopping and changing, some players get fed up with it."

Palmer out

Many pundits have specifically been critical of Palmer, who was reinstated into Tuchel's squad with the Chelsea man suffering a 2026 World Cup snub.

The 24-year-old had the entire summer break after his omission to recover from a lingering groin injury and critics have pointed out that the midfielder has only played five games in the Premier League so far this season.

Gascoigne, considered one of England's greatest ever players, was called up to the England under-21 side in the summer of 1987 and scored with a free-kick in his debut in a 2–0 win over Morocco.

Following his performance, he was then called up to the senior squad by Bobby Robson for a friendly against Denmark in September 1988 and came late in the game for Peter Beardsley in a 1–0 win.

Teammate Bryan Robson referred to the midfielder as 'challenging Maradona as the best player in the world' at the 1990 World Cup.

3 Gazza demanded more emotion from the current crop of England players on talkSPORT Breakfast on Tuesday Credit: talkSPORT

Graham Taylor replaced Robson as the England boss and switched Gascoigne in favour of 32-year-old Gordon Cowans.

However, once Gascoigne returned to peak fitness, he immediately reclaimed his spot for a crucial World Cup qualifier against Norway.

He remained an integral figure for England across successive managerial reigns, including under Glenn Hoddle.

However, prior to the 1998 World Cup squad selection the midfielder was pictured on a night out, prompting Hoddle not to pick him in the final squad.

After hearing the news, Gascoigne wrecked Hoddle's room in a rage. He would never play for England again.

Sports.title: Premier League rival offers Dejan Kulusevski return update
Sports.content:
Dejan Kulusevski's international teammate and Premier League rival Yasin Ayari has given the latest on his injury recovery.

Kulusevski is now nearing 500 days out of action after suffering a knee injury in May 2025 that has seen him sidelined.

3 Kulusevski has not played a game since May 2025 amid a long, gruelling recovery, but he is now getting closer to a return to action Credit: Getty

The Tottenham midfielder has been through multiple setbacks, missing an entire season and a World Cup with Sweden.

But Brighton's Ayari has lauded his good friend and teammate for his mental strength during his 'not normal' recovery period.

Kulusevski finally returned to Spurs training earlier this month and has been back alongside his teammates this week.

It marked an incredible feat to work his way back and it seems that he is closing in on long-awaited return to action.

When could Kulusevski return?

Speaking to Swedish outlet Fotbollskanalen, Ayari admitted he didn't know any specifics but that he is making progress.

Ayari said: “He has started training and is making progress. I’m happy for him, that he can come back and do what he loves.

"I just hope things will go well when he’s 100 per cent."

"I don’t know [when he will be back]. I don’t see him every day,” he added. "We’ve all missed him in the national team. Hopefully soon.

"It’s hard for me to say [if he’ll be match fit soon]. I don’t see him every day, I only talk to him. I hope soon.

"He’s back on the training pitch, so step by step we hope he’ll be back. When he’s back, he’ll be 100 per cent.”

3 Kulusevski is back in Spurs training and is nearing a comeback, with Ayari positive when giving the latest on his Sweden teammate Credit: Getty

Sweden manager Graham Potter opted not to select Kulusevski in his squad for the three-week international break.

Potter was keen for him to reintegrate at Tottenham first before considering bringing him back to the national set-up.

Ayari hails 'incredible' Kulusevski

Ayari also discussed his envy for Kulusevski's mentality after going through such a long period away from football.

“He has always been fit and taken care of his body," the 22-year-old said. "It’s mostly mental, seeing how mentally strong he has been during this process.

“That he has managed to have a smile on his face even when it has taken so long. There have always been setbacks, but he always wakes up happy."

“It’s incredible how strong he has been during this journey," he added. "There aren’t many people who can wake up and keep fighting when they’ve been through so much.

3 Ayari has hailed Kulusevski for his mental strength throughout his time on the sidelines Credit: Getty

“He keeps fighting and is happy at the same time. When it comes to that, it’s not normal.

"He’s very strong mentally. I learn a lot from it.”

Sports.title: Roy Keane refuses to apologise to Andy Robertson over iconic ‘big baby’ jibe
Sports.content:
Roy Keane has refused to apologise to Andy Robertson for calling him a ‘big baby’ following an altercation with an assistant referee.

Whilst at Liverpool in 2023, Robertson claimed he had been elbowed in the throat by linesman Constantine Hatzidakis during a 2-2 draw with Arsenal.

3 Robertson brought his nine-year stint at Liverpool to an end in the summer Credit: Getty

The Scotland left-back was incensed after Hatzidakis appeared to swing at him on his way off the pitch for the half-time interval.

But in the Sky Sports studio, pundit Keane had little sympathy for Robertson and told him to get on with the game.

"He should be more worried about his defending," said the Manchester United legend on television at half time.

"Do you know what he is? That Robertson, I’ve watched him a number of times. He’s a big baby. That’s what that guy is.

"Just get on with the game and concentrate on your defending. He does grab the linesman first."

Unimpressed, Keane went on to repeat the word 'baby' in a hilarious reaction which had Jamie Carragher, Gary Neville, Micah Richards and host Dave Jones in stitches - and it's regularly found online to this day.

Keane meets Robertson

Now, more than three years later, Robertson and Keane came face-to-face and revisited the notorious incident.

The former Liverpool defender, who currently plays for Tottenham, was a guest on the latest episode of The Overlap alongside Keane, Ian Wright, Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher and Jill Scott.

After the incident was brought up on the podcast, Robertson admitted the incident had been 'something over nothing', before Keane shared the reason behind his frosty reaction.

Keane remarked: "Players have to remember, and this is not an apology, when in the studio, we can have long days can't we?

3 Robertson had claimed to have been elbowed by linesman Hatzidakis in the 2023 incident

3 Keane was typically honest as he doubled down on his 2023 comments Credit: X @WeAreTheOverlap

"It can be a bit flat, sometimes a player can do something and you're agitated by having a long day."

Responding to Keane, Robertson jokingly quipped: "The first two 'babies' were alright, the third was one too far."

This left all pundits amused, before Keane responded in light-hearted fashion by insisting he felt under pressure to react strongly on air.

He said: "In my defence, when I said it - we get agitated with traffic all the way to game, but then none of them [his fellow pundits] are saying anything.

"I'm looking at them going: 'You've got to say something', that's why I put the last 'baby' in.

"They're all staring at me like, 'f****** say something'. Am I right?"

Robertson then finished by jokingly taking aim at Carragher, who had laughed at Keane during the original incident.

"I wasn't happy with you [Carragher] laughing either by the way," the Scotland captain said.

Ultimately, linesman Hatzidakis faced no punishment from the PGMOL for the incident, but then went almost two years before assisting another Liverpool game up in January 2025.

Robertson, meanwhile, left the Reds in the summer after nine years at Anfield and has since joined Spurs on a free transfer.

His start to life in north London has been far from easy though, with Roberto De Zerbi's side without a win from their first five Premier League matches this season and bottom of the table.

Sports.title: ‘Don’t know if I can continue’ – Ex-Premier League manager could quit months after taking job
Sports.content:
‘Don’t know if I can continue’ – Ex-Premier League manager could quit months after taking job

Ex-Fulham boss Marco Silva has hinted that he could walk away from Benfica just three months after taking charge.

The Portuguese tactician, who spent seven years managing in England, admitted he is struggling to get to grips with football back in his homeland.

3 Silva was left furious by the officiating in Sunday's Portuguese 'Classico' Credit: AFP

Silva’s frustrations boiled over following his side’s 3-1 defeat to reigning Portuguese champions Porto on Sunday.

The 49-year-old was furious at the refereeing in the match at the Estadio do Dragao, particularly after Benfica defender Clement Lenglet was dismissed ten minutes before the interval.

The former Fulham boss then suggested that referees in Portugal are often influenced by what clubs say before and after matches.

He went on to question how long he could put up with it, referencing that he had come from a ‘different culture’ after many years working in English football.

Portuguese outlet Record published a transcript of Silva’s comments following Sunday’s defeat that left his side five points adrift of Porto.

“I won’t comment on the sending off. If the club has something to say about the match, I think it should say it,” Silva said.

“I don’t know if I’ll be able to continue like this until the end of the season, because I come from a different culture.

“Here, unfortunately, you can influence referees before matches, after them and during the week, and sometimes it works. I’m not going to go down that route.”

Silva’s disgruntlement at referees is not exclusively reserved for Portuguese football.

He had his fair share of run-ins with officials during his time in the Premier League with one clash landing him a whopping £87,000 fine.

3 Silva was caught in a war of words with the referee in Sunday's clash Credit: Getty

It remains to be seen whether his doubts will continue throughout the season having managed just seven league games so far.

Silva is attempting to do what Jose Mourinho was unable to do and steer Benfica to a first league title since 2023.

But his suggestion that clubs created pressure for referees in the lead up to matches that he believes can affect the outcome is likely to anger prominent figures in the Portuguese game.

Former Chelsea and Tottenham boss and now Porto president Andre Villas-Boas appeared less than impressed by Silva’s words, claiming they were borne out of frustration at his side’s defeat.

“I think it was great refereeing,” Villas-Boas said.

He went on to remind reporters that even Porto had been on the receiving end of decisions that had been 'difficult to understand'. He then pointed towards the table instead.

3 Silva, who enjoyed spells in charge of Watford, Everton and Fulham, has a chequered history with match officials Credit: Getty

“The statistic I know is that Porto have 21 points and seven wins,” Villas-Boas added.

Sports.title: ‘Disgrace to my country’ – Ex-Arsenal star hopes players return early with ‘injury’ during international break
Sports.content:
Perry Groves has urged Arsenal players to fake injuries on international duty to ensure they're fully fit for Premier League fixtures.

Five high-profile players pulled out of Thomas Tuchel's England squad for the upcoming UEFA Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia, and Croatia.



3 Declan Rice is one of them despite making it past the 80-minute mark in five of the games he's played this season Credit: Getty

Declan Rice was among those who departed the camp, returning to the Emirates Stadium as he cited 'injury issues.'

However, the Three Lions international started for the Gunners in their 3-0 defeat to Brighton and did not appear to leave the pitch injured.

Everton's James Garner has been drafted in to replace Rice for the international clashes.



While critics have condemned players for opting out of representing their country, former Arsenal winger Groves insists the Gunners midfielder has made the right call.

On talkSPORT's Inside Gooners, he said: "You’d hope there’s conversations with Mikel Arteta and the international managers, and you would be telling your players if they’re going away with their international team to play the first game and then suddenly get a little back spasm.



"Seriously, I might be a disgrace to my country for saying it but I’m not bothered. I’ve said before that I want England to do well, but it’s not going to change my life whereas Arsenal winning does.

"Let's be honest, every Arsenal fan will be glued to their phone during the break looking at different international teams and looking at who's not playing or worrying over why players are getting subbed.



"Just go away with your national team, but don’t get injured because that Leeds game is massive. All of them are massive, but because of the way we played against Brighton, a draw against Leeds and the pressure will be ramped up."

Rice fitness concerns

Rice managed to avoid a red card in the closing seconds of the defeat at the Amex Stadium after losing his composure.

Seagulls winger Malick Yalcouye leaned into the England international in order to cause a reaction. Rice then chased down Yalcouye and swiped his legs from underneath him, sending him down to the ground.

3 Tuchel's long-term focus has now switched to Euro 2028, which will be played on home soil Credit: Getty



Additionally, the 27-year-old has been managing a persistent neural issue affecting his lower back and hamstring since early 2026, which restricted his overall impact for Tuchel's side during the summer World Cup.

During the tournament, there was multiple concerns for the midfielder including from Gabby Agbonlahor, who said: "He’s not 100 per cent, let’s put it that way."

Stuart Pearce responded: "Yeah, exactly, but you wouldn’t think it with his performances.

"[But] is that [continuing to play while nursing an issue] going to do him more damage and is he likely to break down? If there is a risk there, I think you’d be foolish as a manager to play him."



Arsenal defender Marli Salmon has also withdrawn from the England Under-18 squad due to injury.

The highly-rated prospect was handed his first senior outing of the season in the 4-2 win over Ipswich Town in the Carabao Cup last Tuesday.

3 Arsenal have strong expertise in developing young stars Credit: Getty

Under-18 boss Will Antwi has since called up Chelsea defender Gabriel Sambou instead, who has represented Poland and England at youth level.



The youngster should hopefully return to action for the club's Under-21 side in a Premier League 2 fixture against Sunderland, unless Mikel Arteta includes him in the squad for the Premier League meeting with Leeds on the same day.

Sports.title: Kylian Mbappe reveals just how close he came to Liverpool transfer in bombshell revelation
Sports.content:
Kylian Mbappe reveals just how close he came to Liverpool transfer in bombshell revelation

Kylian Mbappe has confirmed he defied his mum's wishes to sign for Jurgen Klopp's Liverpool in 2017.

The France captain burst onto the scene with AS Monaco as a 16-year-old in 2015, with Europe’s big hitters already circling for his signature.



5 Mbappe showed huge promise at formative club Monaco, earning himself a big-money move to Paris Saint-Germain Credit: Getty

Two-years later, Liverpool were poised to lure the starlet to Anfield but faced competition from Real Madrid and Mbappe’s hometown club Paris Saint-Germain.

If the decision had been down to his mum and agent Fayza Lamari, then Mbappe would have been lacing up his boots for the Reds.

But Mbappe had other ideas despite having held a meeting with Klopp on board a private jet over the south of France in 2017.



The plane took off from Blackpool before landing in Nice where Klopp met with Mbappe and his mother.

Klopp then spent several hours mid-air trying to persuade Mbappe to sign for Liverpool rather than a move back to home city Paris.



Inside Mbappe's Liverpool snub

“It was while I was playing in Monaco, I had to take a decision. And yes, I was close to Liverpool,” Mbappe recalled in an interview with The Athletic.

“My mum was a big fan of Jurgen Klopp and the favourite destination for my mum was Liverpool. She wanted me to go there.



“I didn’t listen because I wanted to play in my city, Paris. I didn’t want to leave my country before I was someone.

“But yes, my mum was always saying ‘Liverpool – you’re going to be there, playing at Anfield, it’s going to be insane for you.’ I was like, ‘OK!’

“She went there (for) the first step of the negotiations. She went to the city, she went to the stadium, she met the people. She was like, ‘It’s a wonderful club, everybody’s so kind, it’s a family club, a big club.’

5 Klopp and maintained a strong relationship with Mbappe throughout the years Credit: getty



5 Mbappe's mum has served as his agent throughout his career Credit: X:@mbappecentral

“She went to Anfield and fell in love with it. She watched a few games alone, to feel the atmosphere, because she wanted to imagine me in this stadium.

“All the time we were talking. ‘What do you think, Mum?’. She’d say, ‘For me, you have to go to Liverpool. I said, ‘OK, OK, OK!’ because Jurgen Klopp was an amazing manager. I met him and had a wonderful relationship with him. I had big respect for him.”

Mbappe, famously spearheaded Monaco's Ligue 1 title charge in the 2016/17 season, pipping his future club in the process.



And it was then and at the age of just 18 when Mbappe fired in 15 goals in 29 Ligue 1 matches and a further six goals in Monaco’s run to the Champions League semi-finals.

That was enough for big-spending PSG to agree an initial loan deal leading to a whopping £166million transfer for the talented forward who grew up in the Parisian Suburb of Bondy.

Despite completing his move to the Parc des Princes, links with Liverpool continued.

5 Mbappe scored 256 time for PSG to overtake Edinson Cavani as the club's all-time leading scorer Credit: Getty



Mbappe, who was nearing the end of his PSG deal in 2022, was again touted as a possible arrival at Anfield.

He later snubbed both Liverpool and Real Madrid to sign a money-spinning contract extension at PSG but later conceded that he was closer to signing for the Reds in 2017 than he was this time round.

Is the door still open for Mbappe and Liverpool?

According to French football expert Julien Laurens, a future stint at Anfield is not entirely out of the question.

"He's 27 going on 28. He will be 28 in December. I think I can see him staying there [Real Madrid] for a long time but then I don't think it's impossible to see him [leave] at some point," Laurens told talkSPORT in May.



"We know that Liverpool is the club that his mum loves. They were the team and the club that they watched the most and they were really loving.

"It's funny because all those of English teams tried to sign him when he was 12, 14, 15, 17. Some went all the way to Nice and parked the private jet at the airport just waiting in case he was not staying in Monaco and decided to leave.

5 Mbappe has picked up a host of goalscoring awards at Real Madrid Credit: Getty

"They were all there ready to make him an offer. So, maybe one day, I think he would be great in the Premier League.



"I think he's got the game for it and he watches it all."

Breaking records in La Liga

Mbappe completed a dream switch to Real Madrid in 2024 on a free transfer and has gone on to score a staggering 94 goals in 111 games for Los Blancos.

He is yet to lead the club to a major honour since his arrival, something he will hope to change under the tutelage of Jose Mourinho this season.

Mbappe is in the running for this year’s Ballon d’Or having finished as top scorer in the La Liga and the Champions League last season.

He also wrote himself into World Cup folklore this summer when he became the tournament’s all-time leading scorer with 22 goals.

Sports.title: Spanish clubs eye swoop for Alejandro Garnacho as ex-Man United star's Aston Villa spell unravels - with £43m attacker playing just 31 MINUTES under Unai Emery
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho is being monitored by clubs in La Liga as he struggles to make an impression during his early days at Aston Villa. The Argentine moved to Villa from Chelsea in the summer on a season’s loan deal, which will become a permanent £43million move if Garnacho hits certain targets. Chelsea describe these conditions as ‘easily achievable’. Yet Garnacho is yet to start a game for Villa and has only played 31 minutes of competitive action for Unai Emery’s team. He has been an unused substitute in each of the last two matches and may not even have made the bench for Villa’s 3-2 win at Tottenham had Brazilian winger Alysson not been ruled out with injury. At this stage there are no thoughts from any of the relevant parties about changing the conditions of the deal. Yet Daily Mail Sport understands that clubs in Spain’s top flight are watching the situation closely. Even though he is an Argentina international, Garnacho was born in Madrid and spent time in the Atletico Madrid academy before moving to Manchester United in 2020, aged 16. La Liga clubs are eyeing a move for Alejandro Garnacho, who has played just 31 minutes on loan at Aston Villa this season Garnacho was signed to play on the left. But youngster George Hemmings has made outstanding progress and is now ahead of him, as are Emi Buendia and Ibrahim Mbaye. John McGinn can operate across the attacking line and Alysson has also made considerable strides. These are still early days in the season and if Garnacho shines during Villa’s training camp in Seville during the international break, his chance may come in October and November. ‘Continue working. Work, work, train, work,' said Emery when asked about Garnacho after Villa’s win at Coventry in the Carabao Cup. 'When he can have minutes to play, try to play well. He is progressing, but we have players in front of him now. 'George Hemmings is playing fantastic. Alysson is also understanding things well and is giving us things I want. Mbaye also responded well. 'We want a competitive team and players to compete in the style we have. Garnacho is a little bit behind because of some circumstances we had in pre-season. It is time to be patient for the time he needs.’

Sports.title: Celtic chief offers full backing to under-pressure boss Martin O'Neill
Sports.content:
Celtic chief executive Michael Nicholson insists the club remain fully supportive of Martin O'Neill despite the veteran manager being under mounting pressure.

O'Neill stated after the 1-0 defeat to Rangers at Parkhead last Sunday that he would take time to consider his future during the international break and whether it might be time to 'wrap it up'.

The 74-year-old, who agreed a one-year deal back in the summer to remain at the helm, has presided over three damaging defeats to Rangers and Ferencvaros over the past week.

Although Celtic do still remain top of the league by two points, a large section of the support had called for a change to be made in recent days.

But, as Celtic released their latest annual accounts showing a post-tax loss of £4.8million as well as cash reserves of £66.4m, Nicholson was adamant the club remain fully behind O'Neill.

'We were delighted to end season 2025/26 on a high, winning the Scottish Premiership on the final day of the season and adding the Scottish Cup and Women's Scottish Cup in the weeks following,' said Nicholson.

Martin O'Neill says he's considering his future as Celtic boss after three defeats on the bounce

Celtic chief Michael Nicholson has offered his support to the under-fire manager

'But last season was a challenging one for the club, both on and off the pitch. Following a period of stability, which has borne fruit in terms of success and growth over recent years, we experienced turmoil which affected the club's performance.

'We will address and learn from the challenges faced and mistakes made.

'The final weeks of the Premiership season; the final match at Celtic Park; the Scottish Cup final; these will live long in the memory for Celtic fans, whose support was a decisive factor.

'I thank Callum McGregor and all of the players and staff for their hard work and determination throughout the season that made the success possible.

'As the Chairman has noted, the environment was unstable, following Brendan Rodgers' resignation and our decision to move on from Wilfried Nancy.

'We owe a debt of gratitude to Martin O'Neill and his management team, who stepped up for Celtic, twice, and who guided the team to success.

'We were therefore delighted that Martin agreed to lead the Club again this season and we have worked with Martin and his team over the summer transfer window to invest in the squad.

'Having started well in the Premiership this season, we experienced disappointment in the UEFA Champions League play-off.

'Reaching the league phase of the Champions League is an objective for us all, and we are sorry not to have achieved it.

'On top of that, the losses in the last week have been painful for us all. We will now come together and support Martin and the players, as we focus our efforts on achieving success domestically and in the Europa League.'

In his own address to supporters, Celtic chairman Brian Wilson claimed that the disastrous appointment of Nancy last season could have worked had it not happened mid-season.

Nancy lasted only a month in the job after presiding over a shambolic run of form and eventually left as statistically the worst – and shortest-serving – manager in the club's history.

The Celtic hierarchy at full-time in Sunday's 1-0 home defeat to Old Firm rivals Rangers

'The events of the past 12 months have been dramatic, sometimes joyful and at other points deeply frustrating,' said Wilson.

'The departure of Brendan Rodgers was an unanticipated event which initiated a period of instability.

'In other circumstances, the appointment of Wilfried Nancy might have worked but his arrival in mid-season and the changes which followed clearly did not.

'Parting ways with Wilfried was hugely disappointing but decisive action had to be taken.

'The return of the great Martin O'Neill, supported by his backroom team as well as a fine squad of players, then proved to be a triumphant success.

'The early stages of the 2026/27 season have brought mixed fortunes.

'Our league campaign started strongly and the first leg tie in the Champions League qualifier gave cause for optimism.

'The second leg defeat to LASK was, accordingly, all the more deeply disappointing for every supporter of the Club.

'This has been followed by our exit from the League Cup. We now move into the Europa League as well as pursuing our defence of the Scottish Premiership and Scottish Cup, with renewed commitment to success.'

In terms of their annual accounts for the year ending June 30, 2026, Celtic's revenue decreased by 22.7 per cent to £111.0million (2025: £143.6million).

Operating expenses including labour increased by 4.3 per cent to £122.1million (2025: £117.1million).

Gain on sale of player registrations of £16.0million (2025: £31.5million). Acquisition of player registrations of £15.6million (2025: £38.6million)

Loss before tax of £6.6million (2025: profit of £45.7million). Loss after tax of £4.8million (2025: profit of £33.9million).Year-end cash of £66.4million (2025: £77.3million).

Sports.title: Alan Shearer accuses Tottenham of overspending on £330m summer makeover and claims splurging an 'absolute fortune' has only piled on pressure - as he questions the 'ability' of Sandro Tonali, Savio and Co
Sports.content:
Alan Shearer has accused Tottenham of overspending as their £330million summer splurge has left them bottom of the Premier League.

Spurs splashed huge money on Sandro Tonali (£100m), Mateus Fernandes (£85m), Savio (£85m), Jan Paul van Hecke (£52m), and Tosin Adarabioyo (£7m) but have picked up just two points in five games.

Shearer has questioned the 'ability' of Tottenham's new signings, with pressure mounting on Roberto De Zerbi to get a tune out of them.

He told Betfair: 'I guess De Zerbi went into this summer with a list of players that he wanted and they have spent a fortune perhaps on all those players.

'I'm not sure the fees warrant the ability, but no one would have expected them to be bottom of the league.'

He added: 'I've said many times, that they brought the players in this summer, but they spent an absolute fortune on them. On everyone, I think.

Alan Shearer has accused Tottenham over overspending and questioned the 'ability' of their signings

The club have endured a nightmare start to the season under Roberto De Zerbi and are bottom of the Premier League

'Van Hecke was a lot of money, Tonali was incredible money, Savio, and Marmoush (on loan) are others as well. It is a long, long three weeks for Tottenham and they simply have to start winning football games when they are back from the international break.

'All the bigger questions will start to be asked, if not already, if they don’t start winning football games very, very soon.

'I still think they'll have enough to stay up. They'll use the Aston Villa situation and what happened to them at the start of last season when I don't think they won in their first five games and they then managed to climb the league and qualify for Europe again.

'They will look at that and think there's still loads of football to be played, which there is, but there's a massive amount of work to be done at Spurs.

'I had them to finish in the top six this season and I am not sure that that will happen now.'

Tottenham did manage to register their first Premier League goals of the season late on in the 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa.

But that was only late on, when the game was lost and many of the fans had already left the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

De Zerbi tore into his men after an abysmal performance in that defeat, saying: 'I am very disappointed, sad and frustrated with the performance.

Spurs spent £329million over the summer, including £85m on Savio from Manchester City

New man Jan Paul van Hecke was at fault for one of Aston Villa's goals over the weekend - but did score later

'We can’t lose the game in this way, we can’t concede the second goal (a simple ball over the top), we can’t lose balance just because we are losing.

'I spoke with our four attackers in minute 51, I asked them to use their head, all second half I was telling people to be calm. But the second goal was incredible.'

Van Hecke fluffed his lines when Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki punted it long, allowing Nicolas Jackson to race through for the opposition's second goal.

De Zerbi added: 'We knew this season Aston Villa are playing 86 per cent more long balls than last season and we spoke in many meetings about it. Now we have to explain another game like (Newcastle) where we played the first half well, got to 60 minutes OK, and then we lose.'

The only match Spurs have won this campaign was a 5-1 thrashing of Championship side Charlton in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

This is the first time they have been bottom of the Premier League since January 2009.

They are second-bottom of the league goalscoring charts, just one goal ahead of Coventry, but have had the ninth-most shots, suggesting that finishing is an issue.

Steven Gerrard pointed to their striking issues on TNT Sports, saying: 'I think Spurs have improved in certain areas, but they've not got a poacher.

'They've not got a goalscorer. They've got some exciting players in the front line, but who is going to get you 20 goals?'

Their only natural striker is Dominic Solanke - with Richarlison exiled - and he has scored 12 goals across two full Premier League seasons with Spurs.

In the summer they sold young English striker Will Lankshear to Middlesbrough for £10m, potentially rising to £20m, and he has scored eight goals in 10 games there.

Tottenham will be looking to make amends quickly after the international break, with their first fixture back coming at Manchester United on October 10.

Sports.title: Andy Robertson claims Tottenham stars are 'guilty of carrying the weight of last season' as relegation alarm bells are sounded again after disastrous start to new Premier League campaign
Sports.content:
Andy Robertson claims Tottenham stars are 'guilty of carrying the weight of last season' as relegation alarm bells are sounded again after disastrous start to new Premier League campaign

Andy Robertson admits Tottenham are still burdened by two years of dismal Premier League form and the repercussions of last season's relegation scare.

After successive 17th place finishes, Spurs are rock bottom at the international break and winless with only two points and two goals from five games.

The bright new dawn anticipated after improvement under Roberto De Zerbi at the end of last season and nearly £400million spent in the summer transfer market has yet to materialise.

'They've had a couple of really tough seasons in terms of finishes in the league,' Robertson, 32, told the Stick to Football podcast on Disney+. 'They've had to go into the market in terms of they've spent a bit of money, but I do believe Tottenham are now starting a journey.

'I don't know how far that journey can go, nobody does, but the determination in that group is, like, you can see last season hurt them a lot. And maybe we're still guilty of carrying that weight of last season on our shoulders.'

Scotland captain Robertson, signed on a free from Liverpool, is one of ten signings, all with some Premier League experience to strengthen resolve and maturity inside the dressing room, but the impact on results has been negligible.

Andy Robertson admits Tottenham are still burdened by two years of dismal Premier League form

The bright new dawn anticipated after improvement under Roberto De Zerbi has yet to materialise

After successive 17th place finishes, Spurs are rock bottom at the international break

Spurs are performing worse than last season under De Zerbi when they took 11 points from seven games.

'We need to forget,' said Robertson, and he referred to the impact of the first goal conceded in a 2-0 defeat at home against Newcastle on the mood inside the stadium.

'We need to now try and get Tottenham back to where we believe they belong. And the fans are still carrying it as well, and you don't blame them. They've been through such a tough time.'

He insists there have been signs of progress for Roberto De Zerbi despite collecting only two points from a possible 15 and crashing out of the Carabao Cup against his former club at Anfield.

'We need the first win, and once we get the first win, I think we'll be really good this season,' he added.

Spurs tried to sign Robertson in January but he was not ready to leave Anfield in mid-season.

'I didn't want to leave but Tottenham came in for me,' he said. 'They were bang in trouble at that point. It was never in my plan to leave in January. I had six months left and I had the World Cup.

'But in January time, it started becoming real that I was going to leave, and that's when I came to peace with it, really.

'It was always Tottenham - as long as they stayed up! At that point, I didn't quite want to go to the Championship. So that was the thing, I ended up then getting invested in Tottenham, watching them and especially when De Zerbi came in, I was fully confident.

'They showed their interest first, and they really wanted me, and I was happy with how much they wanted me.'

De Zerbi helped to sell the Spurs vision to Robertson.

'We had a couple of video calls over the summer,' said the Scot. 'He's super ambitious. He wants to be able to win trophies, he wants to be competing and things like that, and he knows it will take time, but he also knows that we need to start showing it sooner rather than later.

'He believes in the squad. And I believe in the squad. Even looking at the team we played against Liverpool in the cup… you've got so much quality, and so many good players, it's just we all need to show it as one, instead of maybe a bit of individual quality.

'We just need a little bit of luck, and we need a little bit more of forgetting about the past and how we need to move forward. I do think as the season goes on, we'll get better.'

Sports.title: Andros Townsend claims his bizarre diet including olive oil, raw cacao and chicken feet slow cooked for eight hours prevented him needing ANY medication after he was run over by a pitch rolling machine
Sports.content:
Andros Townsend claims his bizarre diet including olive oil, raw cacao and chicken feet slow cooked for eight hours prevented him needing ANY medication after he was run over by a pitch rolling machine

Andros Townsend has claimed he shunned medicine during his recovery from being run over - because his bizarre diet was remedy enough.

The former England international has described how he couldn't walk out of sheer 'agony' after almost being crushed by a pitch roller at half-time during a match in Thailand.

But over the next day, Townsend relied on his diet - which includes slow-cooked chicken feet, olive oil, and raw cacao - to repair his body.

'The next 24 hours were all about giving my body everything it needed to recover, while avoiding simply masking the pain through medication,' the 35-year-old wrote on TikTok.

'Food is medicine.'

Townsend regularly shares his culinary masterpieces - typically presented with his tee-shirt off - in a bid to encourage his viewers to eat 'real food'.

🚨Andros Townsend got lucky to avoid injury during warmups in the Thai League pic.twitter.com/ctEOycMZcF — Polymarket Sports (@PolymarketSport) September 19, 2026

Andros Townsend says his diet acted as his medicine after he was run over by a pitch roller

Townsend was bizarrely run over while warming up for a game at this new club in Thailand

On this occasion, his recovery food consisted of six eggs, blueberries, extra virgin olive oil, raw cacao, smoked wild-caught salmon, raw cheese, an orange, tomatoes, eight-hour slow-cooked chicken feet in soup - a 'favourite', and kiwi.

The combination appears to have worked, as Townsend shared a clip of him walking unsupported - something he was unable to do in the hours after the accident, though he had initially played on without feeling much.

He told Track Radio: 'I heard my team-mates screaming, and then before I could react, I felt the pressure of that roller going over me.

'It's amazing how I've gone from not missing a game through injury and almost getting killed by a pitch roller to walking away unscathed.

'I think diet is so, so important.

'I didn't really feel anything that initial few minutes. It was only after the game, I was on the bus, and it all hit me pretty quickly.

'We were on a 10-hour journey home after that game.

'My knee just started to balloon and before long I couldn't walk, I was in agony, my knee was throbbing. Even to go to the toilet, players were having to assist me.

The former England winger admitted he was extremely fortunate to escape unscathed after being run over in Thailand on Saturday

'That all seems to have settled down now. Touch wood, I'm pretty unscathed.'

Footage of the incident quickly went viral on social media, but Townsend later made light of the ordeal on his Instagram story, posting: 'It turns out Stoke away wasn't so bad after all. Swipe to see why.'

He also told Piers Morgan's Football Uncensored show: 'Every time I see it, I'm cringing, I'm in disbelief. When I sent it to my kids, my kids thought it was AI. Literally, I had to explain to them, for the next ten minutes, that it was real.

'It's horrible to watch back and to see what could have been but, like I said, thankfully I was fortunate I did manage to fall onto the floor at the right time, so nothing snapped as the roller went over me. And I'm here today to laugh about and tell the story.'

Townsend joined Thai Premier League outfit PT Prachuap during the summer transfer window.

PT Prachuap - based in Prachuap Khiri Khan province, 150 miles south of Bangkok - appeared to have leaked Townsend's arrival two weeks before he joined when they asked if anyone had a three-bedroom house available for the player to live in. They are the 17th club of his career.

Townsend made 29 appearances for Kanchanaburi Power last season, scoring three goals.

He has previously played for Spurs, Newcastle, Palace and Everton, and moved to Thailand after a short spell with Turkish side Antalyaspor.

Townsend making the move comes after he worked for ITV as a co-commentator during the World Cup.

The ex-England winger went viral at the tournament for his unconventional diet - which includes eating raw steak.

He released a slew of videos promoting his all-natural diet including raw steak, sardines and boiled eggs.

Townsend claims to have been eating raw meat for four years, dating back to his time when he was in the Premier League and would have had access to industry-leading dietary advice.

Eating raw meat is a risk. There is potential for it to be contaminated with harmful bacteria, such as E. coli or Salmonella, or parasites.

There are 'safer' versions of raw meat, such as whole cuts, which restrict the chance for bacteria to get inside compared to ground meat. However, the bacteria can still exist on the surface.

Townsend says he has not had any health issues from consuming raw meat and defends his diet on the basis that he gets more nutrients.

Some nutrients, such as Vitamin B1, Vitamin B6, and Vitamin B12, can be partially degraded in cooking and so raw meat retains a higher concentration of them.

He is not the only footballer to evangelise about the virtues of raw products; Norway and Manchester City striker Erling Haaland enjoys raw milk as part of his diet, though he cooks his meat rather ferociously.

Sports.title: Paul Gascoigne reveals why he knew Tottenham 'were going to struggle'... as his old club slump to bottom of the Premier League before the international break
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham midfielder Paul Gascoigne has pinpointed the moment he knew Spurs would struggle this season.

The north London side have endured a nightmare start to their first full season under Roberto De Zerbi as they sit at the foot of the table without a win in five Premier League games.

Despite finishing 17th in back-to-back seasons, the Lilywhites – who spent over £300million on a rebuild in the summer – have hit a new low, with just two points from a possible 15, their worst-ever start to a top-flight campaign.

Spurs' struggles have been a surprise to many due to the heaps of business they did in the summer transfer window. However, Gascoigne, who played over 100 times in white, is not so shocked.

'Last season was incredible,' Gascoigne told talkSPORT. 'I went to their training ground; it was unbelievable. And straight away in my head, I thought, "They are going to struggle".

'Because everything is on a plate for them; when I played, the stuff and equipment we had. Everything is on a plate for them, but they have got to buck their ideas up.

Former Spurs midfielder Paul Gascoigne has said he expected Tottenham to struggle this season

The Lilywhites are rock bottom of the Premier League after the first five games of the campaign

Gascoigne says stars have 'everything on a plate' and don't have to fight

'The fans were fantastic when I was there, so they've got to do better this season.'

Tottenham's torrid start is already taking its toll on De Zerbi, and following the third defeat of the season against Villa, he could not hide his emotions.

He hit out at his team’s defensive ‘fragility’ and the feeble manner of Villa’s goals, especially the ‘unacceptable’ second, scored on the break by Nicolas Jackson at the start of the second half.

'I was very disappointed, very sad, very frustrated with the performance,' fumed De Zerbi. 'We can’t lose this game in this way, absolutely. We can’t concede the second goal. We can’t lose balance.

'At the beginning of the second half I spoke with the four attackers, to use their heads, be calm. It was minute 51. All the second half, be calm, play, enjoy, don’t take risks. But the goal we conceded, the second goal, was incredible.'

De Zerbi was no happier about the opener, scored by Johan Manzambi when Spurs were down to ten men because Micky van de Ven was off having treatment for a facial cut after a clash of heads with Tyrone Mings.

'I don’t want to speak about the first half when we dominated and created more chances to score,' said De Zerbi. 'My focus is on why we concede the first goal with 10 players, just for one minute in that situation.

'We can stay stronger, we can communicate more, we can defend in a compact way. I put [Rodrigo] Bentancur to centre back and Mateus Fernandes into midfield. If we have a red card, we could play for 60 minutes with 10 players, so what is the problem?'

Sports.title: Morgan Gibbs-White ditches Dubai just TWO hours into family holiday to answer England's SOS call - as fiancee Britney De Villiers shares bizarre video of him leaving
Sports.content:
Morgan Gibbs-White ditches Dubai just TWO hours into family holiday to answer England's SOS call - as fiancee Britney De Villiers shares bizarre video of him leaving

Morgan Gibbs-White had to ditch his family holiday in Dubai after just two hours to answer an emergency England call-up because his team-mates pulled out.

The Nottingham Forest star had gone away with his fiancee Britney De Villiers - with whom he has two children - after missing out on Thomas Tuchel's squad.

But Gibbs-White found himself answering an SOS call from Tuchel after five squad members withdrew from England duty.

And De Villiers shared a bizarre video to her 615,000 TikTok followers of the two lovebirds mouthing a High School Musical 2 song as Gibbs-White left the hotel room.

In the video, Gibbs-White leaves with his suitcase as he and De Villiers take it in turns to lip-sync lyrics from the song 'Gotta Go My Own Way'.

At the end, the 26-year-old winger waves goodbye and mouths the crushing climactic line: 'I've gotta leave but I'll miss you.'

View this post on Instagram

Morgan Gibbs-White has starred in a bizarre TikTok video with his fiancee Britney De Villiers after his emergency England call-up

De Villiers posted the dramatic video after Gibbs-White abandoned their family holiday in Dubai

It is a big opportunity for Gibbs-White, who was omitted from England's World Cup squad but now has the chance to prove himself against Spain, Czechia, and Croatia during the unprecedented three-week international break.

He has six England caps, all off the bench, but his last outing came in October 2025 against Wales.

The forward has made a reasonable start to the season, scoring once and setting up two goals in the Premier League.

His inclusion comes after Cole Palmer, Declan Rice, Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento all pulled out of their national service. Gibbs-White and James Garner have stepped up in their place.

Rice played the entirety of Arsenal's 3-0 defeat by Brighton on Saturday but has pulled out of the squad to manage his physical load.

Chelsea sources say Palmer has a muscular injury, while Manchester United boss Michael Carrick said Rashford had an 'issue' after their weekend draw with Fulham.

Rashford has been battling a hip issue since the World Cup and the injury needs management.

Mainoo is also struggling with an issue. The 21-year-old was in the squad at the World Cup, but did not play a single minute. However, he has played in all of United's league games this season, starting the last four.

It is a huge opportunity for Gibbs-White, who missed out on Thomas Tuchel's World Cup team

Cole Palmer is one of five players to pull out of the three-week international break

Livramento was forced to pull out of the World Cup squad with a calf injury, did not play for Newcastle United at the weekend and is yet to start a game this season.

Tuchel is scheduled to speak this Friday, when he will be able to offer his opinion on losing five players.

The German previously warned Palmer, who was left at home for the World Cup, that he had a 'point to prove' and needed 'to step up' to 'keep his shirt and justify the nomination'.

He added: 'So now it is a new competition. Some players, some positions, have more injuries. Some have less injuries. Cole has his starts that he always had but he has his numbers back - he has his assists back, he has decisive goals back - so that is why he is in the squad.'

Tuchel cited having too many attacking midfielders to include them all as the reason for Gibbs-White's initial omission.

'It makes no sense to nominate three, four, five No 10s,' Tuchel said. 'It just does not help anyone.

Sports.title: 'We lost the edge, what's the point?': Liverpool's £241m signings Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz couldn't settle because team-mates 'didn't care' after Diogo Jota's death, says Andy Robertson
Sports.content:
Former Liverpool defender Andy Robertson has admitted that Alexander Isak and Florian Wirtz struggled to settle in at Anfield last season because the squad 'didn't care about football' following the death of Diogo Jota.

Jota was tragically killed in a car accident alongside his brother Andre Silva in northern Spain in July 2025. The 28-year-old had been on his way to report to Merseyside for pre-season training.

In the same summer, Liverpool purchased both Isak and Wirtz for a combined £241million. However, both players struggled in what was a difficult season for the Reds, as they finished fifth in the Premier League.

Robertson, who is now at Tottenham following nine years at Anfield, was a close friend of Jota's and, during an episode of The Overlap, has explained how the forward's sudden death affected the settling-in period of the big-money signings.

An emotional Robertson said: 'It's difficult to describe or talk about really because what we went through, it was horrendous.

'If I'm talking about the new signings, they're coming into a club that is heartbroken. And that is where I felt so sorry for these guys because they had signed and had signed for big money and all.

Former Liverpool defender has opened up on how the death of Diogo Jota affected the Reds squad last season

The Scot said that Alexander Isak (left) and Florian Wirtz (right) struggled to settle at Anfield because of how Jota's death impacted the club

'If I'm talking about football, it took them months to settle in because we didn't care about football. That was the truth of it because we just lost one of your best mates in the changing room.'

Robertson was entering the final year of his Reds deal, having already won everything there is to win during his time at the club, when he learned that his friend and team-mate had passed away suddenly.

The Scotland international confessed that the Liverpool squad 'lost' their determination on the pitch due to the tragedy, which led to poor results, and ultimately, a trophyless season.

He continued: 'I think all footballers we all have that edge, don't we? I think when you lose that edge sometimes, then you can't perform to your best. And I think last season we lost the edge.

'When I look back on it, we lost that maybe determination a little bit, and things like that because I know at times we were going "What's the point?" Look at what Jotsy's family are going through, look at his kids.

'But yeah, we were grieving as a group. It was our mate at the end of the day. He's not a footballer to us. He was a team-mate, he was a friend, he was an everything.'

“He was our mate. He wasn’t just a footballer to us.” 😞



Andy Robertson opens up about the tragic passing of Diogo Jota and the profound impact it had on everyone at Liverpool. ❤️ pic.twitter.com/KcCuSvAwLa — The Overlap (@WeAreTheOverlap) September 22, 2026

Robertson was a very close friend of Jota during their five years together at Anfield

The Scot had gone to Jota's wedding weeks before he died before attending his funeral

Jota and his brother were on a road trip to the northern Spanish port city of Santander, in order to catch a ferry to the UK as Jota was due to return to Liverpool for his sixth pre-season on Merseyside.

Jota was driving after being advised by medical professionals not to travel by plane following lung surgery earlier in the summer.

He had married his childhood sweetheart Rute Cardoso at a church in Porto, Portugal, just 11 days before the devastating collision, which Robertson and fellow former Liverpool team-mate Caoimhin Kelleher attended.

'For us, it was incredibly difficult,' Robertson added. 'I mean, the week before he died, I was at his wedding.

'That's one of the most difficult things you will ever go through. Seeing him on the happiest day of his life then the next week you are seeing his family torn apart.'

Sports.title: Wayne Rooney makes Man Utd transfer claim on JJ Gabriel's next club decision
Sports.content:
Wayne Rooney makes Man Utd transfer claim on JJ Gabriel's next club decision

There is a lot of talk over where JJ Gabriel's future could lie after he asked to leave Manchester United

View Image JJ Gabriel has told Manchester United of his desire to leave the club. (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

Manchester United legend Wayne Rooney has claimed that a move to Spain could be on the cards for JJ Gabriel, with the youngster's exit from the club an open secret to those close to the situation. The 15-year-old has told the club that he wishes to leave.

‌



Talks have been held with Barcelona and Real Madrid over a potential move, although United could block the exit, with a tribunal then needed to sort the situation. Gabriel was expected to be part of the squad and potentially make his first-team debut for United in the Carabao Cup clash vs Brighton before the news broke.

‌



Rooney made the breakthrough as a teenager at Everton, with his son, Kai, also now playing in the United academy set-up. The former striker has suggested that a move to Spain could be the most likely option, despite the club doing everything possible to try and convince him to stay.

‌



Lewis Hall says it was a 'no-brainer' to snub Man Utd despite transfer interest READ MORE :

Speaking on Disney+'s Stick to United, Rooney said: "I think that anyone close to it knew that was coming. In fairness to Manchester United, they've done everything, they've done absolutely everything to keep him, to keep him at the club.

"I think it's been known that there's been a desire to go and play probably in Spain, I think, I might be wrong, but this is what you've heard over the years. The club have treated him probably differently to the other players because he is such a special talent.

"I know, I recognise, I understand that because I was that player at Everton and I was getting that treatment at Everton which was you're getting a bit more, your parents get given stuff, you're getting that special treatment more than the other players are getting. Which as a club you need to do to try and keep your better players.

‌



"It's just disappointing, of course, because he is such a top player and he's a lovely kid. So you never know whether it's gone too far and whether there is a chance to stay.
