Every scanner that gets overridden for cash, every police escort sold for $5,000, is a small transaction that adds up to something much larger: a generation of West African institutions being hollowed out from the inside, one bribed official at a time. Money on this scale does not stop at corrupting a customs post. It buys judges, financiers elections, and arms the same criminal networks it enriches. A region that cannot secure its own ports and highways against traffickers will find it just as hard to secure them against anything else.

JOS LEIJDEKKERS WILL eventually be caught, or he will not; that is, in the end, a matter for Dutch, Sierra Leonean and Interpol investigators. But whether West Africa produces the next Leijdekkers-scale network, and whether it takes years or weeks to unravel next time, is entirely within this region’s own hands. Liberia, Ghana, Sierra Leone and their neighbors have now each been handed unmistakable proof that their ports, their patrols and their own officials are being tested for weaknesses by organized crime on an industrial scale. The only responsible answer is to close that gap together, before the next shipment — and the next bribe — finds it first. The choice in front of West Africa’s governments is not complicated. Cooperate now, or explain later why they didn’t.

World.title: Liberia: Freeman Challenges Liberia’s US$1 Billion Revenue Story, Says US$400M Is Being “Squeezed” From Economy
World.content:
Liberia’s Economist and Politician Mr. Simeon Freeman

MONROVIA — Liberia’s historic crossing of the US$1 billion domestic revenue mark is being celebrated by the government as a major fiscal achievement.

By Edwin G. Genoway, Jr

Liberia’s economist and politician Simeon Freeman has raised fresh questions over Liberia’s revenue system, claiming that approximately US$400 million is being squeezed out of the local economy through charges that are not reflected in the government’s budgetary revenue figures.

Freeman said the amount includes payments associated with port operations, terminal charges, shipping companies, tracking fees and other costs incurred when goods enter Liberia.

While acknowledging that international trade taxes account for a significant portion of government revenue, he argued that the broader financial burden imposed on importers and consumers extends beyond what appears in the national budget.

“If you put all of that inflow together, you’re talking about US$400 million that is squeezed out of the local economy,” Freeman stated.

Freeman argues that these additional costs ultimately find their way into the prices Liberians pay for goods and services, particularly in an economy heavily dependent on imports. “By mopping money from the local economy, it makes the cost of goods very expensive,” he said, linking the alleged unbudgeted charges to rising consumer prices and declining purchasing power.

“How much money is circulating out of the pockets of Liberian consumers and businesses through charges that do not appear as direct government revenue in the national budget,” he intimated.

In a pointed economic commentary, Freeman challenged the growing celebration around government’s record revenue performance, arguing that the headline figure alone does not tell the full story of Liberia’s economic condition.

His argument is that government can increase revenue while ordinary Liberians simultaneously become poorer in real terms if the cost of raising that revenue is ultimately transferred to consumers through higher prices. “Every aspect of this budget is mopping money from the local economy,” Freeman said.

“By mopping money from the local economy, it makes the cost of goods very expensive.” The comments come days after President Joseph Nyuma Boakai announced that Liberia had raised more than US$1 billion in domestic revenue during the first nine months of 2026.

The President described the achievement as a historic milestone and said the money was mobilized through taxes, duties, fees and other lawful payments from individuals and businesses. He also said the government intends to ensure that the revenue translates into benefits that Liberians can see and feel.

But Freeman’s analysis challenges Liberians to look beyond the revenue headline.

‘The money is coming from somewhere’

Freeman’s argument rests on a basic economic principle: government revenue does not appear in isolation from the economy, he said

Taxes, duties, fees and other government charges are ultimately paid by individuals and businesses. Where businesses incur higher costs, those costs can be passed on to consumers through higher prices. That, Freeman argues, is the part of the US$1 billion story that deserves greater public scrutiny.

“The government gets the money by mopping and squeezing it from the economy,” he said “What that means is, when tuition goes up, it’s not the school that you blame.” For Freeman, the issue is therefore not whether government should collect revenue.

It is whether the country’s revenue system is increasing the productive capacity of the economy or simply extracting more money from an economy whose businesses and households are already under pressure.

Freeman focused particularly on Liberia’s import-dependent economy

He argued that the official tax figures do not necessarily capture the full range of costs associated with moving goods into Liberia.

According to his analysis, importers face customs-related taxes alongside port, terminal, shipping, tracking and other charges.

The economist contends that when those costs accumulate, they eventually become part of the price paid by consumers. “Something costs one dollar in China, very cheap. One dollar in China comes to Liberia and costs about 10, 15 dollars. Now you understand why.”

Freeman’s specific estimate that approximately US$400 million is being removed from the economy through additional charges is still subject to independent verification. But his broader economic argument is more fundamental: the price consumers pay at the end of the supply chain reflects not only the original cost of the product, but also the taxes, fees and other costs accumulated along the way.

The uncomfortable connection between revenue and prices

Freeman linked government revenue collection to the everyday economic struggles facing Liberians. He pointed to rising transportation costs, food prices, rent and education expenses as examples of the pressure households are experiencing.

“When government mop up the money, they spend it on themselves and not necessarily on us,” Freeman argued.

The IMF has reported that Liberia’s recent revenue performance has been supported by stronger income and international trade taxes, among other sources. It has also emphasized the importance of maintaining a prudent fiscal stance and improving the quality of public spending.

Freeman also turned his attention to Liberia’s debt

He argued that a significant portion of the government’s fiscal resources is already committed to servicing debt.

The FY2026 budget and subsequent fiscal planning have indeed placed substantial emphasis on debt management, while the IMF has continued to monitor Liberia’s debt position as part of its economic program.

Freeman’s concern is that Liberia could find itself in a cycle where government collects more revenue, borrows more money to finance development, and then uses an increasing amount of future revenue to service those obligations.

“You have to keep borrowing repeatedly for every major project,” Freeman said. His broader warning is that revenue growth without corresponding growth in production, investment and household incomes may not fundamentally transform the economy.

President Boakai has argued that the billion-dollar milestone must ultimately translate into tangible improvements in the lives of Liberians.

World.title: Kawambwa bar owners warned against under age patrons
World.content:
Kawambwa Town Council has issued a final warning to bar and nightclub owners against admitting persons under the age of 18 into their premises.

Council Secretary, George Biemba emphasised that allowing underage patrons into bars and nightclubs is prohibited under the Liquor Licensing Act No. 20 of 2011.

Mr Biemba noted that despite an earlier warning issued in February this year, some establishments in the district have continued to entertain minors.

“We are reminding all licensed premises that the law forbids admitting persons below 18 years, selling or supplying them with liquor, or permitting them to consume alcohol on the premises. This is a final warning and all should comply,” MrBiemba said.

Mr Biemba said bar and nightclub owners found violating the law risk facing fines, prosecution, and closure of their businesses.

He urged all operators to strictly comply with the law, stressing that the stated penalties will be enforced without further delay by the local authority.

The Council has since called on liquor-licensed premises to cooperate with the local authority and ensure that underage persons are not allowed to access or consume alcohol.

The warning by the local authority comes in the wake of a surge in the number of underage persons patronizing bars and nightclubs in the district.

World.title: ZRA calls integrity in tax administration
World.content:
The Zambia Revenue Authority (ZRA) has called for collective responsibility from stakeholders in Nakonde District in Muchinga Province in ensuring integrity in tax administration within the trading ecosystem.

Nakonde ZRA Station Manager, David Mungela, said integrity is tested when financial interests and pressure come into play.

Mr Mungela was speaking during an ethics engagement meeting with the business community held at Izukanji Lodge in Nakonde district.

The meeting was held in collaboration with the Anti-Corruption Commission.

Mr Mungela stated that ZRA has adopted an outward looking approach to its integrity agenda by engaging beyond its officers to include taxpayers and other players.

“Corruption, smuggling and fraud do not only affect ZRA, they increase the cost of doing business and undermine resources meant for national development,” he said.

Meanwhile, Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) Corruption Prevention Officer, Chindika Mtonga, said corruption disproportionately affects the vulnerable in society.

Mr Mtonga noted that while institutions such as ZRA, the Drug Enforcement Commission and Zambia Police support the Commission in fighting the vice, citizen participation remains critical.

“Citizens must join the fight against corruption because without your involvement our efforts will be in vain,” he said.

And speaking during the same meeting, Nakonde Chamber of Commerce and Industry President, Thomas Botha called for enhanced collaboration between ZRA and the ACC to curb corrupt practices.

Mr Botha further commended ZRA for simplifying the process of acquiring a Taxpayer Identification Number (TPIN).

“We need to collaborate more to reduce corrupt practices and we commend ZRA for automating the issuance of TPINs,” Mr Botha said.

World.title: Hichilema underscores the importance of diplomatic ties
World.content:
President Hakainde Hichilema says diplomacy is a critical tool in achieving the Grow Zambia Agenda, as it nurtures mutually beneficial relations for countries.

President Hichilema has underscored Zambia’s focus on growth in his second term, noting that diplomatic relationships are critical for mutually beneficial economic development.

The Head of State said this in a speech read for him by Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mulambo Haimbe at the United Nations General Assembly, in New York.

“Diplomatic relations mean new markets for our farmers, new partners for our investment drive and new friends for Zambia in the institutions that shape the global economy,’’ he stressed.

This is contained a statement issued to the media in Lusaka by First Secretary for Press at the Permanent Mission of Zambia to the UN, Namatama Njekwa, Zambia signed Joint Communiqués with Uruguay and Vanuatu.

Ms Njekwa revealed that the agreements open avenues for cooperation in agriculture, livestock, climate change adaptation, eco-tourism, trade, and investment.

She stated that Zambia also held talks with Malawi, agreeing to enhance collaboration in trade, energy, infrastructure, and connectivity, including Malawi’s interest in the Lobito Development Corridor.

Ms Njekwa further indicated that Zambia also held talks with Cuba where the two countries reaffirmed their longstanding friendship and solidarity, pledging continued cooperation in health, education, and multilateral coordination.

She added that Zambia also exchanged support with Cuba for respective candidatures to the UN Human Rights Council and other committees.

Ms Njekwa revealed that the Zambian delegates further engaged UN officials, focusing on rule of law, human rights, misinformation, and the country’s cooperation with the UN development system.

She however stated that Minister of Health, Roma Chilengi participated in the launch of the Accra Reset High-Level Panel report on reforming global health governance, which aligns with Zambia’s principle of strengthening national priorities through international cooperation.

Ms Njekwa further disclosed that Zambia will co-host the follow-up meeting on the Sevilla Commitment on Wednesday, with additional bilateral engagements on investment, energy, and infrastructure scheduled throughout the week.

The Assembly is convened under the theme “Restoring Trust, Managing Transformation: A United Nations that delivers for all.”

World.title: Masebo cautions the public against fake social media messages
World.content:
United Party for National Development (UPND) Senior Management Committee Member and Former Minister of Lands , Sylvia Masebo has urged Zambians to ignore social media messages allegedly aimed at promoting hatred and division by individuals who want to destroy the good name of the country.

Ms Masebo has cautioned the public that social media is heavily laden with falsehoods, disinformation, and manipulated content targeting the UPND members especially former cabinet Ministers.

She has noted that all online content or insinuations tagging her name are all fake, adding that she has never given an interview to any media platform, individual journalist or blogger since the August 13 , 2026 general elections.

Ms Masebo who is an entrepreneur and politician who has served in various portfolios said this during a media engagement in Lusaka today.

“All they want is to create division between the President and his former Ministers like myself and others which will never work.

Masebo has pledged deep loyalty to President Hichilema, stating that she will remain committed to the UPND regardless of electoral losses or results of her petition in court.

“President Hakainde Hichilema’s administration has stabilised Zambia’s macroeconomic environment and all the constitutional laws that have been made by this government. I was part of them so I am still in the government, I am in the senior management committee of the party;” she said.

“Zambia must remain under the leadership of President Hichilema as the country is on a stable path of economic recovery and democratic governance, the country is in safe hands under President Hichilema,” she said.

She further denied social media reports claiming that she called the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) a corrupt institution, saying that she fully respects the constitutional mandate of the commission as an independent body managing national elections.

Ms Masebo stressed that taking a petition to court is her constitutional right and not undermining the ECZ.

“I took the matter to court because I was aggrieved by how I was maligned by my competitor, how I was defamed by one competitor which is my constitutional right and I have no issues with the ECZ,” she stated.

She further revealed that attempts to divide UPND party members by enemies of the government should be ignored.

Ms Masebo stressed that following the August 2026 general elections, quite a number of parliamentary election petitions have been lodged at the high court by various losing candidates, saying that she is not the only one who has petitioned her opponent.

World.title: Govt. launches of Transformative Sustainable Food Systems programme
World.content:
Government has called for stronger coordination among sectors and institutions in addressing Zambia’s food security and nutrition challenges.

Permanent Secretary for Administration in the Office of the Vice President, Lillian Kapusana, says the challenges affecting food systems are interconnected and require a coordinated, systems-based approach rather than isolated interventions by individual institutions.

Ms Kapusana was speaking today at the official launch of the US$500,000 two year Technical Cooperation Programme, on Catalysing Transformative and Sustainable Food Systems in Zambia, supported by the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) of the United Nations.

She said the programme provides an opportunity to bring institutions together around a common food systems agenda and shared results, saying the initiative would also support the review of nutrition coordination guidelines and Zambia’s food systems pathways developed in 2021.

Ms Kapusana said the two year programme will support government and FAO in catalysing practical and institutional changes aimed at improving nutrition outcomes and strengthening the resilience of Zambia’s food systems.

She further said the project will focus on strengthening food systems coordination and governance, as well as promoting sustainable production, markets and consumption, surveillance and compliance mechanisms.

Ms Kapusana said the project will be implemented in Solwezi and Zambezi districts of North-Western Province, targeting vulnerable farming households and building the capacity of agriculture and nutrition extension workers.

She said combining targeted local implementation with national systems strengthening would allow lessons from the pilot activities to inform policy, guide future investments and support scaling up of successful interventions.

Ms Kapusana observed that Zambia has made progress in agricultural production and nutrition, with stunting levels declining from 35 percent in 2019 to 32 percent in 2024, but the progress remains insufficient to achieve Sustainable Development Goal number Two, of ending hunger by 2030.

She however, said Zambia continues to experience production and consumption patterns heavily centred on maize, while diversification into nutrient-dense crops, livestock, fisheries and other nutritious foods remains low.

“The situation contributes to low dietary diversity, while smallholder farmers continue to face climate variability, post-harvest losses, market access constraints and limited integration of crop and livestock systems,” added Ms Kapusana.

Ms Kapusana has since assured stakeholders that the Office of the Vice President would support government ownership, inter-sectoral coordination and strategic partnerships throughout the project cycle.

Meanwhile, FAO Representative in Zambia, Suze Filippini, said the project will support the government in strengthening coordination across sectors while promoting nutrition-sensitive and climate-smart agriculture, improving food safety systems and market linkages, operationalising the animal identification and traceability system.

Ms Filippini explained that the project is intended to catalyse lasting transformation by strengthening national institutions, partnerships, approaches and investments beyond the lifespan of the programme.

She said food systems affect production, household food choices, nutrition and health, environmental sustainability, employment, markets and the resilience of communities to climate and economic shocks.

Ms Filippini pointed out that Zambia continues to face interconnected challenges, including limited production diversity, market barriers, post-harvest losses, climate vulnerability, food safety risks and persistent malnutrition which need coordinated action.

She further said improved food safety and traceability systems will help protect consumers, strengthen livestock disease surveillance and create opportunities for producers to access domestic, regional and international markets.

Ms Filippini said the success of the project will ultimately be measured by improvements in the livelihoods of Zambians, stating that the project will support efforts to make rural communities more resilient to climate-related and economic shocks.

World.title: SEC in Muchinga to sensitise public on financial literacy
World.content:
Muchinga Province Deputy Permanent Secretary Brian Sichande says financial literacy remains key to Government’s agenda of creating a financially informed population.

Mr Sichande said Government was committed to implementing progressive policies, with financial literacy being an important area of focus.

He said this when a team from the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) Financial Inclusion and Education Unit visited him at his office.

Mr Sichande emphasised the need to promote financial literacy among young people, stressing that youths were the future of the country and needed to understand the value of money and how to use resources appropriately.

He said a lack of financial literacy could lead to the misuse of resources.

“If you did not have this lesson from the onset on how best to spend money, you risk taking the money somewhere it is not supposed to go. If a resource was meant to build schools, let it build schools. If it was meant to build markets or buy medicine, let it do that,” he said.

Meanwhile, SEC Manager for Financial Inclusion and Education Sitali Mugala said the Commission was targeting young people under the National Strategy on Financial Education initiative.

Ms Mugala said the initiative was aimed at promoting a culture of saving and investment from an early age.

She said SEC was conducting a National Capital Markets Debate across the country to encourage youth participation in capital markets.

“We are going around the country conducting financial literacy sensitisation. The debate is a build-up to the national debate that will be held in Chipata next month. As we move from province to province, tertiary institutions that have expressed interest will compete amongst themselves,” she said.

Ms Mugala said the Commission was targeting students from six institutions in Muchinga Province, including Kapasa Makasa University in Chinsali and Zambia College of Agriculture in Mpika.

World.title: Lusaka DEBS hails 2026 Grade 6 Literacy Quiz Competition
World.content:
The Ministry of Education has called for greater investment in literacy programmes that equip learners with knowledge and skills beyond the classroom.

Lusaka District Education Board Secretary, Christopher Nyungila, says the 2026 Grade Six (6) Literacy Quiz Competition is helping learners gain knowledge in museum education, financial literacy, general literacy and road safety.

Mr Nyungila said this in a speech read on his behalf by Ministry of Education Standards Officer, Anderson Katete during the competition hosted by the Lusaka National Museum in partnership with the Bank of Zambia(BoZ) .

He said museum education is important in helping learners understand the country’s heritage, culture and scientific knowledge.

Mr Nyungila also encouraged learners to develop financial literacy from an early age by learning how to use resources prudently.

He further called for strengthened road safety education, saying learners remain vulnerable to road traffic accidents caused by reckless driving and vandalism of road safety infrastructure.

Mr Nyungila said Government’s investment in education should be complemented by initiatives that develop practical knowledge and skills among learners.

And BoZ Assistant Director for Communications, Besnert Mwanza who was represented by BoZ Strategic Communications Manager, Daniel Tonga said more than 2,000 pupils have benefited from the Lusaka National Museum Schools Literacy Programme since its inception in 2019.

Ms Mwanza said the programme has helped strengthen literacy and critical thinking skills while promoting financial literacy, road safety awareness and museum education.

“I encourage you to cultivate good financial habits from an early age and make responsible financial decisions,” she advised.

She commended the Lusaka National Museum, Ministry of Education, Road Transport and Safety Agency (RTSA) and other partners for their contribution to the education and development of children.

Meanwhile, Lusaka National Museum Director, Perrice Nkombwe has called for stronger collaboration between museums and schools to give learners practical opportunities to understand Zambia’s history, culture and heritage.

Ms Nkombwe said regular interaction with museums can complement classroom teaching and help learners develop cultural awareness alongside academic knowledge.

“Museums are centres of learning that reflect our national identity,” she said.

She also encouraged learners to develop good reading habits and observe road safety practices, saying the skills will contribute to building informed and responsible citizens.

World.title: Serenje DC urges workers to embrace a clean environment
World.content:
Serenje District Commissioner, Ellen Mibenge, has urged workers in the area to embrace the “Keep Serenje Clean, Green and Healthy Campaign” as part of efforts to keep the town clean.

Ms Mibenge says every worker should participate in the campaign as part of the Government’s efforts to promote cleanliness and environmental sustainability across the country.

Speaking during a meeting with Government workers, Ms Mibenge said a clean environment is a catalyst for human and socio-economic development, as healthy citizens are more productive.

“The Keep Serenje Clean, Green and Healthy Campaign aims to involve every citizen of Serenje, not just the Council. Let us all participate in cleaning our surroundings to help prevent outbreaks of diseases in the district,” she said.

Ms Mibenge observed that some workers were using the campaign as an excuse for reporting late for work on Fridays.

The DC further expressed disappointment with some companies, traders and local residents who have continued to shun the exercise, which is aimed at promoting the development of the district.

She said authorities will seriously consider sanctioning business owners and workers who refuse to participate in the campaign.

The Keep Serenje Clean, Green and Healthy Campaign is conducted every Friday from 08:00 hours to 10:00 hours to promote environmental sustainability, public health and community development.

World.title: Africa: All of Africa Today - September 22, 2026
World.content:
Monrovia — South Africa Pushes for Permanent African Seat on UN Security Council

South Africa is leveraging ongoing intergovernmental negotiations on UN reform to advance the African Union's demand for permanent representation. Speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly, South Africa's Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Mxolisi Sizo Nkosi, highlighted Security Council reform as a core priority for Pretoria as it rallies support across member states.

The Security Council currently comprises 15 members: five permanent and ten non-permanent members elected for two-year terms. South Africa maintains that the body must expand to reflect contemporary global realities, specifically addressing Africa's historic absence from the permanent category.

UN Voices Deep Concern Over Escalating Security Crisis in Ethiopia



The UN has expressed strong concern over a deteriorating security situation in Ethiopia, pointing to the formation of a new coalition of armed groups, widespread instability, and repeated drone strikes.

Speaking at a press briefing on September 21, UN Secretary-General Spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric said the UN was "deeply concerned" by the ongoing escalation. The warning comes amid heightened tensions across the country, including fresh clashes between federal forces and regional troops in northern Tigray.

South West Somalia Steps Up Flood Preparations Ahead of El Niño Rains

South West State President Sheikh Adan Mohamed Nur Madobe convened a high-level ministerial committee and the Somalia Disaster Management Agency (SoDMA) to review emergency preparations ahead of expected El Niño rains.

Officials outlined risk mitigation plans aimed at preventing flood damage, safeguarding communities, and enhancing disaster response capabilities across the state. President Madobe urged government agencies and humanitarian partners to streamline coordination and ensure emergency equipment is pre-positioned in high-risk zones.

South African Women Need Protection, Not Warnings, Says Human Rights Watch

The discovery of several women's bodies on the outskirts of South Africa's commercial capital, Johannesburg, has caused fear, anxiety and outrage across the country. All the women were found naked or partially clothed, according to police. Some of the bodies had bruising. At least three suspects are already in custody as authorities continue to examine possible links between the killings

Writing for Human Rights Watch, researcher Stacey-Leigh Manuel emphasized that these horrific killings are not isolated incidents, but rather symptom of South Africa's ongoing national emergency regarding gender-based violence.

World.title: Niger: Junta Strips 5 More Exiled Critics of Nationality
World.content:
press release

Nairobi — Latest Crackdown Heightens Rights Concerns Amid Renewed Political Tensions

Niger's junta has provisionally stripped five more exiled opposition figures of their nationality, extending a controversial policy increasingly used against critics of the military authorities, Human Rights Watch said today.

On September 17, 2026, Gen. Abdourahamane Tiani, who has led Niger's junta since the July 2023 coup, signed a decree removing the nationality of five prominent Nigeriens living in exile. The decree derives authority from a 2024 order creating a national terrorism database with overbroad inclusion criteria and inadequate due process requirements and safeguards for redress. The order jeopardizes privacy and data protection rights and increases the risk of statelessness.



"The Niger junta's use of a terrorism database to deprive people of their nationality without any meaningful legal safeguards raises serious human rights concerns," said Ilaria Allegrozzi, senior Sahel researcher at Human Rights Watch. "Nationality is a fundamental legal status, not a privilege that governments can take from people for political reasons."

The five affected are former Prime Minister Ouhoumoudou Mahamadou; Amadou dit Ange Barou Chekaraou, Oumarou Moussa Ibrahim, and Ousmane Abdoul Moumouni, all former advisers to President Mohamed Bazoum, who was ousted in 2023 and remains arbitrarily detained; and Boubacar Seyni Souley, a social media activist critical of the junta.

The September 17 decree accuses the men of various offenses, including disseminating information capable of disturbing public order, providing intelligence to foreign powers, electronic defamation, demoralizing the armed forces, and threatening state security.

The decree raises questions about compliance with Niger's existing legal framework. The 1984 Nationality Code does not provide for "provisional loss" of nationality. Where deprivation of nationality is permitted, the law requires the authorities to notify the person concerned and give them one month to submit a written defense before the measure is published in the official journal.

"Nothing of the sort is happening here," the Alliance of Sahel Democrats, a coalition of Nigerien, Malian, and Burkinabè diaspora political opposition groups advocating a return to constitutional rule, said in a statement on September 18. The alliance also noted that the September 17 decree is depriving individuals of their nationality while they are still being prosecuted, in contravention of the 2024 order, which states that deprivation of nationality can only be imposed after a conviction.

According to Niger's press agency, the junta's latest action brings the number of people provisionally deprived of Nigerien nationality under the 2024 order to 25. In October 2024, the junta provisionally stripped nine people linked to former President Bazoum of their nationality. In June, authorities revoked the citizenship of Mariama Djibrine, an opposition figure living in exile.

In a September 19 statement, the G25-Niger, an opposition coalition of civil society groups and media organizations formed in 2025, said the 2024 order "is being used as a tool of political repression ... to crack down on opponents and other dissenting voices."

Since taking power in 2023, Niger's military junta has entrenched authoritarian rule and consolidated sweeping and unchecked powers, systematically weakening institutions capable of holding the military authorities to account.

In the past year alone, the military authorities have dissolved all political parties and several independent unions, suspended dozens of civil society groups, detained journalists under a broad cybercrime law, criminalized consensual same-sex relations, announced Niger's withdrawal from the International Criminal Court, and prolonged the country's political transition without any roadmap toward democratic elections. In addition to Bazoum, the junta continues to arbitrarily detain Moussa Tchangari, a prominent human rights defender.

The authorities have also taken steps to curb criticism from abroad. In June, Niger's foreign affairs minister instructed diplomatic missions to monitor online criticism of the military authorities, signaling growing scrutiny of the diaspora's discussions of the country's political and human rights situation.

The political climate in Niger has become increasingly tense in recent weeks, Human Rights Watch said. On August 28, mutinous soldiers attacked a military base at the international airport in Niamey, Niger's capital, and the presidential palace, with hours of gunfire. The mutineers also briefly seized the headquarters of the state-run national television, disrupting broadcasts. General Tiani called in Russia's government-controlled Africa Corps, whose intervention, including the use of armed drones, helped loyalist forces suppress the mutiny.

Close 

Niger is a party to the United Nations Convention on the Reduction of Statelessness, which restricts states from depriving people of their nationality when doing so would leave them stateless. Colleagues of the five affected by the September 17 decree said that at least four of them only possess a Nigerien passport.

Those who are without a nationality as well as their families risk being deprived of legal and social protection abroad. It could prevent them from returning to Niger, which is their right under international human rights law.

"The Niger junta has been depriving perceived political opponents of their nationality without meaningful due process, and contrary to Niger's obligations to prevent statelessness and protect fundamental rights," Allegrozzi said. "The junta should immediately revoke the decree and suspend the use of the easily abused terrorism database."

World.title: Djibouti: Djibouti Frees Top SA Investigative Journalist Micah Reddy
World.content:
South African investigative journalist Micah Reddy of the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists was detained on Saturday, but is now on his way back to South Africa.

Micah Reddy, the South African investigative journalist who was detained by government authorities in Djibouti on Saturday, 19 September, was released on Tuesday and is on his way home to South Africa, unharmed.

His family announced this on Tuesday following two days of anxiety after he and his local fixer Kooki Mahmoud disappeared from their hotel in Djibouti at about 1pm on Saturday. Reddy's family said in a statement that Mahmoud had also been released without charge.

"It is with immense relief and delight that we share the news that he is on his way back to South Africa, unharmed," the family said.

Reddy, a journalist and Africa Coordinator at the International Consortium of Investigative Journalists (ICIJ), had been held in the custody of Djiboutian authorities "from 1pm on Saturday, 19 September 2026", the announcement added.

"Despite numerous efforts to establish his whereabouts and condition, no official information was provided until today," the family said.

World.title: Sudan: Drone Strikes Destroy More Than 330,000 Learning Materials in Sudan's North Kordofan State
World.content:
New York/Nairobi/Khartoum — Drone strikes on two warehouses in Shikan locality, North Kordofan, on 20 September destroyed over 292,000 school textbooks, 40,000 Arabic Language and Mathematics Review Books, and other learning materials intended for distribution to children.

The materials were to be distributed from October 2026, marking the start of the new school year, including to schools in West Bara, Bara and Um Dam, with the loss expected to affect the learning of thousands of children.

"The destruction of these learning materials is a setback for children at a time when every effort is being made to get them back into the classroom," said Angela Kearney, UNICEF Representative in Sudan. "Many children have missed years of schooling due to the conflict. With schools already facing shortages of teachers, desks and learning materials, this loss will further undermine children's access to quality education. Every child has the right to education, and that right must be protected."

Delivering education supplies to the conflict-affected areas in Sudan is often challenging, making the loss of these materials particularly significant. Access to safe learning opportunities remains essential to helping children learn, recover and build their futures.

UNICEF calls on all parties to protect civilians and civilian infrastructure and uphold their obligations under international humanitarian law. Education supplies and facilities must be safeguarded to ensure children can fulfill their right to education.

World.title: North Africa: Egypt Declares Suez Canal Secure As August Revenue Surges to $567 Million
World.content:
CAIRO — Egypt's Suez Canal Authority (SCA) has declared the waterway safe, with maritime traffic flowing normally as August revenue rose 56.7 percent year-on-year to $567.1 million, up from $326 million in the same month of 2025. SCA Chairman Osama Rabie announced the figures during a ceremony in Alexandria marking World Maritime Day 2026, organized by the Maritime Transport Sector of the Ministry of Transport.

The revenue increase represents a notable rebound for a canal that has endured significant disruptions in recent years. Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty previously said Red Sea tensions had cost Egypt roughly $11 billion in lost Suez Canal income. The latest numbers point to a recovery for one of the country's most vital sources of foreign currency.

The canal transited 1,358 vessels in August 2026, a 27 percent increase from 1,070 vessels in August 2025. Net tonnage rose 51.1 per cent to 68.3 million tonnes, up from 45.2 million tonnes a year earlier.

Rabie emphasized that navigation remained stable and services continued at high efficiency. He added that canal pilots were carrying out their duties with the highest levels of readiness and professionalism.

Despite the strong year-on-year gains, traffic has not returned to pre-disruption levels. Average canal transits stood at about 40.8 vessels per day between January and August 2026, compared with 73.7 per day in 2023. Canal revenue reached $4.67 billion in fiscal year 2025/2026, a 23 percent increase, though vessel transits and cargo tonnage remain below the canal's peak performance.

The Suez Canal remains a critical artery for global trade, linking the Mediterranean Sea to the Red Sea and offering the shortest maritime route between Asia and Europe.

World.title: Liberia: A Decade On - the World Is Still Listening to Liberia's Ebola Story
World.content:
Ten years after Ebola swept through Liberia and claimed thousands of lives, the world is still turning to this small West African nation for answers. On Sunday, in a wide-ranging conversation, Chris McCall of The Lancet's World Report, the news section of one of the world's oldest and most trusted medical journals, sat down with Gregory T. Blamoh, Secretary General of the Liberia National Red Cross Society (LNRCS), to revisit an outbreak that reshaped the country's approach to public health emergencies.

The conversation was part of a broader examination of how nations once devastated by epidemics have turned hard-won experience into lasting institutional memory.

"Our success in the Ebola response was collective," Blamoh said. "Every Liberian was involved and learned from the response. Systems have been put in place, and every Liberian is fully aware of Ebola. And if we were to have any recurrence, the impact will not be as devastating as the first outbreak."

Community volunteers built that collective response on the ground, many mobilized through the LNRCS.

Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn

During the 2014 outbreak, Red Cross volunteers trained, equipped, and trusted by their neighbors stood on the front lines, working across four areas of intervention that remain central to the organization's emergency work today: Safe and Dignified Burial, Risk Communication, Contact Tracing, and Psychosocial Support.

Ten years on, those four pillars remain embedded in Liberia's emergency preparedness architecture.

The LNRCS has continued training volunteers, strengthening early warning systems, and keeping communities informed work that has left the country better prepared for future public health emergencies.

Among the most sensitive and, at the time, most misunderstood interventions was Safe and Dignified Burial. Ebola spreads readily through contact with the bodies of the dead, making traditional burial practices a serious transmission risk.

Working in full protective equipment, 240 LNRCS-trained burial team members took on the difficult task of safely managing the remains of 3,820 Ebola victims while preserving as much dignity and cultural respect as possible.

It required constant, careful engagement with grieving families, community members, and traditional leaders, building the trust needed to explain why long-held burial practices had to change to protect the living.

Alongside the burial teams, Red Cross volunteers led sustained awareness campaigns, going house to house, market to market, and community to community to explain how the virus spread and how it could be stopped. In a crisis defined as much by fear and misinformation as by the disease itself, these conversations became one of the response's most powerful tools, correcting rumors, dispelling myths, and building trust.

Close 

The experience underscored a lesson that still shapes humanitarian response today: communities are not simply recipients of information, but essential partners in saving lives.

Volunteers also formed the backbone of contact tracing, systematically identifying and monitoring people who had been in contact with confirmed cases, following them through the 21-day incubation period, and alerting health authorities at the first sign of symptoms. This community-level monitoring helped catch potential cases early and contain chains of transmission before they could grow work that demanded discipline, persistence, and close coordination with health authorities.

The response also recognized the psychological toll of the outbreak on survivors, families, communities, and responders themselves.

Psychosocial support was woven into the Red Cross response, offering counseling and community-based care to help people navigate grief, stigma, fear, and trauma effects that, for many communities, lingered long after the outbreak was officially declared over.

A decade later, Liberia's Ebola experience continues to demonstrate the value of preparedness, community trust, local leadership, and volunteer action. The Red Cross volunteers at the center of the response were more than emergency workers; they were neighbors and trusted voices who translated public health messages into action that saved lives.

Today, the systems and community networks strengthened during the Ebola response continue to inform Liberia's readiness for future emergencies. As Blamoh put it, the experience "isn't just history; it's a roadmap other nations are learning from."

Ten years later, the world is still listening to Liberia. And Liberia's lessons still matter.

World.title: From campus radicals to Beijing's AI sabotage: Rep Randy Fine says 'US fighting to save Western civilization'
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

U.S. Rep. Randy Fine (Fla.-6) has emerged as one of the most outspoken foreign policy voices in Congress during his short tenure on Capitol Hill. He frames the modern political battleground not just merely as a domestic election, but as an existential struggle to preserve Western civilization.

In a wide-ranging exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, the Florida Republican pulled no punches as he tied anti-Israel sentiment and opposition to domestic AI data centers directly to foreign influence operations by Iran and China, positioning himself as an unapologetic fighter for President Donald Trump’s agenda.

GOP REP RANDY FINE DECLARES THAT DEPORTING ALL ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS IS THE TOP WAY TO MAKE THE US AFFORDABLE

As the Israeli-Palestinian conflict has emerged as a political lightning rod, serving as a primary litmus test for the American left, Fine believes foreign money has played a large part in shaping public opinion:

"I think it's a focused effort over many decades to try to pollute our population with these ridiculous ideas. But I think it's accelerated since October 7th as massive amounts of foreign money have come in to try and manipulate public opinion through social media. They lie. And here's how you know they lie. When other countries kill tens of thousands, hundreds of thousands of their people, no one seems to be bothered.

"But when Israel defends itself from a terrorist attack, they lose their minds. Iran killed 40,000 of its own people in a couple of days earlier this year. Those same people who are upset with Israel are actually siding with Iran. The good news is the vast majority of the American people understand that the United States and Israel are fighting to save Western civilization, and that's certainly a message that I'm focused on spreading every day."

As the Israeli-Palestinian conflict is sweeping through mainstream culture, with the recent cancellation of Macklemore's tour dates in football stadiums, Fine is a staunch defender of Robert Kraft's decision, and denies it's merely "conservative cancel culture":

"So first off, they weren't political statements. I mean, is calling for the death of Jews a political statement? I mean it's anti-Semitism in the same way racism against black people is. And while you're allowed to be an idiot, as this Macklemore guy is, you don't have the right to perform in a stadium that's owned by private citizens. He didn't want a guy who puts a prosthetic nose on his face, in order to appear to be a Nazi, performing in his stadium. He has every right to say that is not welcome.

"That doesn't mean Macklemore can't stand on the street corner and preach his views. Cancel culture is when you cannot exist, when you're debanked, when you literally cannot function in society. But in the same way, I have the right to say whatever I want, other people have the right to you can't say it in my house. And that's all that's happened here. I think he [Robert Kraft] did the right thing. I think we need more of it."

AOC JOINS MACKLEMORE FUNDRAISING MEMO TARGETING ROBERT KRAFT

Fine has also been at the forefront of condemning the militant pro-Palestine protesters who have taken over university campuses across the country over the past year:

"I think we draw the line at violence. Every student has the right to get an education. And so, for example, when Jewish students are not able to come to class, when they're not able to walk across campus, when they're blamed for the actions of a country on the other side of the world, that is where you've crossed a line.

"Look, I had to deal with the free Palestine idiots when I was in college, you know, 30 years ago. But they didn't affect my ability to actually exist and to do my job and to be a student. So I just didn't worry about it."

Fine has described himself as "MAGA through and through" and sees himself as one of the president's staunchest defenders in Congress:

"Well, I believe in making America great again. I've been a huge supporter of the president. I was the first member of the Florida House to support President Trump when he ran for president again in 2024. And I believe that the president is really putting his fingers in the dam of the destruction of Western civilization, which so many are trying to shove down our throats.

"So I'm here to be a warrior and a soldier for President Trump's agenda, and I've been proud to do it since I got elected on April 1st of last year."

As domestic opposition to data centers has skyrocketed, and AI regulation emerges as a major issue heading into the midterms, Fine warns that China is using both issues to win the geopolitical advantage over the United States.

"I think it's largely an op by China. And let's explain why. So I think the 21st century, who wins the 21st century, will largely be defined by who wins the war over AI. And that fight is on four levels.

"One is hardware. Who has the best hardware? Right now, America is in the lead on that. Who has the best software? Right now, America is on the lead.

"Who has the best energy infrastructure? Unfortunately, China has the lead on that because while the idiots on our side have said let's not have coal-fired power plants …let's not have nuclear, let's get all of our energy from solar and windmills, China, who's selling us all the solar and the windmills, is putting up coal-fired power plants. So cheap, plentiful energy, China's winning that fight.

"But the fourth front in that fight is what they call compute: data centers. If you want to use Grok, if you want to use ChatGPT, if you want to use Claude and you type that stuff in, something needs to be doing the thinking. It's not happening on your phone, it's happening at a data center. And China has realized that if they can get America to not put data centers in, well then those data centers have to go in China and China wins on that front of the war.

"Does that mean you should be able to put a data center in a neighborhood? No, it doesn't. But does that mean the data centers are a critical part of re-industrializing the United States to make sure we win the war over AI? It absolutely is."

Finally, Congressman Fine addressed the looming midterm elections, as Republicans face headwinds to retain control of both chambers, making a forceful case for the GOP's accomplishments in the 119th Congress:

World.title: ESPN personality Chris Canty shares wildly inaccurate statement about Ole Miss football on 'First Take'
World.content:
With Week 3's showdown between LSU and Ole Miss delivering on every single level, talking heads were still reacting to the Rebels' 32-24 win over the Tigers on Tuesday morning. Given that it was one of the most highly anticipated college football games in recent history, taking a few days to dissect it all is well warranted, but if you're going to do so, you have to have the most basic facts correct.

ESPN did not abide by that rule.

'First Take' host Stephen A. Smith was joined by former NFL players Jeff Saturday and Chris Canty to discuss Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss and what his future in the league could look like. While Canty dropped compliment after compliment about Chambliss and his abilities, one statement he made about Ole Miss' history as a program was not even close to being accurate.

"Ole Miss has had two wins against AP Top 10-ranked teams in the last 60 years, and that dude has both of them," Canty said while pointing to a graphic of Chambliss.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

While we can say that Canty is being a prisoner of the moment and also understand that he was likely fed that 'statistic' about the Rebels by a producer or researcher at ESPN, we can also recognize just how far detached from reality it is.

MISSISSIPPI GOV TROLLS LANE KIFFIN, LSU AFTER OLE MISS DEFEATS TIGERS IN COACH'S RETURN TO OXFORD

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

As Canty noted, Chambliss led Ole Miss to a win over LSU on Saturday and against Georgia in last year's College Football Playoff, giving him two wins over AP Top 10 teams, but he and the program have accomplished that feat many, many more times than two.



Just last season, No. 4 LSU visited Ole Miss and Chambliss led the Rebels to a 24-19 win. In 2024, Jaxson Dart pushed the Rebels past No. 3 Georgia. Ten years earlier, Ole Miss beat No. 3 Alabama 23-17 and No. 4 Mississippi State six weeks later, before beating the Crimson Tide on the road the following year when Bama was the No. 2 team in the nation.

Since the turn of the 21st century alone, Ole Miss has beaten 16 teams ranked inside the AP Top 10.

Mistakes happen, but some are far more egregious than others, and Canty's certainly falls into that category.

World.title: Deadly helicopter crash kills 2 pilots battling raging wildfire in Yosemite
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Two pilots were killed when a firefighting helicopter crashed while battling a wildfire in Yosemite National Park.

The helicopter went down while conducting water bucket drops on the Dome Fire on Sunday, according to The Associated Press (AP).

The pilots were the only people aboard the aircraft. They worked for Precision Helicopters, a company contracted to support the firefighting operation, the AP reported.

'WE THOUGHT WE WOULD DIE': PASSENGERS THROWN INTO CEILING DURING TERRIFYING FLIGHT

The deceased pilots were later identified as Ryan Cutter and Greg King, according to social media posts from Precision Helicopters.

Cutter had been a helicopter pilot since 2011, including a year-and-a-half with Precision Helicopters, according to his LinkedIn profile. He was described as a "deeply loved husband, son, friend and godfather" on GoFundMe.

King had previously worked on wildland fires in Alaska and extensively alongside the Alaska Division of Forestry & Fire Protection, according to a statement from the agency.

The agency said King had close ties to its wildland firefighting community, including loved ones who currently work for the division.

"Greg was a dedicated aviator and a dear friend to many of us," the agency said. "We are mourning both pilots who bravely supported firefighting efforts, and our hearts go out to their families."

CLICK HERE TO 

Precision Helicopters also paid tribute to Cutter and King in a social media post following the crash.

"These two men brought honor to the mission. Their dedication and service will never be forgotten," the company wrote.

The Super Puma helicopter was using a water bucket to help suppress the Dome Fire when it crashed near a lake, Benjamin Cossel, a spokesperson for the Federal Complex Incident Management Team overseeing the firefighting response, told AP.

The FAA and National Transportation Safety Board will investigate the crash, with the NTSB leading the investigation, according to the FAA.

Hundreds of firefighters are continuing to try to contain the Dome Fire.

The crash occurred as hundreds of firefighters continued working to contain the Dome Fire, which started on Sept. 15 near Wawona, California.

About 580 personnel were battling the wildfire, which had burned roughly 4.7 square miles and was about 15% contained, the AP reported.

The crash site was southeast of Ostrander Lake, about seven miles northeast of Wawona and roughly nine miles south of Yosemite's El Capitan, according to the AP.

A procession carrying the two deceased helicopter pilots was seen traveling through Merced on Monday, Sept. 21, according to Fox 26 in California.

World.title: Jaxson Dart knee injury evaluation continues with serious possibility he may miss the remainder of the season

The possibility Jaxson Dart may miss the rest of the New York Giants season has not been ruled out, a source confirmed to Outkick on Tuesday, as medical evaluations continue on the New York Giants quarterback's left knee.

Dart, his doctors and the team will determine next steps for addressing the knee injury he suffered Monday night, early in the game, against the Los Angeles Rams.

The source declined to say why Dart could miss the season. That outcome, however, would become likely if Dart requires surgery for a detached MCL ligament — a procedure that could carry a recovery timeline of four to five months.

GIANTS QUARTERBACK JAXSON DART SUFFERS KNEE INJURY AGAINST RAMS, MCL ISSUE FEARED

"I'm not sure exactly what news or anything's been stated, but right now, evaluations are ongoing," Harbaugh said. "We haven't got any final decisions yet. We've learned a lot more.

"I wouldn't really want to share too much until decisions get made. That takes more than one person, takes everybody involved. So when we know, you know, what direction we're gonna have to go or whatever it might be."

Harbaugh will meet with Dart (again) after he gets a second opinion on the MRI test he underwent on Tuesday. Then a decision on what to do next will be made in conjunction with the medical experts and Dart.

"So, I don't want to get out over our skis on that," Harbaugh said.

OutKick first reported on Monday night that Dart had suffered a sprained MCL and would miss time.

Asked after the game about his quarterback and reports of an MCL sprain, Harbaugh said the reports were in the correct "neighborhood."

World.title: Sturgill Simpson says talent is 'not as rare as people think' and work ethic matters more
World.content:
Sturgill Simpson doesn't think there's a hidden secret to success in music.

Simpson has carved out an incredibly loyal following in the country music industry by singing largely outlaw country tunes.

However, that's far from his only skill. He also released a pair of albums under his alter ego Johnny Blue Skies.

‘YELLOWSTONE’ STAR LUKE GRIMES REVEALS OUTLAW COUNTRY WAS 'NO-GO' IN PASTOR FATHER’S HOUSE

His secret to success?

Just work hard.

Sturgill Simpson blasts entitled and lazy singers.

Simpson spoke with Playboy about his rise in the music industry, and he took some not-so-subtle shots at people who don't think they need to earn it.

"I had all the thankless f***ing jobs. There are so many people I met when I moved to Nashville 15 years ago who had exponentially more talent than I do, but they had no work ethic. Or they thought [sic] that, because they were brilliant, they didn’t have to earn their medals," Simpson told Playboy (via Whiskey Riff).

He continued, "No, b*tch, get in the van and go do circles and sleep on f***ing floors for six months until 12 people in a room give a sh*t. That’s the only thing that’s going to be lasting. If you’re waiting on some machine to pump you out, that machine is going to flush your a** too. Talent’s not as rare as people think."

Simpson's comments shouldn't come as a surprise to anyone. This is the man who famously once said he was "plotting" the "destruction" of the music industry. Or, that's certainly how his comment was interpreted.

He's nothing if not honest and straight to the point. That's the authenticity that has gained him millions of fans.



The Kentucky-born country singer also does more than just sing. He does some acting, and appeared in the legendary HBO show "The Righteous Gemstones" to sing a cover of "All the Gold in California." It's 100% worth checking out online because it's hilarious and also impressive.

World.title: DAVID MARCUS: In deep blue Minnesota a red dawn may be rising ahead of the midterms
World.content:
NEW You can now listen to Fox News articles!

Six months ago, very few people imagined that this year’s senate and governor races in Minnesota would be anything but Democratic Party blowouts, but as we approach October, and the beating heart of the midterms, the Gopher state appears suddenly and stunningly in play.

Recent polling, as shoddy as this cycle’s surveys have been, show GOP senate candidate Michelle Tafoya within 2 or 3 points of her opponent, sitting Lt. Gov. Peggy Flannagan, and while the chaos surrounding the death of Alex Pretti at the hands of ICE is in the rearview mirror, the massive Somali fraud scandal decidedly is not.

On Sunday, I headed over to Cowboys Saloon in Lexington, Minn., just north of the Twin Cities, to attend a Vikings game watch party for local Republican volunteers, where I found Lisa Demuth, Speaker of the Minnesota House and candidate for governor, rallying the troops ahead of some door knocking and leafleting.

LEE CARTER: THE SUMMER POLLS MISSED THE POINT: VOTERS ARE MOVING — AND THE MIDTERMS BEGIN

Demuth is running against sitting senator Amy Klobuchar for governor as the Minnesota Democrats play a high stakes game of political musical chairs, in which poor Gov. Tim Walz has already lost his seat.

"We have heard from Minnesotans across the state," Demuth told Fox News Digital, "when we’ve been traveling, that they are ready for a change, it's nice to see the polling start to reflect that, but we were hearing voters ready for a change, ending fraud, making the state affordable, just all the desperate change we have needed."

Over the next several weeks, the key question will be whether Minnesota Republicans, and fed-up independents, really believe they can win this time, after decades of Democrat dominance

Minnesota’s GOP House Majority Leader, Harry Niska, was also on hand for the 9-3 Vikings victory and offered this explanation to the tightening races: "It’s not a surprise to those of us who have spent months talking to voters in Minnesota as more and more Minnesotans become aware of the billions of dollars that have been stolen from our taxpayers."

'WE HAVE NOT SLOWED DOWN': MINNESOTA NOT OUT OF THE WOODS ON MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL, EXPERT WARNS

The fraud that Niska refers to is, of course, the ongoing scandal surrounding the Minneapolis community in the Cedar Riverside neighborhood, that has been bilking tax dollars with fake learning centers and autism care, to the tune of a possible $9 billion, with a "B," dollars.

Indeed, the scandal, now long since a national story, was on the tongues of almost everyone I spoke to, of both parties, in the warm afterglow of the Vikings "W" once the canvassers had left to knock upon doors.

MINNESOTA'S ANTI-ICE AID FUND BECOMES LATEST CASUALTY OF STATE'S EMBARRASSING FRAUD PROBLEM

"It’s infuriating," Tony, in his late 30s, told me, going on to say, "There’s just no rules, and we all pay for it, it's like, how does this even happen?"

I met Bill and Laura, who appeared to be longtime friends over a cigarette and they had two distinct takes on the races. Bill told me of Michelle Tafoya, "She doesn’t impress me," then suggested, "I just don’t see the makings for an office for [her]."

WALZ APPROVAL RATING CRATERS TO LOWEST LEVEL EVER AND TRAILS TRUMP AMID MASSIVE FRAUD SCANDAL: 'TIRED OF IT'

But, when I asked how Minnesotans were feeling about their leadership on the state and federal level, it was Laura, without a beat who insisted, "We’re all very discouraged," prompting Bill to admit that Walz, "Took the opportunity to make choices that were not well conceived."

In one dire last comment, Laura shook her head and said, "People are losing hope, man."

My longest conversation of the day was with Dan, a smart, well-traveled and worldly man with a lovely little dog named Jasper.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION

Dan is a Democrat who freely acknowledges that bad mistakes have been made by Democrats in his state, but who sees the GOP as an existential threat, "They want to destroy the country," he told me, "just start with data centers, they just seem to serve these corporations."

Dan is skeptical that Tafoya and Demuth can pull of the upsets, and gave me one pretty compelling reason why when he pointed a table of about 8 people, various ages, in their purple and gold and finery, saying, "I promise you every person at that table is a Republican, how many do you think will vote?"

"Three," I replied, "Maybe four?" To which he simply said, "Bingo."

The flipside to Dan’s turnout argument were the two or three dozen volunteers stomping the suburb for the GOP even as we spoke, and having that kind of ground game as early as September is typically something you see from Democrats, not from Republicans.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Over the next several weeks, the key question will be whether Minnesota Republicans, and fed-up independents, really believe they can win this time, after decades of Democrat dominance, if they do, and all signs point to yes, then expect a nail-biter in the Land of 10,000 Lakes coming this November.

This column will be in Minnesota for the rest of this week, looking to find out if a red dawn is really rising in Minnesota.

World.title: ‘Looksmaxxing’ influencer Clavicular charged with rape of teen girl
World.content:
“Looksmaxxing” influencer Clavicular has been charged in connection with the rape of a teenage girl at his family’s house in Cape Cod last May, according to a criminal complaint.

Clavicular, 20, whose real name is Braden Peters, was charged with rape, drugging someone for sexual intercourse and procuring liquor for someone under 21 years old. The complaint was filed on Sept. 8 in Orleans District Court in Barnstable County, Massachusetts.

Aleksandra Vasilevna Mendoza, an 18-year-old influencer known online as Alorah or Alorah Ziva, alleged that in May 2025, while she was in Massachusetts, Peters called her an Uber to his family’s Cape Cod house. Once there, he got her drunk on vodka while they livestreamed on Twitch and then raped her, according to a criminal complaint from the Chatham Police Department. His mom and grandmother were allegedly in the house.

The charges come months after Mendoza sued Peters in Miami, accusing him of sexual battery in connection with the events of May 2025. The civil lawsuit also separately alleges he injected her face with a non-FDA-approved fat-dissolving substance during a November livestream in Florida.

A source familiar with the matter confirmed that the charges against Peters are in connection with Mendoza’s allegations.

Peters’ attorney at the time Mendoza’s civil lawsuit was filed said that he denies the allegations and “intends to vigorously defend himself.” The influencer defended himself in a series of posts on X on Monday night; he included a section of a video Mendoza previously posted in which she spoke about meeting Peters in May 2025 and called him “super nice.” Peters also shared what appears to be a handwritten letter Mendoza sent him, in which she said she was “thankful for you helping me.”

“How about dont finance cars you cant afford,” he wrote in one post. “Happens to all successful young men, people try to come for your money. Greed is evil.”

Mendoza’s lawyer told NBC News they have “no comment at this time as the police are handling the criminal matter.” Peters’ attorneys declined to comment.

The Bulwark first reported the criminal charges. Peters’ representative, Mitchell Jackson, said the outlet was “exaggerating” in its article and that Peters had not been served with an arrest warrant. An email to the general mailbox of The Bulwark seeking comment was not immediately returned late Monday.

“Braden Peters has not been physically served. As usual the Bulwark is exaggerating,” Jackson said in a text message Monday night. A source familiar with the matter confirmed that Peters had not been served as of Tuesday morning.

According to the Massachusetts criminal complaint, Mendoza told police she met Peters on Instagram in May 2025, while Mendoza was a minor, and they developed an online business relationship. Her civil lawsuit alleges that Peter offered to help make Mendoza well known online, and paid her $1,000 to make four “looksmaxxing” videos.

Eventually, the criminal complaint says, Peters ordered Mendoza an Uber to his family’s residence in Chatham, Massachusetts, a seaside town at the southeastern tip of Cape Cod.

Mendoza said Peters’ mother and grandmother greeted her when she arrived at the house on May 23, 2025, early in the evening, according to the criminal complaint. She then went into Peters’ bedroom, where they livestreamed on Twitch while drinking alcohol. According to the criminal complaint, Mendoza told police she felt “peer-pressured” to drink.

She said Peters “instructed her to say that the alcohol is water, so that neither his Twitch

account nor live stream gets banned,” according to the criminal complaint. After making out on Peters’ couch, Mendoza said she fell asleep in Peters’ bed, according to the criminal complaint.

Mendoza told police that she woke up the next morning to Peters having sex with her, according to the criminal complaint.

“She stated that because it was already occurring, she did not tell Mr. Peters to stop,” the criminal complaint says. “Ms. Mendoza advised that she did not consent to the sexual intercourse.”

Mendoza told police she did not say anything to Peters as he was on top of her because she was in “shock,” and that she never verbally consented to the sex. She said that after Peters finished having sex with her “he was so cold” and ordered her an Uber home, according to the criminal complaint.

In her civil lawsuit, Mendoza additionally alleged Peters had sex with her when she was drunk “to the point where she was unable to give consent.” The criminal complaint did not mention that allegation.

Mendoza did not receive a sexual assault forensic exam after the encounter, according to the criminal complaint.

According to the criminal complaint, she initially told police she told a friend about the encounter but could not provide the friend’s contact information at the time. When police called her back later, she told them she “did not tell anyone the full extent of what occurred,” according to the criminal complaint.

Police attempted to contact Peters multiple times in response to the allegations, per the criminal complaint, but he did not contact authorities as of Aug. 30.

Mendoza said she saw Peters again in November 2025 after they ran into each other at a networking event in Miami, her civil lawsuit says. Peters then allegedly invited Mendoza and her friends to his place in Delray Beach, Florida, for a streaming session on Kick.

Mendoza alleged that during the livestream, Peters injected her with a syringe of Aqualyx, a fat-dissolving compound he did not reveal was not approved by the Food and Drug Administration, which he said would reduce fat in her face, without her consent, according to the civil lawsuit.

“The video shows that Peters had problems injecting Mendoza. In fact, Mendoza’s right cheek has perforated,” the civil lawsuit says, adding that Peters allegedly suggested that the syringe contained methamphetamine.

Peters and Mendoza saw each other a handful of times after that, including instances where Peters paid bouncers to let Mendoza into bars and purchased alcoholic drinks for her, according to the civil lawsuit.

In July, Peters filed a motion to dismiss several counts and challenged the sexual misconduct claim, which was added in an amended complaint. That motion is still pending. Peters is set to be deposed on Oct. 1, and the case remains pending.

Over the last few years, Peters has gained enormous fame as something of a godfather of “looksmaxxing,” an online phenomenon among young men. “Looksmaxxing” is the general practice of trying to maximize your physical appearance through a wide range of dieting, exercise and grooming habits. It promotes men with sharp jawlines, low body fat and symmetrical faces.

“Looksmaxxers” sometimes attempt to achieve the optimal male physique through extreme measures, including “bone smashing,” or using a hammer to intentionally break facial bones so they grow back more defined. Experts have called the trend potentially unhealthy and dangerous.

The new charges against Peters are not his first run-in with the law.

Peters and two other people were charged in April in Florida with shooting at an alligator. He and another person pleaded no contest to unlawfully discharging a firearm in public and were given six months of probation and ordered to serve 20 hours of community service, according to NBC South Florida.

He was also hospitalized in April in Miami after a suspected overdose, according to his representative. He said in a livestream at the time, after being released from the hospital, that “I ain’t gonna be doing any more substances for a little while, hopefully for forever.”

World.title: Hayden Panettiere died from accidental overdose of drugs, including fentanyl, coroner says
World.content:
“Heroes” and “Nashville” star Hayden Panettiere’s death has been ruled an accident caused by the toxic effects of multiple drugs, including fentanyl, officials said Tuesday.

The Greenville County Coroner’s Office said that her “cause of death has been ruled as toxic effects of fentanyl, 4-ANPP, Alprazolam, Methocarbamol, and Quetiapine.”

There were no signs of trauma that would have contributed to Panettiere’s death, the release added.

Panettiere, 36, died Aug. 16 at a South Carolina apartment complex where she had been staying. Authorities found her unresponsive after responding to a report of a cardiac arrest.

The Greenville Police Department said there were no signs of foul play during the initial response and investigation. The Drug Enforcement Administration was also investigating Panettiere’s death.

Panettiere’s on-again, off-again boyfriend, Brian Hickerson, was at the apartment complex at the time of her death and showed authorities what a police report described as a “bag of medication” he said she was taking.

An attorney for Hickerson did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment on Panettiere’s death. Panettiere’s mother, Lesley Vogel, also did not immediately respond to NBC News’ request for comment.

In an interview with NBC News last month, a former DEA special agent who probed the overdose deaths of Michael Jackson, Matthew Perry and other celebrities said investigators were likely attempting to reconstruct Panettiere’s final days.

“They will use forensics to exploit her telephone, try to re-create the last two or three days of her life from looking at text messages, looking at phone calls, looking at interaction with people on social media,” said Bill Bodner, a 32-year veteran of the DEA’s field office in Los Angeles.

“Once there’s a timeline of what she was doing before her death, it becomes easier to kind of find where that drug distribution took place that killed her,” Bodner added.

Panettiere’s relationship with Hickerson — an aspiring actor from South Carolina — appeared to have ended in 2020 amid allegations of domestic violence, but her mother told NBC News that they were still seeing each other when she died.

Panettiere detailed those allegations, along with her struggles with addiction and postpartum depression, in her recently released memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning.”

Hickerson pleaded no contest to a charge of injuring a spouse or girlfriend in 2019 in Los Angeles, and he was sentenced to four years of probation, court records show. Panettiere sought a restraining order against Hickerson in 2020, though the outcome is unclear.

In a statement in August, a lawyer for Hickerson reiterated that police found no signs of foul play in Panettiere’s death. The attorney, Sloan Ellis, added that the actor’s death remained under investigation.

“Out of respect for Hayden’s loved ones and the ongoing investigation, there will be no further comment at this time,” Ellis said at the time.

Panettiere began appearing in television commercials as a young child. She landed a breakout role on the NBC sci-fi series “Heroes” and later earned two Golden Globe nominations for portraying an ambitious and volatile country musician in “Nashville.”

In her memoir, Panettiere wrote that her life began to spiral after she had a daughter with Ukrainian heavyweight boxing champion Wladimir Klitschko in 2014. She began drinking heavily to cope with postpartum depression and Klitschko’s distance, she wrote.

Panettiere eventually checked into rehab and gave Klitschko custody of their child in 2018.

If you or someone you know is struggling with a drug or substance abuse problem, call these numbers for help: The Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration’s national helpline is 1-800-662-HELP (1-800-662-4357); the National Drug Helpline is 1-844-289-0879; and the American Addiction Centers’ hotline is (866) 464-3073.
