World.title: Iraqi banking sector capital tops 21.4T dinars amid sovereign credit pressures
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The total capital of Iraq’s banking sector has surpassed 21.4 trillion Iraqi dinars, with aggregate banking assets reaching 155 trillion dinars, according to data presented by the Iraqi Private Banks League (IPBL) on Tuesday, September 22, 2026.

Speaking during a financial workshop convened by the Parliamentary Finance Committee and attended by an Iraqi News Agency (INA) correspondent, IPBL Executive Director Ali Tariq delivered a comprehensive overview of the nation’s banking architecture against the backdrop of prevailing macroeconomic and sovereign credit challenges.

Tariq outlined core macroeconomic indicators, citing Central Statistical Organization data placing Iraq’s population at 46 million following the latest census, alongside an International Monetary Fund estimate pegging nominal Gross Domestic Product at $264 billion.

However, he cautioned that Iraq remains classified in the high-risk, non-investment grade category by Fitch Ratings, carrying a sovereign credit rating of B-minus. He stressed that while this tier reflects an entity’s current capacity to meet short-term debt servicing obligations and interest payments, it signifies acute economic vulnerability, a razor-thin fiscal safety cushion, and severe exposure to external macroeconomic shocks.

The minus modifier, Tariq noted, positions Iraq at the absolute lowest threshold of the B rating band, leaving the sovereign profile just one notch away from a downgrade into the CCC category, where default risks become acute and sovereign borrowing costs escalate sharply.

Such credit metrics, he warned, inflate bond yields required to entice international investors and complicate sovereign and institutional access to international capital markets while driving up debt insurance and borrowing costs.

Turning to the domestic institutional footprint, Tariq detailed the scale of the financial system, which currently encompasses 73 operating banks. This total includes 7 state-owned banks, 55 domestic private commercial and Islamic banks, and 11 branches of foreign banking institutions.

The ecosystem is further supported by 18 licensed electronic payment service providers, 3 microfinance entities, and 458 registered foreign exchange and remittance bureaus, forming the backbone of the domestic financial circulation network.

World.title: East Baghdad field supplies Iraq’s electrical grid with 25 million cubic feet of gas
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The East Baghdad oilfield is bolstering Iraq’s efforts to increase the utilization of associated gas and enhance fuel supplies to the electricity sector.

A new gas processing unit has been inaugurated with a capacity of 25 million standard cubic feet per day at the East Baghdad field, one of Iraq’s most significant oil resources.

Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair inaugurated the associated gas processing unit at the East Baghdad oilfield on Tuesday. This important milestone aims to recover associated gas and minimize flaring.

The produced gas—once processed and separated to meet approved technical specifications—is transported via pipeline to the Bismayah power plant, boosting reliance on domestic gas for electricity generation.

The new unit is integral to the Iraqi Ministry of Oil’s strategy to enhance gas recovery and connect production to the national gas network and power plants, thereby bolstering domestic energy production.

The oilfield is being developed in partnership with the China-based company EBS to enhance and advance Iraq’s oil sector.

An enormous discovery raised the reserves of the East Baghdad field to 15 billion barrels.

This discovery enhances Iraq’s position as one of the world’s top oil producers and creates new avenues for output expansion and revenue generation.

In collaboration with EBS, Iraq’s Midland Oil Company (MOD) said last year that two billion more barrels had been found in the oilfield.

Given that this discovery represents the largest expansion in central Iraq’s crude oil reserves in decades, the energy industry is paying close attention to it. Several studies are being done to develop strategies to maximize productivity and use this important resource.

This finding raises the overall reserves of the East Baghdad field to 15 billion barrels, up from 13 billion barrels before the latest discovery.

The discovery is a major step that supports the Iraqi oil sector and increases national income since the oil field is considered the largest in central Iraq.

World.title: Iraq coach Graham Arnold confirms readiness ahead of Oman clash
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq national football team head coach Graham Arnold confirmed on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, that the squad is navigating a new competitive cycle with sufficient tactical quality and veteran composure to secure victory against Oman.

Speaking during the pre-match press conference in Basra attended by an Iraqi News Agency (INA) correspondent, the Australian manager stressed that the team blends experienced international campaigners with emerging young talent eager to establish themselves on the international stage.

Arnold highlighted the presence of key veterans, noting that players who featured in the FIFA World Cup—most notably forward Aymen Hussein—provide tactical leadership and tournament maturity for the younger prospects.

The manager emphasized that following recent personnel and technical staff adjustments, the focus remains firmly on future development and modernizing the team’s tactical structure, describing the tournament as a vital benchmark for Iraqi football’s continued progression.

Addressing squad fitness and roster updates, Arnold revealed that forward Ali Al-Hamadi sustained an injury and has been replaced in the camp, while confirming that the remainder of the roster is in solid physical condition.

Despite the injury setbacks, the coach reiterated full confidence in the newly integrated call-ups to meet the tactical demands of the match. Arnold dismissed looking back at prior results, stating that the singular collective objective is to execute a winning performance against Oman and compete directly for the championship trophy.

World.title: Iraq plans disarm Iran-backed militias by June 2027
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi revealed an ambitious plan to disarm Iran-backed militias in his country by June 2027.

In an interview with The New York Times, al-Zaidi said that the disarmament decision is not optional but a necessity, describing it—alongside the fight against corruption—as a matter of honor.

According to al-Zaidi, the plan begins with a 90-day period during which the militias would refrain from launching attacks in exchange for guarantees that they would not be targeted by US forces; this would be followed by a weapons-handover process concluding by June 30, 2027.

The prime minister said that the militias are still pushing for an extension until the end of the year, but a top Iraqi security source warned that the plan would collapse unless Washington and Tehran reach a peace agreement.

Al-Zaidi claimed that he intends to disband these militias as autonomous formations and merge them into the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF) as individuals. He also stated that any groups functioning under militia identities beyond the deadline will be considered illegal.

On the other hand, these groups insist on their right to bear arms as long as “occupation forces” pose a threat—a reference to the war waged by the United States and Israel against Iran last February.

The spokesperson for the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, Sabah al-Numan, said last month that the government remains dedicated to regulating firearms and guaranteeing that they are under the control of the state and its official security agencies.

Al-Numan stated that a specialist committee had been created and that discussions were underway on how to control weapons in a way that preserves them, adding that the issue was a fundamental demand.

The Undersecretary of the Ministry of Interior, Hussein al-Awadi, announced on Monday that authorities plan to collect up to six million weapons in the upcoming months. This initiative is part of the government’s efforts to limit weapon possession strictly to security forces.

World.title: Iraq domestic public debt surges 21% to 109.5 trillion dinars by July 2026
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s total domestic public debt rose to approximately 109.5 trillion Iraqi dinars by the end of July 2026, marking a 21 percent expansion since the close of 2025, according to official statistical disclosures released by the Central Bank of Iraq.

Figures published indicate that internal sovereign debt increased by roughly 19 trillion dinars over the first seven months of the year, up from 90.5 trillion dinars recorded at year-end 2025. This internal borrowing trajectory accelerated steadily across the summer months, climbing from 103.2 trillion dinars at the end of May to 106.1 trillion dinars in June, before reaching 109.5 trillion dinars at the close of July.

The sovereign debt portfolio remains heavily concentrated within central bank liabilities and short-to-medium-term credit instruments. Claims held by the Ministry of Finance in favor of the Central Bank of Iraq represent the single largest share of the domestic obligation, standing at 72.5 trillion dinars, or over 66 percent of the total figure.

Direct commercial and state bank loans constitute the second-largest portion at 18.95 trillion dinars, representing more than 17 percent. Government bonds account for 9.33 trillion dinars, or roughly 8.5 percent, while short-term treasury bills issued to satisfy immediate fiscal liquidity requirements comprise 8.74 trillion dinars, or approximately 8 percent of total internal commitments.

The sharp rise in domestic debt underscores Baghdad’s intensifying reliance on internal deficit financing to sustain state operational outlays amid constrained liquidity and persistent pressure on sovereign revenue channels.

World.title: Iraq loses $60 billion since outbreak of US-Iran conflict
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi revealed that Iraq—the world’s third-largest oil supplier—has lost approximately 60 percent of its monthly export revenues due to the ongoing conflict between Washington and Tehran, which has disrupted maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

In an interview with The New York Times, al-Zaidi explained that Iraq’s total losses since the outbreak of the conflict have reached around $60 billion.

Although Iraq is considered a regional partner of Iran, Tehran has not permitted Iraqi oil tankers to pass through the Strait of Hormuz, according to al-Zaidi.

“We held extensive discussions. Iran’s decision is firm. Their goal is to drive up global oil prices. It is not a matter of how close we are to them; ultimately, they want to exert pressure,” al-Zaidi said.

Since he assumed office, al-Zaidi has put forward proposals to build pipelines that bypass the Strait of Hormuz. Earlier this year, Iraq agreed to a one-year deal to increase oil exports to Turkey via an existing Iraqi pipeline and is now seeking to expand the line’s capacity.

During his recent visits to France and Germany, al-Zaidi suggested plans to build pipelines through Turkey that would allow Iraqi oil to be transported directly to Europe.

The attempt comes as Iraq is under increasing pressure from Washington—its main security and economic partner—to restrain Iran-aligned groups that have acquired enormous military power and political influence.

At the same time, Iran is seeking to deepen its influence in the country and expand its use of these militias in its conflict with Washington.

Disarming militias has presented a challenge for previous Iraqi administrations. Iran-backed factions have become established in the past few years, creating parties deeply connected with the political and economic institutions, making it difficult to control them.

World.title: Iraq suspends flights by Iranian airlines
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iranian airline flights to Iraq are facing contradicting reports, with government sources alleging a suspension while transport authorities say flights are operating normally.

Iraqi government sources told news agencies that Iraq will halt all Iranian airline flights starting Tuesday. These sources claimed that Baghdad must comply with restrictions, which are part of US sanctions on Iran, or face serious penalties.

The spokesperson for Iraq’s Ministry of Transport, Hussein Ahmed, refuted claims of a flight suspension. He affirmed that flights between Iran and Iraq are continuing as scheduled and emphasized that no official directives to cease operations had been issued to Iraqi airports.

The new threat to Iranian airlines stems from broad secondary sanctions imposed by US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent.

The United States launched an economic pressure campaign known as “Operation Economic Outcast” to effectively isolate the Iranian regime from the global economy.

Under these laws, any country or firm that provides services to Iranian aircraft is completely removed from the global US dollar system. The services include fueling airplanes, offering ground handling and landing services, and selling passenger tickets.

Countries in the region have already taken decisive action. Major regional airlines, notably Turkish Airlines, AJet, and Pegasus, have entirely removed Iranian routes from their systems, canceling all flights to and from Iran until at least March 2027.

An ongoing stoppage of flights between Iraq and Iran would create major inconvenience, as Iraq is a main destination for thousands of Iranian Shiite pilgrims visiting holy sites in Najaf and Karbala annually.

World.title: PM Al Zaidi meets Marco Rubio in New York, pledges state monopoly over arms
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi reaffirmed the federal government’s resolve to finalize sovereign transitions and enforce the state’s monopoly over weapons during a high-stakes bilateral meeting with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in New York.

According to a statement issued by the Prime Minister’s Media Office and reported by the Iraqi News Agency (INA), the discussions took place on Monday, September 21, 2026, on the sidelines of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly.

Prime Minister Al-Zaidi stressed Baghdad’s commitment to advancing long-term bilateral relations with Washington, framing the relationship around a comprehensive strategic partnership grounded in constructive economic cooperation and shared strategic interests.

Addressing core security and governance files, Al-Zaidi reiterated Iraq’s determination to complete all outstanding constitutional and sovereign benchmarks, emphasizing that the disarmament of armed factions and the consolidation of all arms under official state command remain non-negotiable legal mandates being executed in accordance with Iraqi law.

For his part, Secretary Rubio expressed the United States’ continued backing for the Iraqi government and people in their efforts to anchor enduring domestic stability, diversify the national economy, and expand global diplomatic and commercial engagement.

Rubio underscored Washington’s support for Baghdad’s sovereign decisions aimed at institutional state-building, reinforcing internal security, and establishing an enabling environment for sustainable economic development as critical regional deadlines approach.

World.title: UPI MDR will fund innovation, protect small merchants: NPCI’s Dilip Asbe
World.content:
The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed.

Why this sudden move to charge MDR on UPI, and how did you decide on the Rs 2,000 threshold and the 0.4% MDR? Will you review the scheme periodically?

How much is expected to be collected in the first year, around Rs 15,000 crore?

What is the rationale for the charge given that the government can easily foot a bill of Rs 20,000 crore, as it is a tiny fraction of its budget, especially when it spends thousands of crores on non-merit subsidies? Why can't banks, NPCI or RBI bear the burden?

What is being done to ensure that customers are not burdened with MDR? Also, is NPCI proposing a relook at GST?

How do you propose to utilise the money to develop the market? Do you see banks and other service providers offering loyalty points for UPI transactions, as is the case with credit cards?

Will there be a check on merchants and consumers splitting transactions to avoid MDR over Rs 2,000?

The new system has created confusion around several aspects of the scheme...

How do you respond to allegations that the decision was taken under US pressure?

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Why is the P2PM limit so low?

The waiver of merchant fees on UPI accelerated adoption during Covid, but growth slowed. In an interview with TOI, Dilip Asbe, MD & CEO, explains how the new fee structure protects small transactions while charging larger merchants, who already pay fees on card payments. Besides, there are a host of exemptions aimed at shielding consumers and small merchants. NPCI expects Rs 13,000-15,000 crore in the first year, with 5% of this being ploughed back to support small merchants, while periodic reviews will assess the model.UPI P2M was charged from inception, and we followed the global model of keeping P2P free and P2M at reasonable cost recovery, much lower than the prescribed MDR for debit and credit cards, net banking or wallets. The government's decision on zero MDR in 2020 helped UPI expand rapidly among merchants during the Covid period. In the last four years, the UPI ecosystem â namely NPCI, banks, fintech start-ups and industry bodies such as the Payments Council of India and IBA â has been seeking a review to ensure a self-sustainable system that can create long-term value for the country, citizens and merchants. UPI growth has slowed, and India remains under-penetrated compared with China and Brazil, where almost 90% of the adult population uses digital payments every day, versus 40% in our case.So, we need investment to expand digital payments, especially among the poor.The charges were finalised primarily keeping in mind the costs incurred by various players to process UPI transactions. Instead of a fixed-fee model, which would penalise low-ticket transactions, we opted for percentage-based charges so that high-ticket transactions with margins can contribute the majority of the MDR. Certain categories with high ticket sizes but lower margins were kept at a flat Rs 5 irrespective of the ticket size, to continue driving adoption. If you review the rates, they are almost at par with global rates for QR-based payments, which are charged similarly without making any exceptions, while these charges remain much lower than those for debit or credit card transactions currently paid by large merchants.It may take some time for the system to settle down. Maybe, in the first year, we will collect Rs 13,000-15,000 crore, of which 5% will be allocated to the small merchant fund to incentivise digital-payment growth among small merchants. We will soon release the guidelines on this.The idea is not to burden small players, as we expect over 80% of the MDR charges to come from businesses with over Rs 1,000 crore turnover. Most of them are already accepting cards and paying much higher MDR on cards under the current construct. There are competing demands on public funds, and this is the best way to make the ecosystem sustainable, grow and innovate without depending on subsidies.NPCI is a not-for-profit entity; all its profits are reinvested in creating infrastructure, reserves for settlement guarantees, innovation and resilience. NPCI needs to not only survive but thrive for the next 100 years.Banks continue to make substantial investments in maintaining and scaling the UPI ecosystem, with annual expenditure often exceeding Rs 2,000 crore for most large banks. At the same time, a Rs 5,000 cash withdrawal can often be substituted by 50 to 100 UPI transactions, highlighting the scale and efficiency of digital payments. While the transition from cash to digital payments has undoubtedly delivered savings through lower cash-handling and ATM-servicing costs, banks also incur significant costs in building and operating resilient, secure and scalable UPI payment infrastructure.Over the last six years, the overall ecosystem has invested over Rs 75,000 crore to maintain and grow the UPI ecosystem without much cost recovery. These investments and innovations will benefit the country in the long run.Running the UPI ecosystem requires around Rs 21,000 crore annually, and we have sought to protect small merchants and low-value payments to help smaller firms raise capital and invest. The idea is also to have more players to increase competition. As a result, person-to-person transactions and merchant payments up to Rs 2,000, with no upper cap on cumulative or repeat transactions, all recurring payments or AutoPay, and small individual merchants receiving up to Rs 1 lakh a month into their own accounts will not face any MDR. Since most of the MDR will be generated from merchants who already accept card payments, the consumer price is already factored into MDR charges, or else we would have seen merchants offering major discounts for UPI and RuPay debit card transactions over the last six years. We have prohibited platform fees and merchants charging customers. We plan to review it periodically along with the ecosystem. On GST, I have no comments to offer since this decision will be made by the finance ministry and GST Council. However, major large merchants will claim an input tax credit for the GST paid.The objective of these charges is to ensure the ecosystem thrives, becomes self-sustainable, and is able to innovate and create value that, in turn, grows UPI. Today, we observe that payment methods with good cost recovery tend to have better innovation and features. For example, EMIs, rewards and discount offers help grow merchant sales, particularly in categories such as electronics. Once cost recovery starts, the ecosystem will create a major drive to onboard new consumers and merchants, install more sound boxes and increase activity in under-penetrated geographies and categories through digitalisation. Amid evolving times and landscapes, it will also allow the ecosystem to invest proactively in cybersecurity and resilience.Any policy that has a ceiling or a floor has these second-order effects. If the consumer is ready to participate in splitting the transactions based on a merchant's request, we do not foresee any harm in this and, accordingly, no upper cap on such transactions has been defined. We believe this may, at best, be a short-term phenomenon and that consumer experience will ultimately win in the long run. What we have seen globally and in India is that it is primarily the consumer's choice that drives digital payments.Yes, but we are working with industry bodies and ecosystem participants to provide clarity. For example, some people have interpreted the no-MDR limit below Rs 2,000 as a daily cap and not a per-transaction limit, which is not the case.The USTR has a reference to a UPI market-share cap of 30%, as well as NCMC standards access to other competing international schemes, which is a fair and factual point, and we believe it must be a country's prerogative to make that decision. We didn't find any reference to charges or MDR, and, as I said above, it benefits competing companies to keep it free.This is more like an intermediate step for a merchant moving from receiving money via standard P2P to graduating into a proper P2M merchant so that it gets the support of a sound box, POS machine or other ancillary services. Even when P2PM merchants move to a proper merchant, they continue to receive transactions up to Rs 2,000 without any charges or cap.

World.title: Gauhati University, Thailand discuss academic, research collaboration
World.content:
Gauhati University and a senior Thai delegation on Tuesday discussed expanding cooperation in higher education, research, information technology, culture, training and student exchange, the university said.

World.title: Delhi govt sets up 81 artificial ponds to discourage Ganesh idol immersion in Yamuna
World.content:

NEW DELHI: The Delhi government has prepared 81 artificial ponds for people to immerse Ganesh idols at designated sites instead of the Yamuna or other water bodies.The government has also set up 110 collection centres for dignified disposal of old and damaged idols and religious material.The two measures form part of an initiative aimed at balancing religious practices with cleanliness and environmental protection.The initiative will provide designated collection containers at suitable locations, including temples, where devotees can deposit old, damaged idols and other puja material instead of leaving them in public places, chief minister Rekha Gupta said.She said such material is often left under trees, in parks, along roadsides and at other public places due to religious sentiments, creating challenges for cleanliness and the environment.Preparations have also been completed at 81 locations across Delhi for artificial immersion ponds for Ganesh idols. The arrangements cover all 13 revenue districts and include security, sanitation, lighting, medical assistance, emergency response and traffic management, according to a statement.The chief minister has appealed to devotees to immerse Ganesh idols only at designated artificial immersion sites and not in the Yamuna or other water bodies.She also urged people not to dispose of puja material, flowers, garlands and other religious items in rivers or water bodies and to give preference to eco-friendly idols.The government has advised devotees to avoid idols made of Plaster of Paris, colours containing harmful chemicals and decorative materials that can damage water bodies and the environment.Arrangements have also been made for removal of idol remains and other material from immersion sites after the festivities, followed by cleaning of the locations as per the prescribed process, it said.The initiative is aimed at providing organised and clean spaces for people to follow their religious traditions while reducing pressure on public spaces and water bodies, the statement said.Gupta said religious faith and environmental protection should complement each other and urged Delhi residents to use only designated collection centres for damaged idols and religious material and artificial immersion sites for Ganesh idols.She said maintaining a clean Delhi was a shared responsibility of the government and citizens, and called for public participation to balance faith, cleanliness and environmental protection.The Ganesh festival began on September 14 and will conclude on September 25, when a large number of idols will be immersed after colourful processions.

World.title: 'Broad daylight dacoity': SC questions overpricing of essential cancer drugs
World.content:
Supreme Court raises concerns over steep pricing of essential cancer medicines

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday questioned the steep markup on essential cancer medicines, with the bench describing the practice as âbroad daylight dacoityâ against patients. The remarks came after the court was informed that an essential cancer drug had a maximum retail price (MRP) of Rs 27,000, even though its price to retailers (PTR) was Rs 2,700, a tenfold difference.âThere are essential medicines for cancer on which the MRP is printed as Rs 27,000 while the PTR is Rs 2,700. This is absolute rampage and carnage. This is broad daylight dacoity with patients,â news agency PTI quoted a bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Sandeep Mehta saying.âIt is very surprising that the authorities who are supposed to take action on this are silent,â it saidThe bench said the price gap was âabsolutely shockingâ and questioned how such pricing could be allowed.âThe MRP is 10 times the rate at which it is provided to the retailers. If this is not extortion, then what it is? People sell their houses, ornaments to get treatment,â the bench said.The observations were made while the court was hearing two petitions dealing with drug-related issues, including demands for tighter price controls.One of the petitioners also raised the issue of registered medical practitioners prescribing generic medicines, and stressed the need for greater regulation of medicine prices.Additional solicitor general K M Nataraj, appearing for the Centre in one of the cases, told the court that the government was not approaching the litigation as an adversarial matter.The bench said fixing medicine prices remained a major concern and adjourned the matter to September 29.One of the petitions seeks measures to make drug formulations more affordable by preventing alleged unethical pricing of essential medicines by pharmaceutical companies and retailers. It also seeks strict enforcement of the Drugs (Prices Control) Order, 2013, to check violations of price-control rules and disproportionate retailer margins.The other petition seeks disciplinary action against doctors for not prescribing generic medicines to patients.

World.title: Rajya Sabha polls for 12 seats: BJP likely to retain 8 in UP, SP eyes gain, BSP at risk
World.content:
BJP likely to retain 8 UP seats, SP eyes 2, BSP faces exit

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The BJP is set to have the numbers on its side in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, with the party-led alliance expected to win eight of the 10 seats going to polls in the state. The Samajwadi Party could take the remaining two seats, based on the current strength of parties in the assembly.The Election Commission on Tuesday announced polls for 12 Rajya Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand and West Bengal. Voting, if required, will be held on October 16, with the results also to be declared the same day.The BJP is also expected to add one seat to its Rajya Sabha tally by winning the lone seat from West Bengal. The seat became vacant after actor Rukmini Mallick, popularly known as Koel, resigned from the House. The Trinamool Congress had sent her to the Rajya Sabha before losing power in the assembly election held earlier this year.In Uttar Pradesh, the BJP-led alliance has around 290 MLAs, while the SP-Congress combine has about 103. A candidate needs around 37 votes to win a Rajya Sabha seat.The BJP can comfortably win seven seats, while the SP-Congress combine can secure two.The contest for the 10th seat could be closer, with the BJP-led alliance starting with around 31 votes against around 29 for the SP-Congress side.The polls could also mark the end of the BSP's representation in Parliament. Mayawati's party has no member in the Lok Sabha and its only MLA in Uttar Pradesh, Uma Shankar Singh, died in August. The term of BSP's lone Rajya Sabha member, Ramji Gautam, ends in November.Gautam is among the nine Uttar Pradesh members whose terms are ending. The others are Union minister Hardeep Singh Puri, BJP leaders Arun Singh, Geeta Shakya, Neeraj Shekhar, Brijlal, B L Verma and Seema Dwivedi, and SP leader Ram Gopal Yadav.Puri's continuation in the Union Cabinet will depend on whether the BJP nominates him for another Rajya Sabha term.The 10th Uttar Pradesh seat was held by former deputy chief minister Dinesh Sharma. It became vacant earlier this month after Sharma resigned from the Rajya Sabha following his appointment as lieutenant governor of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.The BSP had managed to retain its Rajya Sabha presence in 2020 after the BJP fielded only eight candidates for 10 seats. The move allowed the BSP and SP to each elect one member unopposed.Gautam was elected unopposed after the nomination of an SP-backed Independent candidate was rejected. The SP had then alleged an understanding between the BJP and BSP.In Uttarakhand, BJP Rajya Sabha member Naresh Bansal's term is ending. The BJP, which has a comfortable majority in the state assembly, is expected to retain the seat.The election notification will be issued on September 29. Candidates can file nominations till October 6. Polling and counting will take place on October 16, if required.

World.content:
The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their âoperation, management and development agreementâ (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline.

SpiceJet:

Dope test on pilots:

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

No fare caps this festive season:

NEW DELHI: Govt is weighing the pros and cons of allowing Adani Group, which operates Mumbai airport, to run an airline. The Delhi and Mumbai airports went the PPP way in 2006 and their âoperation, management and development agreementâ (OMDA) does not allow the operators to have beyond 10% stake in an airline. Recently the Adani Group had sought amendment to the same.âGovt is clear that India needs more airlines, given the number of airports going to come up in India and the demand. Our ambition is to have at least five airlines with at least 100 aircraft each. So if someone wants to start an airline, govt supports the idea. The issue is an airport (Mumbai and Delhi) doing so. We are examining the pros and cons of the same,â Union aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said here Tuesday.Naidu said no decision on the Adani request has been taken so far. âWe need to create a system where the cons (of allowing such a move) are taken care of. Pros we know. As such in govt there is no clause or rule anywhere which stops airport operators from having airlines other than the OMDA agreement for Delhi and Mumbai. If let us say BIAL (Bengaluru operator), which is still a private operator, wants to operate an airline, there is no rule stopping him.Thatâs why we have to take a balanced approach,â said Naidu.Adaniâs request has divided the airline industry with IndiGo promoter Rahul Bhatia opposing the move and Akasa founder Vinay Dube being in favour of the same.The minister spoke about other issues at an UDAN event here Tuesday. âThe aviation ministry, Airports Authority of India and 21 States & UTs (have) come together and sign MoUs to put a greater focus on speed, sustainability and long-term viability of projects in the next phase of UDANâ¦ 100 airports will be developed under challenge mode over the next 10 years,â Naidu said.The cash-strapped airlineâs woes have been mounting and its passengers often suffer delays running in several hours. âWe are closely monitoring SpiceJetâs operations and finances through the aviation â regulatory body to ensure safety is not compromised. Operational and financial scrutiny is being done. SpiceJet got Rs 150 crore under ECLGS. Getting more funds is something the airline has to work with banks with. It is a private airline. Our priority is to ensure passengers donât face inconvenience and that safety is not compromised,â Naidu said.âThe intention of the ministry is that all pilots must get tested within a year. The framework for the same has to be issued by the regulator DGCA. We have given our intent to them and they are holding deliberation with stakeholders. The DGCA rule change to ensure this is expected,â said the minister.Airfares will not be capped this festive season and the aviation ministry will advise airlines to keep the same at reasonable levels, said the minister. The hike being seen in recent dues is not due to the spike in demand but due to increased jet fuel prices.âWe engage with airlines continuously and have regular meetings with them. And we definitely point it out to them that during this festive season, you have to ensure that the fair prices are kept at a reasonable level so that the people who want to travel, especially in these important times, get to see the benefit,â the minister said.

World.title: Confident of a hat-trick in U.P.: Nabin
World.content:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) would retain power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term in the 2027 Assembly election, party national president Nitin Nabin said on Tuesday.

“Neither our workers nor our leaders are part-time politicians. Our only aim is to serve the public,” he said addressing a gathering of office-bearers and workers in Saharanpur, concluding his two-day visit to western U.P., his first after becoming the national president.

“Today I had the opportunity to meet the workers and interact with our senior leaders in Saharanpur and the whole of western Uttar Pradesh. The enthusiasm of the workers and their energy clearly indicate that in 2027, the BJP will again form a government with a thumping majority,” he said.

Draws road map

Earlier in the day, he held meetings in Saharanpur with several MPs, MLAs and key office-bearers of the party and outlined the road map ahead. During the interactions, the party chief emphasised strengthening booth-level preparations.

On Monday, he addressed a Yuva Samvad programme in Meerut as part of an outreach to the youth.

“Under the leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modiji and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanathji, there is a public belief in development with cultural heritage. The common man is confident that under these two leaders, the goals of a developed Viksit Bharat (Developed India) and Uttam Pradesh (best State) will be achieved,” he said at Tuesday’s event, praising the Union and State governments for introducing various welfare measures and ending “lawlessness” in the State.

He urged party workers, whom he described as the party’s “backbone”, to ensure that “lotus blooms again” in U.P.

Differing voices

Meanwhile, west U.P. MPs — Iqra Hasan (Kairana) of the Samajwadi Party (SP) and Imran Masood (Saharanpur) of the Congress — made contradictory claims over their parties’ roles and capabilities in taking on the ruling party ahead of formal discussions on a pre-poll alliance.

Mr. Masood said, “Only [Congress leader and Rae Bareli MP] Rahul Gandhi is the Opposition’s voice across the country, which unnerves the BJP. No one should be under any illusion — nothing is possible without Rahulji.”

The Saharanpur MP has been pushing for the two parties to reach an early seat-sharing arrangement while claiming an “equal partner” status for the Congress.

On the other hand, Ms. Hasan said only the SP chief Akhilesh Yadav is capable of defeating the BJP. She added that without her party, the Congress has little hope in U.P.

“Only Akhilesh Yadav is capable of defeating the BJP. On its own, the Congress won’t be able to achieve much,” she said.

World.title: FACT foundation day observed
World.content:
The foundation day celebrations of Fertilisers and Chemicals Travancore Limited (FACT) were held at the company’s Udyogmandal club here on Tuesday (September 22).

Madhu S. Nair, former chairman and managing director of Cochin Shipyard Limited, delivered the first C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer memorial lecture.

A portrait of Iyer, the Dewan of the erstwhile princely State of Travancore, was unveiled on the occasion. Eleven senior employees of the public sector company were honoured, according to the company management. S. Sakthimani, chairman and managing director, FACT, attended.

Meanwhile, the Communist Party of India (CPI) alleged that the management had tried to observe the foundation day in respect of C.P. Ramaswamy Iyer.

N. Arun, Ernakulam district secretary of the party, said in a communication that Iyer had only played a natural role as Dewan of the erstwhile Travancore in setting up the public sector unit. There is a deliberate attempt to glorify him by celebrating him on the occasion of the foundation day of the company, he said.

He alleged that the State government had maintained silence over the political agenda behind attempts to highlight Iyer’s contribution to the formation of the company.

World.title: Monsoon Session of Odisha House witnesses ruckus over textbook errors, mines Act
World.content:
The Monsoon Session of the Odisha Assembly began on a stormy note on the expected line with the Biju Janata Dal and Congress targeting the Mohan Majhi government over two contentious issues—the fiasco in the preparation of school textbooks and allegations that the State’s interests were compromised in the Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Act, 2026.

Repeated disruptions marked the day as Opposition members rushed to the well of the House, demanding accountability from the State government over the issues. The BJD demanded the resignation of School and Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond over distributing error-ridden textbooks for the current academic year. The government has started distributing corrected textbooks, but nearly half the academic year has passed.

Revenue loss

Meanwhile, Congress members raised the issue of the MMDR Amendment Act, 2026, alleging that the Centre had taken away the State’s authority over its mineral resources. They demanded the withdrawal of the amendments and probed how much revenue the State stood to lose due to its implementation.

Speaker Surama Padhy was forced to adjourn the proceedings following vociferous protests by the BJD and Congress members. The BJD later took its protest to the streets, staging a demonstration at Lower PMG Square, in front of the State Assembly.

The Assembly session will continue till October 3. The government plans to introduce six Bills during the session.

World.title: Probe sought into alleged secrecy over Assembly panel’s visit to Aralam farm
World.content:
Alleging that the District Tribal Mission authorities deliberately kept secret the visit of the Kerala Legislative Assembly Assurance Committee to the Aralam farm rehabilitation area and assessment of issues related to the construction of the elephant proof wall, Adivasi Dalit Munnetta Samithi president Sreeraman Koyyon has sought an inquiry into the matter.

Mr. Koyon alleged that the secrecy was intended to block discussions on corruption in the tribal rehabilitation area over the past decade and on the deaths of tribal people in wild elephant attacks, which he attributed to administrative lapses.

He said that an officer facing allegations and still holding charge as Tribal Rehabilitation Development Mission (TRDM) site manager and senior officials of the Aralam Farming Corporation were behind the move. He said the latter had helped private companies and individuals obtain tribal land in Aralam farm on lease and use lease agreements to secure loans from scheduled banks.

Mr. Koyon alleged that MLAs from both the ruling and Opposition fronts attempted to portray the committee’s visit as a private visit, and termed it a betrayal of the tribal community. In a complaint submitted to the Assembly Speaker, he sought action against officials who allegedly concealed information about the committee’s visit and demanded an investigation into the circumstances surrounding the visit.

World.title: BJP maintains dominance in Rajasthan urban bodies by winning 6 deputy mayor seats
World.content:
After its victory in the mayoral contests and polling for chairpersons of municipal councils and municipalities in Rajasthan on Monday, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) continued its winning spree for the posts of deputy heads of urban bodies on Tuesday.

The ruling party maintained its dominance in the urban local bodies by winning the seats of deputy mayors in six of the seven municipal corporations where the polling was held. A Congress-supported Independent councillor was elected in Pali.

Besides seven municipal corporations, the polling was held in 47 municipal councils and 251 municipalities.

Draw of lots

Despite securing the mayoral post in Bikaner, the Opposition Congress lost the deputy mayor’s seat to BJP’s Pankaj Gehlot. In Ajmer, BJP’s Hemant Sankhla and Congress’s Naurat Gurjar received 40 votes each, after which the decision was taken through the draw of lots, resulting in the victory for Mr. Sankhla.

Congress-supported Independent Mahboob T. was also declared elected through draw of lots in the Pali Municipal Corporation. Mr. Mahboob and BJP’s Vikram Pal Singh secured 29 votes each, after which the result was announced through the prescribed procedure.

BJP’s Dinesh Bhatt defeated Congress candidate Lakshminarain Meghwal in Udaipur, while BJP’s Ajay Poonia defeated Congress’s Mamta Saini in Alwar. BJP’s Ambika Saini won as the deputy mayor in Bharatpur, which is the home district of Chief Minister Bhajan Lal Sharma. The BJP succeeded in Bharatpur Municipal Corporation despite the Independent councillors having formed the largest group by winning in 65 wards in the local body elections held recently.

BJP’s Radheshyam Somani was elected unopposed as the deputy mayor in Bhilwara Municipal Corporation. On Monday, BJP’s Jaswant Kanwar was also elected unopposed as the mayor in the industrial city.

The counting of votes at the municipal councils and municipalities was in progress till late in the evening, while the trends indicated the BJP’s lead at majority of the places, where it was likely to form the boards.

World.title: Freezing democracy: On the Election Commission of India and West Bengal
World.content:
Almost 28 years after Mamata Banerjee set up the All India Trinamool Congress and designed its symbol of ‘grass and flowers’, the Election Commission of India (ECI) on September 17, 2026, froze the party’s name and symbol. The 14-page order stated that since two rival groups — one led by Ms. Banerjee and the other by Arup Roy — are now claiming to be the party, the matter requires “substantive determination”, and neither group can use the party’s name or symbol. The ECI has allotted new names and symbols to both groups. The ECI’s move has effectively denied Ms. Banerjee of her party’s name and symbol. For nearly three decades, crores of voters have placed their faith in the party’s name and symbol, elected Ms. Banerjee as Chief Minister of West Bengal three times, and sent scores as its MPs to Parliament. Even in the April 2026 West Bengal Assembly polls, 41% of the electorate, or more than 2.60 crore voters, voted for Ms. Banerjee’s party, while the margin between it and the Bharatiya Janata Party was only about 32 lakh votes. Opposition parties, including the Congress, have said that similar attempts to freeze the name and symbol were made in the case of the Shiv Sena, calling such action of freezing the name and the symbol as “party theft” and a case of democratic decline.

Political parties are organic entities that keep democracy vibrant and alive and any attempts to engineer their dissolution is an attack on the very foundations of India’s democracy. If a political party has to wither away, it should happen only through the determination of the people. Serious questions have been raised about the role of the ECI, which held the West Bengal Assembly polls in 2026 after a hurriedly organised Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral rolls that left lakhs of voters out, and is now freezing the name and symbol of the principal Opposition party. Free and fair elections form the bedrock of the republic. When political parties, which are engines for ensuring that the will of the electorate is reflected through free and fair elections, are dismantled and stripped of their names and symbols, the ECI cannot absolve itself of responsibility or hide behind processes and practices. The BJP leadership in West Bengal has repeatedly claimed that, after the Assembly polls, there would be no existence of the Trinamool Congress as a party. The ECI’s acts of omission and commission clearly suggest that it is acting in tandem with the interests of the BJP.

World.title: Haryana police use water cannons, tear gas to disperse farmers protesting paddy procurement delay
World.content:
The Haryana police used water cannons and tear gas shells to disperse a large number of farmers who tried to block National Highway-44 near Shahbad in Kurukshetra on Tuesday afternoon during a protest over the alleged delay in paddy procurement.

The farmers briefly blocked the highway around 1.30 p.m., following which the police intervened. Several farmers were injured, though Bharatiya Kisan Union (Charuni) president Gurnam Singh Charuni said none suffered serious injuries. The road remained blocked for around 10 to 15 minutes, he said.

Kurukshetra Superintendent of Police Chander Mohan said the administration had offered to hold talks with the farmers, but they still attempted to block the highway. “We are very clear that the National Highway cannot be blocked,” he said, adding that some policemen were also injured in the clash.

Mr. Charuni said the farmers had been protesting against the government’s failure to begin paddy procurement despite increasing arrivals in mandis. He said the farmers had given the government time until September 22 after the Deputy Commissioner intervened during a panchayat meeting on September 16.

“The arrival of paddy is increasing rapidly. More than two lakh quintals have already arrived in this region. Eight to 10 lakh quintals may have already arrived in the mandis, but procurement has not started,” he said.

He alleged that the delay was deliberate and linked to corruption, claiming that physical verification of paddy acreage had not been completed. Referring to last year’s experience, Mr. Charuni alleged that inflated and fictitious acreage, including land where paddy had not been cultivated, was uploaded on the government portal without action against those responsible.

The All India Kisan Sabha, Haryana, condemned the police action, alleging that the government was deliberately delaying procurement and imposing various conditions on farmers. State president Master Balbir Singh and general secretary Sumit Dalal also alleged that limits were being imposed on the quantity of crop that could be procured from individual farmers and that farmers were facing difficulties operating procurement-related portals.

The AIKS leaders said the protest had been announced in advance by the BKU (Charuni), but alleged that the government and administration remained “insensitive and anti-farmer”.

World.title: NC, BJP members spar on issue of holiday on anniversaries of Maharaja Hari Singh, Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah
World.content:
Noisy scenes erupted in the Jammu and Kashmir assembly on Tuesday (September 22, 2026) as the ruling National Conference (NC) and the opposition BJP sparred over the official holidays on the anniversaries of Dogra monarch Maharaja Hari Singh and NC founder Sheikh Muhammad Abdullah. Meanwhile, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) flagged the issue of the closure of highways in Kashmir during the movement of security forces’ convoys.

As the J&K assembly convened the session in the morning, NC legislator Abdul Majeed Larmi pitched for declaring official holidays on the birth and death anniversaries of Mr. Abdullah on December 5 and September 8, respectively, in J&K. “Either Abdullah’s birth and death anniversaries should be observed as holidays, as in the past, or drop the holiday of the birth anniversary of Maharaja Hari Singh [on September 23] too. Sheikh Abdullah was an unparalleled legend from J&K,” said Mr. Larmi.

The remarks of MLA Larmi, supported by other NC legislators, sparked high-pitched sloganeering and protests from the BJP legislators. “How can they talk about cancelling a holiday?” said BJP legislator R.S. Pathania.

Meanwhile, Opposition PDP legislator Waheed-ur-Rehman Para also supported the NC demand. “It’s a legitimate demand of the NC. There should be a holiday on July 13 too, which we observe as Martyrs’ Day,” said Mr. Parra. Another PDP legislator, Muntazir Mehdi, displayed a placard demanding a holiday on July 13, when around 22 Kashmiri civilians were in an uprising against the Dogra monarch in 1931.

The Lieutenant Governor administration included Maharaja Hari Singh’s birth anniversary a public holiday in 2022. Earlier, it dropped the official holiday observed on Mr. Abdullah’s anniversaries and July 13.

Meanwhile, PDP’s Para also raised the issue of the closure of highways in Kashmir during the movement of convoys of security forces. “Locals provided land for highways. The same people are being discriminated against. It’s like the ‘Berlin Wall’. The entire population cannot be punished for a single act of violence,” said Mr. Parra.

He demanded that the Omar Abdullah government should “take the issue up with the Unified Command to end the discrimination and humiliation.

NC MLA Larmi seconded the demand of Mr. Parra. “This House should pass a resolution urging the Government of India to take action. We are not against the security apparatus. However, the procedures laid down cause inconvenience to locals, students, and patients. Ambulances get stuck, students miss their exams and the passengers miss their flights,” said Mr. Larmi.

Mr. Larmi said the Home department may not be under the Chief Minister in a Union Territory, “but the government should intervene to stop it”.

World.title: 'Terrific man' Shehbaz gets special mention during Trump's UNGA speech
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday called Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif a “terrific man” during his address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) as he once again mentioned his role in ending the Pakistan-India conflict in May 2025.

During a speech that covered the conflict in Iran, artificial intelligence and criticism of the UN, Trump once again listed conflicts that he had played a role in ending.

“Since I took office, it has been my honour to help settle eight wars, and in so doing, become friendly with the leaders of many of those countries,” Trump said.

“It was a great honour to do it,” he added.

He highlighted that he had been able to settle these conflicts via his “great relations”, as well as the use of tariffs.

Listing off the countries, he noted “Pakistan and India” as a conflict he settled, alongside Thailand and Cambodia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and the Gaza conflict, among others. He noted that almost all of these countries had written him letters of thanks for his role.

“The prime minister of Pakistan — terrific man — said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving 30 million lives and probably many more than that,” he added.

Tensions between India and Pakistan had flared in April 2025 when a deadly terror attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir was, without evidence, blamed on Islamabad, which strongly refuted the allegations.

The two sides traded a series of tit-for-tat blows that ended in May with the declaration of a ceasefire by Trump, who has since repeatedly talked about his role in ending the military escalation between the two countries.

He has also praised Chief of the Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on several occasions, calling him a “ highly respected general ”, a “ great fighter ” and “ my favourite ”.

Trump warns he could ‘annihilate’ Iran without peace deal

Trump also used his speech to argue that the war with Iran prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warn that he could “annihilate the Islamic Republic” if no deal is reached to end the conflict.

While predicting his administration would strike a peace deal with Iran following the November 3 US midterm elections, Trump called on other nations to join America in isolating Iran economically to force it to the negotiating table.

“I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?” Trump said.

“Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?”

Trump added: “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations? But I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election.”

The remarks marked the latest justification Trump has offered for the war with Iran. He has previously cited a range of reasons for the February US-Israeli strikes, including Tehran’s nuclear programme, its support for regional proxy groups and the prospect of regime change.

Iran has consistently denied seeking to develop nuclear weapons.

“I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to. They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election,” Trump said in his speech.

“I call on all nations to help to enforce the complete economic isolation of Iran,” he said.

He also addressed other topics, noting that a deal between Russia and Ukraine to end Moscow’s invasion was possible in the near future.

“We’re working very closely with the leaders of Russia and Ukraine, and we will get that one done. It’s going to happen, I think, more quickly than people understand. They’ve had it,” he said.

Calls for all nations to quit ‘rogue institution’ ICC

During his address, the US president also called for all nations that are part of the International Criminal Court to quit the body, calling it “out of control”.

“The United States is equally opposed to the out-of-control institution known as the International Criminal Court,” he said.

“I call on all nations that are members of the ICC to officially resign from this rogue institution immediately,” he added.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has vowed to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick”, describing the court as an “intolerable threat to US sovereignty”. The body tries individuals for the world’s worst crimes.

Washington has imposed a series of sanctions on ICC officials, furious at the court’s issuance of an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — a close US ally.

Trump said Washington would “never allow US service members or anyone else to be investigated or given show-trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us”.

The United States is not an ICC member and has never ratified the Rome Statute that established the court. Israel, Russia and China are also not members.

Rejects international regulation of AI

Addressing the General Assembly, Trump firmly rejected calls for international supervision of artificial intelligence, calling them a “globalist scheme” to control the new technology.

He also announced that the US government would henceforth use the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” in its communications, hoping that the world would follow suit.

“It sounds much better” and “it’s much more accurate”, he added, musing on whether the rest of the world would adopt the term.

Trump also dismissed warnings from AI safety advocates, comparing them to warnings about climate change, whose human causes are affirmed by the overwhelming consensus of the scientific community.

“Every major new technology brings challenges, and super intelligence is no exception,” he said.

“The very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming… are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us, and that everything is going to be a total disaster.”

Ahead of the week of meetings and speeches in New York, leaders of more than 20 countries urged binding safety measures for advanced artificial intelligence, warning that the technology’s development could outpace the ability to control it.

AI superpowers China and the US are not signatories.

Trump told the UN that the “United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control… artificial intelligence”. UN chief Antonio Guterres, meanwhile, called for the US and China to start a dialogue on the technology’s future akin to US-Soviet engagement at the height of the Cold War.

“Governments with the greatest AI capabilities have the greatest responsibilities to humanity, to establish channels for dialogue, transparency, trust and cooperation,” Guterres said in his address to the assembly.

“At a pivotal moment during the Cold War, strategic rivals came to recognise the need to manage shared existential risks.”

China and the US are currently discussing creating a communication channel for AI concerns in anticipation of a Washington summit meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.

Both powers confront rising fears that increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems could eventually escape human control, even as they race for technological supremacy.

Trump has come out strongly against AI safety measures, vowing on Saturday not to allow the “destruction” of the AI industry, a major driver of the US economy, over what he calls unjustified fears.

China’s President Xi Jinping in July said artificial intelligence should not be dominated by a single country and urged international cooperation on its development.

PM Shehbaz meets Kuwait’s crown prince

PM Shehbaz is also attending the UNGA session in New York, as well as Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar. The premier met with Kuwait’s Crown Prince Sheikh Sabah Khaled Al-Hamad Al-Sabah on Tuesday on the sidelines of the session.

He conveyed warm greetings to the crown prince and reaffirmed Pakistan’s brotherly relations with Kuwait, a statement by the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) said. It added that the two leaders reviewed bilateral ties and discussed avenues for further strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

PM Shehbaz “emphasised the importance Pakistan attaches to its relations with Kuwait and highlighted the potential for enhanced cooperation in trade, investment, energy and human resource development”. The two leaders also exchanged views on regional and international developments, reiterating their shared commitment to the promotion of “peace, stability and prosperity”.

The premier also met Kenyan President William Ruto on UNGA sidelines, discussed Pakistan-Kenya relations and expressed satisfaction at their positive trajectory, the PMO said.

He also met Somalian President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud, according to an official statement.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs1.70 per litre, HSD by Rs3.12 per litre
World.content:
The government on Tuesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs1.70 per litre and that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs3.12 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs392.05 per litre while HSD will cost Rs418.96 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for Sept 23 (Wednesday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources
World.content:
Security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram from Afghanistan and also effectively responded to firing by the Afghan Taliban, security sources said on Tuesday.

According to the sources, the terrorists tried to infiltrate the border from Nangarhar and Paktia in Afghanistan. They identified the terrorists as those belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term that the state uses for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan.

When the attempt was thwarted, the Afghan Taliban began firing on Pakistani checkposts on the border, the sources said, adding that the firing was unprovoked.

In retaliation, Pakistani troops targeted multiple checkposts of the Afghan Taliban and their defensive positions, the sources said. They added that several Afghan Taliban operatives fled the posts as a result of the retaliation.

According to the sources, security forces were constantly monitoring the border situation and remained prepared to respond to any aggression.

Pakistan saw a resurgence in terrorism after the Afghan Taliban returned to power in Kabul in 2021.

A day ago, the information ministry said Pakistan had conducted airstrikes on terrorist sites “in the border region with Afghanistan”, killing more than 28 terrorists.

In a statement, the ministry stressed that the “calibrated” strikes were carried out “against the hideouts and safe havens of terrorist organisations responsible” for the recent multiple terrorist incidents in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

The airstrikes came a few days after a major attack in the old Police Lines in KP’s Kohat claimed 23 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.

On Sunday, two officers and four others were martyred while eight terrorists were eliminated during a fire exchange between a security forces convoy and armed combatants, the military’s media wing said.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.

The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

World.title: Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway to be closed for all types of traffic from 11pm on Wednesday
World.content:
Islamabad police on Tuesday issued an advisory stating that the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway (M-1) will be closed to all types of traffic from 11pm on September 23 (Wednesday).

“Those travelling from the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and from other areas, should avoid using the M-1 and postpone non-essential travel,” the advisory, posted on the social media platform X, said.

The advisory noted that the M-2 Motorway between Lahore and Islamabad will remain open to all types of traffic, and urged motorists to take this information into consideration when planning their journeys.

The development came amid a planned long march to Islamabad by the PTI for the release of party founder Imran Khan, which is scheduled to take place on Sept 27 (Sunday).

Police have already set up around 2,000 containers around the federal capital and at Attock Bridge, an entry point from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern parts of the country.

On Monday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had warned the PTI against its Sept 27 long march, urging the party to refrain from proceeding with the protest.

“We have clearly told them (PTI) that they can never achieve anything through such drama, and I will say again that there is still time; they should not go into this situation,” Naqvi said during a press briefing, advising the party to “not enter a dead-end street”.

The interior minister vowed the government will not “leave any loopholes” in its response if the party went ahead with the protest.

It should be mentioned that the Jamaat-i-Islami, which had also announced a long march to Islamabad against the petroleum levy, said on Tuesday it was postponing it at the request of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, pending a meeting with him.

World.title: Afghanistan's situation demands continued attention in view of implications for regional peace, Dar tells OIC moot
World.content:
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar told a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) on Tuesday that the situation in Afghanistan demanded continued attention, particularly considering its implications for regional peace, security and stability.

Dar was addressing the meeting of the OIC’s Contact Group on Afghanistan on the sidelines of the 81st session of United Nations General Assembly in New York.

Dar recalled that in Aug 2021, Afghanistan saw a “watershed moment” as the US troops withdrew from the country and the Afghan Taliban returned to the helm in Kabul.

He said Pakistan was the first country to “open its doors to our Afghan brothers at the time”. Dar added that Pakistan had also hosted an OIC session in December 2021 to garner Muslim countries’ support and mobilise international support to address the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan.

“It was hoped that the Taliban would honour Afghanistan’s international obligations and their own commitment for eliminating terrorism, promoting inclusivity and protecting the human rights of its citizens. However, the expectations of the OIC members and the larger international community have remained unfulfilled,” he said.

He said the Afghan Taliban had failed to seize the opportunity to integrate Afghanistan with the wider world and the improve the lives of the Afghan people “due to their misplaced priorities and flawed ideologies”.

“We can help Afghanistan and should help Afghanistan to integrate into the international community,” he said, adding that the Afghan Taliban were required to first take steps for creating a conducive environment to this end.

These steps included concrete and verifiable action to prevent the use of Afghan soil for terrorism against any neighbouring country, particularly Pakistan. These attacks, he said, were planned and orchestrated from Afghanistan from “external backing to destabilise the region”.

Dar said Pakistan was “seriously concerned” about the presence of over two dozen terrorist groups in Afghanistan that threatened regional international peace and security.

He said law enforcers in Pakistan were making “enormous sacrifices” to counter terrorism as Pakistanis continued to be targeted by terrorist groups from Afghanistan.

In this connection, he also mentioned the recent attack in the old Police Lines in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kohat. The attack clai­med over 20 lives and injured about 100 others. Eight terrorists were killed during an overnight clearance operation launched to clear the area.

Dar also thanked Qatar, Turkiye and Saudi Arabia for their mediation efforts to “counsel the Taliban to find an amicable and peaceful solution”.

“As a collective voice of the Muslim world, the OIC has a vital role in addressing the situation in Afghanistan,” he said. “This group must urge the Taliban to eliminate terrorism holistically and with sincerity, and end their patronages of terrorist groups.”

Dar also asked that the OIC call on the Afghan Taliban to honour their international obligations and commitments, curb trafficking through illegal smuggling networks, lift all restrictions on women and girls that ran contrary to Islamic principles and norms of Muslim society and rethink policies that denied fundamental freedoms to ordinary Afghans “who have already suffered enough from civil war and conflict”.

He called for a politically inclusive process of government in Afghanistan and the facilitation of resettlement and integration of Afghan returnees to their homeland, noting that the international community also had a responsibility to share this burden.

He also stressed the need for adequate international funding to meet humanitarian aid requirements and for socio-economic developments in Afghanistan.

“No country desires normalcy and stability in Afghanistan more than Pakistan, and no country has suffered from the consequences of instability and insecurity in Afghanistan more than Pakistan,” Dar said.

He reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to supporting efforts to achieve a stable and peaceful Afghanistan, while highlighting the need for “mutual respect, sincerity and demonstration of necessary political will by the Taliban”.

Tensions between Islamabad and the Kabul have remained high, punctuated by cross-border clashes over the past year.

Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil, particularly those linked to the banned TTP, that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

Last week, Pakistan told the UN Security Council on that it would respond to terrorist threats emanating from Afghanistan in self-defence as and when needed and in accordance with international law.

Earlier this month, the Foreign Office (FO) declared that meaningful progress in relations with Kabul would depend on the Taliban taking concrete and verifiable action against TTP and other terrorist groups operating from Afghan territory.

It maintained that while Islamabad welcomed China’s continuing engagement, the external facilitation could not substitute for action by Kabul against terrorist infrastructure.

According to a UN Security Council-mandated monitoring report — covering the period from Dec 16, 2025 to June 9, 2026 — Afg­han Taliban’s continued support for TTP has contributed to a rise in the frequency and lethality of terrorist attacks in Pakistan, even as Kabul has taken some initial steps to rein in the group.

The report also pointed to growing operational and facilitation linkages among the TTP, Al Qaeda, Islamic State-Khorasan (ISIL-K) and the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).

More to follow

World.title: Anthropic unveils Claude Opus 5.5, says performance comparable to top-tier Fable 5.1
World.content:
Anthropic on Tuesday launched Claude Opus 5.5, a new AI model that it says delivers performance comparable to its top-tier Fable 5.1 while costing 4o per cent less to run than its predecessor.

The release lands amid growing debate over AI risks. Anthropic Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei earlier this month called on the global AI community to slow down the pace of releasing new capabilities to address safety concerns.

Anthropic said Opus 5.5 underwent external testing by independent AI safety research groups Frontier Design and METR before launch and includes safeguards previously reserved for its most capable systems.

According to Anthropic, Opus 5.5 outscored rival OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol on a software development benchmark while costing roughly one-third as much to run.

Opus 5.5 is priced at $4 per million input tokens and $20 per million output tokens, 20pc below Opus 5, Anthropic said.

The model is available on platforms including Amazon Web Services , Google Cloud and Microsoft Azure.

The model also scored better than previous systems in internal safety tests and was about 85pc less likely than Opus 5 or Mythos 5.1 to attempt to bypass containment boundaries in a dedicated evaluation, the company said.

Claude Sonnet 5.5 and Claude Haiku 5.5 will be released in the coming weeks, the company said, bringing many of the same performance, speed and safety improvements.

Anthropic is also expanding programmes that give vetted cybersecurity and life-sciences researchers broader access to the model.

World.title: Trump, Greenland, Denmark sign deal in bid to end Arctic standoff
World.content:
United States President Donald Trump and the leaders of Greenland and Denmark signed an agreement on Tuesday that permits a larger US military presence on Greenland and may resolve a standoff over the strategically located and mineral-rich island.

The agreement, signed during Trump’s visit to the UN General Assembly in New York, stops short of Trump’s demand that the US adopt Greenland as a US territory to head off the growing Arctic presence of Russia and China.

But the deal does permit a greater US military presence on the icy territory, an option that emerged as Greenland leaders argued against a complete US takeover.

A text of the deal released after the signing event said the US can establish a “Golden Dome” defence system in Greenland as a shield against ballistic missile threats. The shortest route from Europe to North America runs via the Arctic island, which is the location of the northernmost US military base.

In his speech to the assembled world leaders at the UN before the signing ceremony, Trump said the agreement gives the US “permanent control over security and all other needs on that territory”.

“No US adversary will ever be permitted to establish a military presence in Greenland any more, or make sensitive investments there without our express written approval,” Trump said.

Trump signed the agreement along with Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen and Greenland Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen in a trilateral ceremony after Trump gave his UN speech.
